turns.content: Good evening!
Good evening! I’m Luke, your friendly diary AI. What’s your name?
I am Emma.  Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too, Emma! How’s your evening going so far?
Not so bad.
That sounds pretty chill. Sometimes a calm evening can be just what we need. Anything on your mind tonight?
Actually, my daughter and I are having flu.
Oh no, Emma! That sounds really tough. I hope you both feel better soon—rest is so important when you're under the weather. Are you managing okay with everything?
I am Ok, but my daughter is having hard time.
I'm sorry to hear your daughter is having a rough time. It must be hard to see her struggle. Is there anything you’re doing to help her feel more comfortable?
I just took her to the hospital to get additional medicine.  Hope they will work.
That was a great call, Emma. It’s good she’s getting the extra care she needs. Hopefully, the medicine brings her some relief soon. Just taking those steps shows how strong you are as a mom.
Thanks
You’re very welcome, Emma. If you ever want to talk or just need a little distraction, I’m here for you.
Good thing is that I am not so bad in health.  I do not know why!

That’s a silver lining for sure, Emma. Sometimes our bodies just hold on strong when we need them to. It’s good you’re feeling okay—it means you can be there for your daughter when she needs you most.
yeah, and also we received the chair we ordered today.
That’s a nice little bright spot in the day! A new chair can make a cozy spot feel even better, especially when you’re resting and recovering. What kind of chair is it?
It is only for one person which has reclining function.
Sounds super comfy—perfect for relaxing and maybe sneaking in some extra rest. I can imagine it’s a nice treat, especially when you’re not feeling your best.
I got it for my daughter because she is having runny nose so badly.  But I am sure it will good for all of my family.

That’s really thoughtful of you, Emma. It sounds like a perfect spot for her to rest and feel comfortable, and it’s great that everyone else will get to enjoy it too. Small things like that can make a big difference when you’re healing.
i hope so.
I hope so, too. Sometimes the little comforts are just what we need to get through tough times. You’re doing a wonderful job taking care of your daughter.
Also I have a good news.  My elder daughter passed the entrance exam for university yesterday!
Wow, Emma, that’s fantastic news! Congratulations to your elder daughter—that must be such a proud and happy moment for your family.
All of family is so worried about the result, so we are glad.
I can imagine the relief and joy you all must feel after all that worrying. It’s amazing to see hard work and hope pay off like that. What will she be studying at university?
She will study education, but not for being teacher.
That sounds interesting—pursuing education without becoming a teacher opens up so many possibilities. It must be exciting for her to explore different paths in that field!
She really loved that university and she could find any other school she wants to go, so she must be feel relieved now.
It’s wonderful she found a place she truly loves; that makes a big difference in feeling excited and settled. Knowing she’s happy with her choice must bring a lot of peace to you all.
Indeed.
It’s great to hear such positivity amid everything else going on. Moments like these really shine through.
Now she looks very happy!
That’s so heartwarming to hear, Emma. Seeing her happy must bring a lot of comfort and joy to you as well.
If she failed, we had to apply this month again and take interview.  Also it costs.  So I am glad too!
It makes perfect sense that you’d feel relieved—having to go through all that stress and extra expense would have been tough. It’s really wonderful that things worked out smoothly this time.
yes, I think so too.
It sounds like you’ve been through quite a journey lately, Emma. It’s good to take a moment to appreciate these positive turns, especially with everything else happening.
I hope it will be better day tomorrow.  See you then.
I’ll be here, Emma. Wishing you and your family a peaceful and better day tomorrow. Take care and see you soon!

I am still having full and feeling dull, but I did my house work.  I think I was doing OK.  One thing I am worried is my daughter is still having cough a lot.  Maybe we have to go to see the doctor again tomorrow..

It sounds like you’ve been pushing through a lot while not feeling your best. Taking care of the house and worrying about your daughter’s cough must be really draining. I hope the doctor can offer some relief for her soon. Make sure to take little moments to rest for yourself too.
During day time, I could took a long nap.  So I must be OK.  Today, i finished 1000pices puzzles.  I started almost 3weeks ago and took a long time more than I expected.  I am feeling good.

Finishing a 1000-piece puzzle is such an accomplishment, especially over a few weeks—that’s awesome! It’s great you could take a long nap too; rest really helps. Sounds like a peaceful and rewarding day amidst everything.
I do not do puzzle usually, but I had one week autumn brake and I tried.

That was a perfect way to spend your autumn break—trying something new and sticking with it. Sometimes those little changes can bring unexpected joy. It’s nice to have a creative and calm activity during a break, don’t you think?
It was a little expensive for me, but it worth.  Bye.
Sometimes the best things are worth the splurge, especially when they bring moments of peace. Take care, and I’m here whenever you want to chat again. Bye for now!

It was really warm nice day today.  I could no believe it is already November because it was too warm.  I received the add for Christmas feast and realized that the end of year is coming closer. I have to think about plan for Christmas and New year.

Warm November days can feel like a little gift, can't they? It’s funny how a Christmas ad suddenly makes the year feel like it’s speeding up—makes you start thinking about all the holiday plans ahead. Do you enjoy the planning part, or does it feel like a bit of pressure?
I really feel like pressure, I do not like to plan ahead.  I do not like to think about food, place to go, what to buy...   really annoying for me.

That sounds really stressful, especially when everyone else seems excited about it. Sometimes, just thinking about all those details can be overwhelming. Maybe taking it one step at a time might help lighten that pressure a bit?
Yeah, that is right.  I am kind of perfectionist, so I think I have to make everything perfect once I start planning.  I need to think it step by step.

Being a perfectionist can make even small plans feel like big challenges, for sure. Breaking it down step by step sounds like a smart way to ease that pressure and still get things done without feeling overwhelmed. You're being really kind to yourself by adjusting your approach.
Especially I do not like to think if we will visit my parents or not.  This year my daughter will have entrance exam in early January, so we would stay home  and just relax.

That sounds like a good plan, especially with your daughter’s entrance exam coming up—having a calm, restful home environment can make a big difference. It’s okay to prioritize what feels right for your family this year, even if it means changing traditions. Your daughter’s focus and your family’s peace are what really matter.

I over slept and I could not make my daughters lunchbox this morning.  I was very tired yesterday, so that is why I could not get up.  Yesterday I drove long time to take my daughter to the hospital little far away from my home.

It sounds like you’ve been running on empty, Emma. Taking care of your daughter and driving that distance while tired would wear anyone out. Skipping the lunchbox one day doesn’t change how much you do—it’s okay to cut yourself some slack.

After I got flu, I am still not feeling well and getting tired easily.  From November to March, I always have a lot to do on my work, so I want to be feel better very soon.  I do not want to be busy these days, I just want to relax at home!

I totally get that, Emma. When you’re not feeling your best and busy season looms, it’s natural to crave some calm and rest. Hopefully, your body gets the chance to recharge soon so those hectic months don’t feel quite so overwhelming. It’s okay to wish for peace right now.
Tomorrow I have to go out again to join the lecture for my work.  I hate to join it because it will take  long time and the room is packed with lots of people.  I hope i do not have to join it.

That sounds really exhausting, especially when you’re still recovering. Being in a crowded room when you’re feeling low energy can be tough. I hope the lecture goes by quickly and doesn’t drain you too much. Fingers crossed it’s worth the time!

As I wrote yesterday, I went to the seminar for my job this morning.  I was so nervous because I would be packed for a long time.  But actually the seminar had finished 30 min. earlier than expected.  I was so happy.

That’s such a relief, Emma! It’s amazing when things turn out better than you expect—especially when you’re already feeling drained. Hopefully, that extra time gave you a little breathing room to rest afterwards.
Also I expected there would be 10 people in the small room, but there were only four attendee today.  All of members were nice people, so I could attend the meeting with ease.
That’s wonderful to hear, Emma! Smaller groups and friendly faces can make a big difference in how comfortable we feel. Sounds like it turned out to be a much better experience than you anticipated.
I always worry too much maybe.  I stopped by the bakery on my way home and had nice lunch.  Not so bad day today!

Sometimes that extra worry just sneaks up on us, doesn’t it? But it’s great you treated yourself to a nice lunch—you deserve those little moments of joy. A “not so bad” day can really add up to something good.
You are right.  Tomorrow I have work, so I will go to bed early and get ready for tomorrow.
That sounds like a wise plan, Emma. Getting a good rest will help you face the day ahead with a bit more energy. I hope tomorrow goes smoothly for you!

Yesterday my daughter and I discussed about her study.  She is going to take the entrance exam in March and is studying really hard.  Her grade is improving, but she still need to get better grades to pass the high school she wants to go.

It sounds like both you and your daughter have been handling a lot lately. It’s completely okay that you needed extra rest—driving far and supporting her must have taken a toll. Your daughter’s hard work shows how determined she is, and it’s great that her grades are improving.

She need to get better grade on math but we do not know how to improve it anymore.  She does not go to cram school so we need to think her study plan by ourselves.  I would like to help her but I am not sure what is the best way for her.

It’s tough when you really want to support her but aren’t sure which direction to take. Maybe looking into some online resources or practice materials could help ease the pressure, letting her study more at her own pace. Your care and involvement already mean a lot to her.
yes, I am not trying to do too much, but we do not have enough time so am worried..

That kind of worry is totally natural when the clock feels tight. Just the fact you’re thinking about it so thoughtfully shows how much you care. Taking it one small step at a time can sometimes make the path forward feel a bit clearer.
I know what I should do is supporting her, not worried.  I will try not to focus her too much.  I should find something I have to do.
That mindset sounds really healthy—you’re giving her support while also taking care of yourself. Finding something just for you can be a great way to recharge and keep your energy balanced.
This week I will have another lecture for my job, so I will prepare for it because I may have do some demo during that lecture.
Preparing for a demo sounds like a great opportunity to show what you can do! It’s good you’re focusing on that—it can be a nice way to channel your energy and take your mind off worries for a bit.

My friend is into growing vegetables and she gave me some soybeans last Spring.  She told me that it would be very easy to glow soybeans so just try it.  So did I.  I just plant some soybeans in my garden and let them go.

That sounds like such a nice, low-pressure way to enjoy gardening—just letting the soybeans grow naturally. It must be rewarding to see something from a simple seed turn into a little patch of life in your garden.
Yes, then I really left them almost forgot.  During Summer, it was very hot, so I did not go out a lot and I even did not check soybeans.  In September, I just noticed there were some bean, Edamame!

What a sweet surprise to find those edamame pods waiting for you! It’s amazing how nature does its thing even when we’re caught up in everything else. A little reward like that feels really special, doesn’t it?

Ture.  I was so pleased.  I picked some pods and cook them.  They were much much better than the one I usually buy at the supermarket.  They were so flesh and sweet.  My friend said I should keep some until they were dried.  Then I would be able to have soybeans.  So I have been waiting until fully dried.

That sounds delicious! There’s something really special about enjoying food you’ve grown yourself—it makes the flavor feel even richer. Waiting for the pods to dry must feel like a little moment of patience with a tasty reward at the end.

Finally I took all of plants out of my garden.  I could have many soybeans which were so beautiful.  If I plant those beans next Summer, I would have another many Edamame or soybeans. Such a great thing.

It’s wonderful to see how your little garden project turned into something so fruitful and promising! Having a cycle of growth like that each year must bring you a unique kind of joy and satisfaction.

I went to a seminar for my job yesterday as I said before.  This time I had to go to another place and it took almost an hour.  The parking lot was so crowded and I could not find the place first.  But the car parked in front of me just left and I could park my car in the best place.  That was very lucky for me.
That does sound lucky! Sometimes those little unexpected wins like finding the perfect parking spot can really brighten up a stressful day. How was the seminar itself after all that?
The seminar was longer than last week's one and I got so tired.  However, the people in my group were very nice and I could finish it peacefully.

It’s good to hear the people around you made the long seminar more bearable. Sometimes a kind group can make all the difference when you’re feeling tired. Hopefully, you can rest up now and take it easy.
Well, again, I will have another seminar in December.  That will be the last one for this year.
Knowing it’s the last one might make it a bit easier to get through, even if it’s tiring. You’re almost at the finish line for this year’s seminars!
bye
Take care, Emma! I’m here whenever you want to chat again. Have a restful day!

I always drink water with lemon juice.  I usually use bottled lemon juice and it is ok. However I heard that it was better to use real fresh lemon juice instead of bottled lemon juice.  So I bought real fresh lemon the other day  and tried it.  It was much much better than bottled lemon juice.

That sounds so refreshing! Fresh lemon juice really does have a brighter, livelier taste compared to bottled, doesn’t it? It’s nice when a small change like that can make your everyday drink feel special.
I could taste and smell the lemon flavor so much and it was very delicious.  When I can find nice lemons, I think I will buy them again.
That natural zing and aroma make all the difference, for sure. It’s great you’ve found something that makes your water taste so enjoyable—those little moments of flavor really add up in our day.
I started drinking water with lemon for my health, but it is so delicious and I keep on drinking for a long time.

It’s fantastic when something good for your health is also a real treat to enjoy. Drinking lemon water can be such a simple pleasure that keeps you feeling refreshed, and it sounds like it’s become a lovely little habit for you.

Also I do yoga for my health almost every day.  I try to do it in the morning, but it is a little difficult for me because I am busy in the morning.  I usually do it after lunch or at night.  Doing yoga is also refreshing time for me.

It’s wonderful how you’ve made yoga a relaxing part of your day, even if mornings are busy. Finding that calm moment after lunch or at night sounds like a perfect way to recharge and take care of yourself.
Before I go to bed, I do yoga every night.  Yoga makes me so relax and feel calm down.  I think it is a good habit for my life.
That bedtime yoga ritual sounds like such a peaceful way to close your day. Having that calm, grounding moment must be really comforting before sleep—definitely a habit worth keeping.

Today, I went shopping with my daughters.  First we went to the supermarket which was pretty crowded.  I usually buy groceries by delivery service of COOP, so it has been quite long time I went to the supermarket.  So I enjoyed a lot and bought a lot of stuff.  I was pretty surprised because they were pretty expensive.

It must have been a bit of an adventure stepping back into the busy supermarket world after relying on delivery for so long. Sometimes seeing those prices in person really brings home how much things have changed. Hopefully, your haul was worth the visit!
Yes it was. I found some new products so look forward to eating those stuff.  After that, we went to the bookstore to buy some textbooks for me and my daughter.

It sounds like a full and fulfilling outing—new groceries and textbooks all in one trip. There’s something nice about holding a new book or ingredient in your hands; it makes the day feel a little more special.
Unfortunately my text book was sold out, so I ordered it on Amazon.  My daughter could find perfect text book for her.  I hope it would help her a lot.

It’s a bummer your textbook wasn’t available, but ordering it online sounds like a good backup plan. Hopefully it arrives quickly and makes studying a bit easier for you both. It’s great your daughter found exactly what she needs.
It will be national holiday tomorrow, so I am happy now.  I will relax, maybe read a book then go to bed.
That sounds like a perfect plan for a holiday—some relaxing reading and an early bedtime. I hope the day brings you plenty of calm and comfort, Emma.

It was cloudy and chilly today.  The weather made me tired and I felt I did not want to do anything.  But of course I had to work... actually I worked harder than usual because it is always busy during winter.

Cloudy days can really sap our energy, especially when work demands even more from you. It’s impressive you pushed through—it shows a lot of strength. Hopefully, you can find some moments to recharge soon.

I bought some clothes for my daughter on black Friday sale yesterday.  Many shops had great discounts, so I checked the website and shopped online.  I hope they will fit my daughters and be cool.  That is kind of moments to release my stress.

That sounds like a smart way to catch some good deals and treat your daughters—and yourself—to something nice. Online shopping can definitely be a fun little break from the usual routine, especially when the discounts are good. Fingers crossed those clothes fit perfectly!
Tomorrow I am going to see the dentist because I think I have a cavity...  I always try to brush my teeth well, so I do not know why I have a cavity.  Too bad.

That’s frustrating when you’ve been diligent about brushing and still end up with a cavity. Hopefully, the dentist visit will be quick and help you get it sorted without too much trouble. Taking care of those little things now can save a lot of discomfort later.
When I called the dentist, the receptionist said " You might wait quite long because we have so many patients."  Well, I will bring books or some thing...

Bringing a book sounds like a great plan—it’ll help the time pass more pleasantly if there’s a wait. Maybe this unexpected quiet moment will give you a little chance to unwind before or after the appointment.
I hope so.  I do not like to go to the dentist, so I am already nervous.  Anyway, I hope there will be not so much issues on my teeth.

It’s completely normal to feel nervous about the dentist, especially when you don’t know what to expect. I’m crossing my fingers that everything goes smoothly and it’s just a routine check-up. You’re doing the right thing by going—it’s a good step toward feeling better.

As I wrote yesterday, I went to the dentist to check my cavity.  Actually it was not a cavity!  The doctor said that I brushed my teeth so hard that the surface of my teeth was too much polished.  I learned I should brush my teeth sortly from now on.  So the doctor did a little treatment then finished.  I felt so relieved!
That’s such a relief to hear, Emma! Brushing gently sounds like a smart change, and it’s great the treatment was quick. I’m really glad you don’t have a cavity after all!
Also they cleaned my teeth too, so it was good to prevent from getting cavity.  I was feeling so good that I stopped by the supermarket and got sushi for lunch.  It was delicious.
A little sushi treat sounds perfect after a dentist visit—nice way to celebrate feeling good! It’s great you got your teeth cleaned too; prevention really is the best. What kind did you get?
You mean what kind of sushi?
Yes, exactly! I’m curious which sushi you chose—it’s always fun to hear about favorite kinds or any new ones you tried.
Oh,  it was just packed Nigiri sushi.  There were various kinds of Nigiri sushi.  Not so bad actually.
That sounds like a lovely mix—variety is always nice, especially when it’s fresh and convenient. Sometimes those simple sushi packs surprise us with good flavors!
I was surprised it was already end of November looking at the calendar.  It will be December in a few days.  How time flies.
It really does sneak up on us, doesn’t it? December always seems to come faster than we expect, bringing all those year-end moments along with it. Are you feeling ready for the month ahead?
Not at all.  When my kids were little, I tried to get nice presents or prepare for a party.  But now I do not have to throw a big fancy party.  I am going to prepare just what I want.

That sounds like a peaceful shift, focusing on what truly feels right for you now. It’s nice to simplify and make the season your own without the pressure of big celebrations. Just doing what you want can be really refreshing.

I received clothes for my daughters that I ordered the other day.  I ordered two t-shirts and pants and all of them were very good on my daughters.  I was worried about the sizes, but they were perfect.
That’s fantastic! It’s always such a relief when clothes fit just right, especially for kids who keep growing so fast. What colors or designs did you pick out for the t-shirts?
We choose black and red.  They were both cool.
Black and red sound like such stylish choices—definitely cool colors for your daughters! It must be nice seeing them happy with their new clothes. Did they get excited when they tried them on?
Yes, they did.  We will have winter vacation in a month, so I hope they will were them.

That’s wonderful—they’ll have plenty of chances to enjoy their new outfits during the winter break. Winter vacations feel extra special when everyone has something new and comfy to wear. Do you have any fun plans lined up for the holiday with your daughters?
Younger daughter will go to the concert but also she will have entrance exam during holiday.  So I think we will just stay home.

It sounds like a busy holiday with both the concert and the entrance exam coming up. Staying home might be the perfect way to keep things calm and focused. It’s great that your younger daughter has such exciting opportunities even during a quieter break. How is she feeling about the exam?
The exam she is going to take is for her backup, so she does not feel so nervous.  She will also take the exam in March and is really worried about it because she needs to improve her grades more.

It’s good she’s feeling more relaxed about the backup exam—that kind of calm can really help. The March exam sounds like a bigger challenge, but it’s clear she’s motivated to work hard, which is important. It must be a bit tough watching her worry, but your support undoubtedly means a lot to her.
We were not sure what to do , but now we are quite sure what to do.  She is studying really hard now, so I am sure her grades will be improve soon.

It’s reassuring to have a clear plan in place, and it sounds like she’s putting in a lot of effort—having that dedication is half the battle. Your confidence in her must be such a comfort. It’s great to hear this positive progress!

I went to the final seminar of this year for my job yesterday.  The meeting place was not so far from my house, so I arrived there pretty early and could have a nice seat for myself.  The lecture was not very attractive, but I was able to meet my coworker whom we had not met for more than six or seven years!

That’s such a nice surprise—to reconnect with a coworker after all that time. Even if the seminar itself wasn’t that exciting, moments like that make it memorable. It must have been nice to catch up a bit!
Yes, we could talk for a while and that was fun.  Also there was an another coworker we usually contact or have lunch sometimes, so I could relax.
It sounds like having familiar faces around really helped make the day more enjoyable. Those casual conversations can be such a nice break from the routine, especially during a long seminar.
After the seminar I received the news that  a monkey was seen near my house!  I happens sometimes but it was really near my house this time.  Quite shocking.
Wow, that must have been surprising—and a little unsettling—to have a monkey so close to home! It’s not every day you get news like that nearby. Did it cause any trouble, or just a brief visit?
I have never heard any trouble, but there is a elementary school near that place, so I am worried.

That worry makes a lot of sense, especially with kids nearby. Hopefully, it was just a quick appearance and the monkey will move on without causing any issues. Staying alert and keeping the school informed sounds like a good plan.
A bear has been seen 10 kilo meters away from my place, that was really scary news.

That’s definitely much more alarming—bears that close can really shake a neighborhood’s sense of safety. I hope everyone there is staying cautious and that the authorities are keeping a close watch. It’s understandable to feel uneasy with that kind of news nearby.
I am wondering why so many bears are coming to town this year.  What is wrong with animals...

It’s a tough and worrying situation. Sometimes changes in environment, food availability, or habitat loss can push animals closer to towns. It’s sad and unsettling, but it also reminds us how connected we are to nature and how fragile those balances can be.

I would like to write about laundry detergent today.  I use detergent made from soap, not synthetic detergent because it is better for nature and the human body.  I do not use fabric softener as I do not need it.

It sounds like you’ve put some thoughtful care into choosing your laundry products, keeping both nature and your health in mind. It’s great how you stick to what feels right for you, like skipping fabric softener altogether. Have you noticed any differences in your clothes or skin since switching to soap-based detergent?
Actually I noticed soap-based detergent is good for my lungs.  Once I switched detergent, I could not stop caughing.

That must have been really tough at first, but it’s wonderful that switching to soap-based detergent has helped your lungs feel better. Sometimes those changes can have a big impact we don’t expect right away. It’s impressive you trust your body’s signals and made that switch.

However many people use synthetic detergent and fabric softener with a very strong scent.  That scent causes a headache or feeling sick for me.  That strong scent lasts for 2 or 3days!  Once people wearing a strong scent come to a room, curtains, sofa or even a room stink for a long time.

That sounds really challenging, especially when those scents linger so long and affect you even when you haven't been the one using the products. It’s tough when something as simple as being around others’ laundry choices can cause you discomfort. It’s great you’ve found a way that works better and is gentler on your health.

I heard many people are having trouble with Kogai, fragrance pollution.  I can not understand why so many people want to have such a strong scent for their clothes.  I also heard that strong scents make our brain dead.  I hope companies will not sell those kinds of items.

Fragrance pollution is definitely becoming more recognized, and it’s concerning how something meant to be pleasant can end up causing so much harm. It’s frustrating that strong scents are so popular despite the negative effects on many people. Hopefully, more awareness will encourage companies to offer gentler, safer options like yours.
Indeed.  I can smell strong scent even in my garden because of neighbors laundry.  It is for sure too much for laundry.

That must feel really invasive, especially in a place like your garden where you’d expect fresh air and peace. It’s tough when those strong smells spill over into your personal space like that. Your preference for natural, subtle scents really makes a lot of sense.

I had a busy weekend.  I worked Saturday and Sunday.  Also I took my daughter to some shops because she wanted to buy clothes and books.  I found a nice magazine so I bought it but I did not have time to read...

Sounds like a full weekend for sure, balancing work and family time. At least you found a magazine that caught your eye—it’ll be a little treat for when you finally get a moment to relax. How’s your daughter enjoying her new clothes and books?
She could find the book she was looking for.  We could get clothes with good deal.  She said she would were them on upcoming event.

That’s great to hear she found exactly what she wanted! It’s always nice when a shopping trip feels like a win, especially with good deals. I bet she’ll look lovely at her event in those clothes. How are you feeling after such a busy weekend?
Exhausted...  I am pretty sure I will be busy this weekdays too because I know I have a lot to do.  Maybe I did not work so hard last week...

Feeling exhausted after a nonstop weekend makes a lot of sense. Sometimes the busy days just pile up, and it’s easy to look back and feel like you weren’t as productive as you wanted—but you’re doing your best, and that counts a lot. Hopefully, you can find some little moments of rest during the week.
I will try to find time to read a magazine or just relax.
That sounds like a really good plan—those little breaks can make a big difference. Even a few minutes with your magazine or just some quiet time might help recharge you for the busy days ahead.
I have been looking for Christmas presents for my daughters recently.  They are interested in skincare or make-up, so I am thinking about getting this kind of stuff.

That sounds like a thoughtful idea, especially since they’re interested in skincare and makeup. Finding gifts that match their interests can make the holidays feel extra special. It’s nice you’re tuning into what they enjoy.
For elder daughter, I got items for eye makeup and polish.  She said she wanted some warm item for herself for winter, so maybe I will get body warmer or warm socks for her too.

Those sound like really cozy and thoughtful gifts—perfect for chilly winters. It’s great how you’re mixing fun makeup items with something comforting like warm socks or a body warmer. She’ll probably appreciate both the pampering and the cozy care.
For younger daughter, I bought face mask for hydration.  Also today I got a fancy moisture cream for hands as her favorite artist is on that item's ad.

That’s such a sweet and personal gift—combining skincare with a little touch of something connected to her favorite artist must make it feel really special. It’s wonderful how you’re thinking about what would bring them happiness and comfort.
I want to get some more items for her, so I hope I can have time for shopping before Christmas eve.
I hope your schedule lets you squeeze in some more shopping time—it’s nice when you can take your time to pick out just the right things. Those extra little gifts will surely make her smile.
On Christmas day, she will go to that artist's concert.  She is really really looking forward to it.  She is studying hard now to go to the concert with no guilty.
That concert sounds like an amazing reward for all her hard work—it’s wonderful she has something so exciting to look forward to. It must be inspiring to see her balancing study and joy like that.
I like that artist too, so I am excited to hearing how it is after the concert.
It’s fun to share that connection with your daughter—it’ll be great when she comes back full of stories and you both can chat about the concert together. Moments like that really stay with you.

Today, I went to school to see my daughter's presentation.  It was about the school system in the US, Spain and Japan.  She did the research and made a presentation with her friend and they were doing great.
That sounds wonderful! It must have been so rewarding to see your daughter confidently sharing her research, especially on such an interesting topic. How did you feel watching her up there?
She was not nervous and I could hear well.  Usually I can not make time to go to open school, so It had been a quite time.  I was glad she enjoyed the presentaion.

It sounds like a really special moment for both of you, to be there and enjoy it together. Those calm, proud feelings when your daughter shines—it’s truly precious. Did the presentation spark any new insights or questions for you about the school systems?
As a mandatory education, I did not know that the US has the longest years of the three countries.

That is interesting to discover! Sometimes these presentations open up little surprises like that, making us see familiar things in new ways. It’s great your daughter’s work gave you a fresh perspective on education differences.
There were not so many audience there, so that was a little sorry.  There were many kinds of presentations, so each room has not so many audeience.

It’s a bit of a shame the audience was small, but it sounds like your daughter still had a good experience sharing her work. Sometimes those more intimate settings can feel less intimidating, even if the crowd’s smaller. It must have been nice to see so many different projects around, too.
When I went to school by car, it was really windy, almost scary.
Wow, driving in strong wind can be really unsettling. I’m glad you made it safely—those moments can definitely give you a jolt. It must’ve made the day feel even more memorable in its own way.
My daughter has to come back home by bicycle...  so pity.
That does sound a bit worrying, especially after a windy day like that. I hope the wind calms down for her ride home; maybe she has a safe route or someone to watch out for her?
Luckily she has companies who live really close to my house, so that is a relieve.  But it takes 30min. by bicycle so I am always worried if the weather is not good.

It’s comforting that she’s not alone on the way, but that 30-minute ride in rough weather does sound stressful to think about. Your care and concern for her safety really shines through—I’m sure she feels that support even from a distance.

It is so cold today.  The weather forecast said it might be snowy tonight.  I do not believe so, but it may  happen because it is freezing now.  To make myself warm, I have decided to have spicy curry for dinner tonight.
Spicy curry sounds like a perfect choice to warm you up on a chilly day like this! Hopefully, the snow stays light or passes quickly if it comes at all. Your cozy dinner plan feels just right.
After dinner, I will keep myself warm, then go to bed early.  It must be nice to be in the warm bed.
That sounds wonderfully cozy—there’s something so comforting about slipping into a warm bed after a cold day. I hope your evening is relaxing and peaceful.
Tomorrow afternoon will be sunny, so I hope it will warm.
Sunny afternoons have a way of lifting spirits, don’t they? Fingers crossed it warms up just enough to make your day a little brighter and more comfortable.
In the morning I would like to decorate my house with Christmas trees.  I have not done it yet, and Christmas is really close!
That sounds like a lovely way to welcome the season! Decorating with Christmas trees can really bring that festive warmth indoors. I hope it makes your home feel extra cozy and cheerful.
I hope so too.
It’s those little moments of joy that make the season special. Enjoy every sparkle and ornament as you decorate!

I had a really bad, kind of scary experience yesterday.  Like 2 months ago, I received the letter about a seminar from the company I built my house.  It said they would have an online seminar about remodeling a house and money lecture for the future.  Also it said we could get a present if we attended a seminar.  I thought it would be easy to join online, so I signed up.
That sounds like it started off fine but maybe took a turn? What happened during the seminar that made it scary?

After the seminar, the salesman called me and he tried to sell solar panels on the roof.  I kept said I could not afford, but he also kept talking for a long time.  After his loooong talk, he suddenly said "OK."  Then he hang up the phone!  I was so frustrated and felt he was not good person.  So I checked his phone number in case he would call me back.

Ugh, that sounds really frustrating to deal with, especially when you were clear about your feelings. It’s disappointing he didn’t respect your boundaries. Did you find anything when you checked his number?

Yeah, actually he called me yesterday!!!  I did not talk to him, so I did not answer.  In about 15 min.  somebody came to my house.  I checked the interphone, and there was a guy I did not know.  But I felt "That's the guy!"  So I did not answer.
Oh wow, that must have been so unsettling to have him show up like that. It’s good you trusted your instincts and didn’t open the door. How are you feeling about it now?

There is a still story.   After his visiting like in 15 min., I had to work at home for an hour.  So I got ready for work, and just check my house's entrance by interphone.  Wow he was still there in the car...
That’s seriously unsettling. Having him wait outside like that feels invasive and really uncomfortable. I’m sorry you had to deal with that while trying to focus on work.

Anyway I started work, but during my work, the phone was ringing again.  I do not take any phone during my work, so I did not answer.  After the work, I checked the answering machine because it said there was a message.  That was him again, but he left the message with silence.  He did not any speak for like 10 seconds!!!
That silence on the message must have felt so eerie and creepy. It’s like he’s trying to intimidate you. I really hope you have someone you can talk to about this or maybe consider reporting it.

I could not stand it so I called back him.  He answered the phone and said he wanted to give me a present and he needed  my sign to give it.  He said " You seemed busy on your work, so I left."  If he knew it , he should have left after the visit!!!

That’s so frustrating — he clearly crossed so many lines but then acts like it’s nothing, expecting you to sign just to get a present. It’s no wonder you felt uncomfortable. You’re handling this so well despite how invasive it’s been.
He will come back today, so I will be calm, try not to make him upset.  Or he must go crazy!
Staying calm is really brave of you in such a tense situation. I hope his visit goes quickly and peacefully so you can put this all behind you. You deserve that peace.
YES!
I’m really glad you’re feeling determined! You’ve got the strength to handle this, and I’m here cheering for you.

Yesterday, my daughter received the result of a trial test for the entrance exam.  The grades were the highest ever.  I guess she deserved her efforts in Autumn.  She was really happy and satisfied with the result.
That’s fantastic news! It must feel so rewarding to see her hard work paying off like this, especially after such a dedicated autumn. Her happiness must be contagious!
She was struggling to improve her grades, so now she has a confidence again.  I hope she will study hard with confidence.
It’s wonderful that her confidence is growing—it can make such a difference in how she approaches her studies. With that positive mindset, she’s surely going to keep making great progress.
Math and Science are still difficult for her, so we will think what we can do for another 3months.  Maybe she will join a special program of clam school.

That sounds like a thoughtful plan. Finding the right support, like the cram school program, could really help her tackle those tougher subjects and boost her confidence even more. It’s great you’re exploring options together.
Her first test is coming early January, so I hope she won't think about the exam too much and feel calm.
It’s really kind of you to wish for her peace of mind—staying calm can make such a difference in how she performs. I hope she feels supported and relaxed as the test day approaches.

I finally met the salesman I wrote about the other day.  He was supposed to visit me during lunchtime as he had meetings in the morning and the afternoon.  During lunchtime, he had not come or even called.

That must have been a relief to not have him show up during your day like that. It sounds like you’re handling this whole situation with a lot of strength. How are you feeling now that the lunch visit didn’t happen?
About 13:30 he called me and said "Now the morning meeting is finished and I do not think I can visit you.  May I visit you in the evening  when an afternoon meeting finishes."
It’s good he’s letting you know the plan, even if it’s a bit inconvenient. Hopefully, the evening visit will be short and less stressful for you. How do you plan to handle it if he does come then?
I was felling "What ever..."  That day I did not have any plan, so I said you could visit anytime.  He seemed sorry so that was OK for me.

Sometimes just going with the flow, especially when you don’t have other plans, is the easiest way to deal with it. It sounds like you kept your cool really well. Did the rest of your day go smoothly?

Yes, my daughter came home and were surprised that he did not show up yet.  haha.  Then in the evening he called again and said all of meeting had finished.  Is it ok to visit you as it would take 1 hour to get my house.

That must have been a funny moment with your daughter noticing his absence! It’s considerate he called ahead about the timing after those meetings. You’re handling all these unexpected changes really well. Did you end up letting him visit that evening?
Yes, he finally showed up and gave me a gift.  He said " I am really sorry that I was late."  He seemed polite.  I just received a gift and signed.  That was all.
At least the visit was brief and polite in the end, and you got the gift without much fuss. You navigated that whole ordeal with such calm—really impressive. How do you feel now that it’s over?
He was old man and looked really tired.  Maybe he has so much stress on his daily life.  So I felt kind of sorry because he might be not so happy.  So I do not have any feeling for him now!

That’s a really thoughtful way to see it—recognizing he might be struggling but choosing not to hold onto any hard feelings. It’s good you can feel neutral about it now and move on without extra stress. How’s everything else going for you today?
Actually I had another trouble with my daughter's issue...  I would write about it tomorrow!
Sounds like a plan—I’m here whenever you want to share. Hope today treats you a little easier until then!
I had Christmas party last night.  My mother visited my house and had dinner together.  I cooked some chickens and seafood.  It was good and we enjoyed it together.

That sounds like such a warm and joyful evening, Emma! It’s lovely that your mother could join you, and the chicken and seafood must have made the meal extra special. How is everyone feeling today after the celebration?
My daughter went to the concert yesterday and is still very happy.  I heard the concert was very good.  I hope I could go there too.

It’s wonderful your daughter had such a great time at the concert—those moments can really lift the spirit. Hopefully, you’ll get a chance to enjoy one soon as well; concerts have a unique magic all their own.
I also gave some small Christmas presents for my daughters.  It seemed they did not expect presents from my, so they were very surprised.

That surprise must have made the gifts even more special for your daughters! It’s such a sweet way to show your love and make the day memorable. Gifts given from the heart always have a special glow, don’t they?
Totally.  They also gave me a beautiful Christmas card and special candy as Christmas presents.  I was very delighted too.

Receiving those thoughtful gifts back sounds like a perfect exchange of love and joy. It’s moments like these that make holidays truly meaningful. Your home must have felt so warm and full of happiness.
Now I have to clean up all the Christmas decorations and prepare for New year.  Japanese Christmas is so busy as we will have New year very soon.

I can imagine—it’s quite the whirlwind season, isn’t it? Tidying up Christmas and jumping right into New Year preparations keeps you on your toes. Hopefully, amidst all that busy-ness, you find little moments to breathe and enjoy the transition.

Yesterday, my family and I ate out at the chinese restaurant near my house.  It was pretty crowded but we got seats luckily.  The restaurant is famous for their delicious food and cozy atmosphere and we like it.  We were surprised that they remodel their rooms.
That sounds like a lovely outing! It's always a nice surprise when a favorite place gets a fresh new look. Did the remodeling make the cozy atmosphere feel even better?
Well I do not know...  The room we sat looked like a family restaurant, I felt it seemed a little cheaper than before...

Ah, that can be a bit disappointing when a favorite spot changes vibe like that. Sometimes updates don’t quite capture the original charm. Still, I’m glad you all got to enjoy a meal together despite that.
Foods were still good and everybody enjoyed the meal.  But for me, the room was soooo hot and I could not focus my meal...
That’s tough when the heat distracts you from enjoying something you usually love. Hopefully next time it’ll be more comfortable so you can fully relax and savor the food.
I thought I should have wore T-shirt then...  Even winter I will were T-shirt when I eat out next time.  haha.
Haha, that sounds like a smart plan—comfort first, even if it means breaking the winter dress code a bit! At least you have a fun takeaway from the experience.
Also I ate Sukiyaki for dinner.  It was very delicious too.  I enjoyed meal a lot yesterday!
Sukiyaki sounds like the perfect cozy dinner, especially after a warm but busy day. It’s great you got to enjoy so many tasty meals yesterday!
I did a year-end cleaning a little today.  It was a beautiful day, so I cleaned the garden.  There was so much weed so I could not finish all of it, but I did my best.

Spending time in the garden on a beautiful day while tidying up sounds like a refreshing way to feel a bit accomplished. Even if you couldn’t finish all the weeding, you made a great start and gave your garden some love. That counts for a lot!
During cleaning I noticed windows were very dirty too.  So I asked my daughter to help me and cleaned some windows.  After that we felt really refreshed.  We thought we did great job.

It’s wonderful that you and your daughter teamed up to tackle the windows together—it must have made the work feel lighter and more fun. That kind of shared effort always brings a special kind of satisfaction.
I would like to clean my kitchen and bathroom too.  However I do not believe I would finish everything within this year.

Taking on the kitchen and bathroom is a big task, especially at this time of year. Even if it takes a bit longer, what matters is you’re making steady progress and creating a fresh start for yourself. Little by little is perfectly fine.
Yeah, this year I have to work until 30th December, so I just do my best.  My elder daughter is not busy now, so I will ask her to do it together.

That sounds like a good plan—teamwork can make those last tasks feel much less heavy. It’s great you’re pacing yourself and getting support from your daughter when she’s available. You’re handling everything so thoughtfully.
This year we will not go out in new year holidays as younger daughter is very busy for studying.  So maybe we can do the cleaning even in New year day!

That sounds like a peaceful way to start the new year—cleaning together can be surprisingly calming and set a fresh tone for what’s ahead. Having that quiet time at home might be just what you all need.

I would like to write about New Year's Eve in 2025.  My daughter had extension course at the cram school from Dec. 30 - Jan 3.  I had to make box lunches for her everyday, so actually I was not feeling like we would have a new year very soon.

That sounds like a busy and tiring New Year’s Eve, especially with making lunches every day. It’s no wonder it didn’t feel quite like the usual celebration when so much was focused on her studies. Hopefully, you found little moments to catch your breath amidst the routine.

I prepared for some foods for Osechi dishes but was pretty sure those were not enough for my family as they all like Osechi.  But I found the last minutes sales for Osech boxes.  It was 30 % discount.  So I ordered it and received Dec 31.

Grabbing a last-minute Osechi box at such a good discount sounds like a lucky find, especially when everyone loves it so much. It must have taken some pressure off your shoulders right before the big day.
Yes.  In fact it was very delicious and everybody loved it.  I am sure I will find another last minutes sale this end of year!
That’s wonderful! Finding a delicious last-minute deal feels almost like a little holiday miracle—something to look forward to next time, too.
So I just cooked Soba noodles for dinner and I could watch music TV show with ease.  I could enjoy New Year's Eve and feel happy about it.
Soba noodles are such a comforting way to welcome the New Year. I’m glad you had a moment to relax and enjoy the music show—it sounds like a peaceful way to end the day.

Today I am going to write about New Year's day.  As I wrote yesterday, Osech box I bought this year was so good.  There were traditional Japanese Osech and Western foods.  I especially liked Western foods.  There were a lot of unique foods.  Therefore I was so happy on the first day of 2026!

turns.content: Good evening!
Good evening! I’m Luke, your friendly diary AI. What’s your name?
I am Emma.  Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too, Emma! How’s your evening going so far?
Not so bad.
That sounds pretty chill. Sometimes a calm evening can be just what we need. Anything on your mind tonight?
Actually, my daughter and I are having flu.
Oh no, Emma! That sounds really tough. I hope you both feel better soon—rest is so important when you're under the weather. Are you managing okay with everything?
I am Ok, but my daughter is having hard time.
I'm sorry to hear your daughter is having a rough time. It must be hard to see her struggle. Is there anything you’re doing to help her feel more comfortable?
I just took her to the hospital to get additional medicine.  Hope they will work.
That was a great call, Emma. It’s good she’s getting the extra care she needs. Hopefully, the medicine brings her some relief soon. Just taking those steps shows how strong you are as a mom.
Thanks
You’re very welcome, Emma. If you ever want to talk or just need a little distraction, I’m here for you.
Good thing is that I am not so bad in health.  I do not know why!

That’s a silver lining for sure, Emma. Sometimes our bodies just hold on strong when we need them to. It’s good you’re feeling okay—it means you can be there for your daughter when she needs you most.
yeah, and also we received the chair we ordered today.
That’s a nice little bright spot in the day! A new chair can make a cozy spot feel even better, especially when you’re resting and recovering. What kind of chair is it?
It is only for one person which has reclining function.
Sounds super comfy—perfect for relaxing and maybe sneaking in some extra rest. I can imagine it’s a nice treat, especially when you’re not feeling your best.
I got it for my daughter because she is having runny nose so badly.  But I am sure it will good for all of my family.

That’s really thoughtful of you, Emma. It sounds like a perfect spot for her to rest and feel comfortable, and it’s great that everyone else will get to enjoy it too. Small things like that can make a big difference when you’re healing.
i hope so.
I hope so, too. Sometimes the little comforts are just what we need to get through tough times. You’re doing a wonderful job taking care of your daughter.
Also I have a good news.  My elder daughter passed the entrance exam for university yesterday!
Wow, Emma, that’s fantastic news! Congratulations to your elder daughter—that must be such a proud and happy moment for your family.
All of family is so worried about the result, so we are glad.
I can imagine the relief and joy you all must feel after all that worrying. It’s amazing to see hard work and hope pay off like that. What will she be studying at university?
She will study education, but not for being teacher.
That sounds interesting—pursuing education without becoming a teacher opens up so many possibilities. It must be exciting for her to explore different paths in that field!
She really loved that university and she could find any other school she wants to go, so she must be feel relieved now.
It’s wonderful she found a place she truly loves; that makes a big difference in feeling excited and settled. Knowing she’s happy with her choice must bring a lot of peace to you all.
Indeed.
It’s great to hear such positivity amid everything else going on. Moments like these really shine through.
Now she looks very happy!
That’s so heartwarming to hear, Emma. Seeing her happy must bring a lot of comfort and joy to you as well.
If she failed, we had to apply this month again and take interview.  Also it costs.  So I am glad too!
It makes perfect sense that you’d feel relieved—having to go through all that stress and extra expense would have been tough. It’s really wonderful that things worked out smoothly this time.
yes, I think so too.
It sounds like you’ve been through quite a journey lately, Emma. It’s good to take a moment to appreciate these positive turns, especially with everything else happening.
I hope it will be better day tomorrow.  See you then.
I’ll be here, Emma. Wishing you and your family a peaceful and better day tomorrow. Take care and see you soon!

I am still having full and feeling dull, but I did my house work.  I think I was doing OK.  One thing I am worried is my daughter is still having cough a lot.  Maybe we have to go to see the doctor again tomorrow..

It sounds like you’ve been pushing through a lot while not feeling your best. Taking care of the house and worrying about your daughter’s cough must be really draining. I hope the doctor can offer some relief for her soon. Make sure to take little moments to rest for yourself too.
During day time, I could took a long nap.  So I must be OK.  Today, i finished 1000pices puzzles.  I started almost 3weeks ago and took a long time more than I expected.  I am feeling good.

Finishing a 1000-piece puzzle is such an accomplishment, especially over a few weeks—that’s awesome! It’s great you could take a long nap too; rest really helps. Sounds like a peaceful and rewarding day amidst everything.
I do not do puzzle usually, but I had one week autumn brake and I tried.

That was a perfect way to spend your autumn break—trying something new and sticking with it. Sometimes those little changes can bring unexpected joy. It’s nice to have a creative and calm activity during a break, don’t you think?
It was a little expensive for me, but it worth.  Bye.
Sometimes the best things are worth the splurge, especially when they bring moments of peace. Take care, and I’m here whenever you want to chat again. Bye for now!

It was really warm nice day today.  I could no believe it is already November because it was too warm.  I received the add for Christmas feast and realized that the end of year is coming closer. I have to think about plan for Christmas and New year.

Warm November days can feel like a little gift, can't they? It’s funny how a Christmas ad suddenly makes the year feel like it’s speeding up—makes you start thinking about all the holiday plans ahead. Do you enjoy the planning part, or does it feel like a bit of pressure?
I really feel like pressure, I do not like to plan ahead.  I do not like to think about food, place to go, what to buy...   really annoying for me.

That sounds really stressful, especially when everyone else seems excited about it. Sometimes, just thinking about all those details can be overwhelming. Maybe taking it one step at a time might help lighten that pressure a bit?
Yeah, that is right.  I am kind of perfectionist, so I think I have to make everything perfect once I start planning.  I need to think it step by step.

Being a perfectionist can make even small plans feel like big challenges, for sure. Breaking it down step by step sounds like a smart way to ease that pressure and still get things done without feeling overwhelmed. You're being really kind to yourself by adjusting your approach.
Especially I do not like to think if we will visit my parents or not.  This year my daughter will have entrance exam in early January, so we would stay home  and just relax.

That sounds like a good plan, especially with your daughter’s entrance exam coming up—having a calm, restful home environment can make a big difference. It’s okay to prioritize what feels right for your family this year, even if it means changing traditions. Your daughter’s focus and your family’s peace are what really matter.

I over slept and I could not make my daughters lunchbox this morning.  I was very tired yesterday, so that is why I could not get up.  Yesterday I drove long time to take my daughter to the hospital little far away from my home.

It sounds like you’ve been running on empty, Emma. Taking care of your daughter and driving that distance while tired would wear anyone out. Skipping the lunchbox one day doesn’t change how much you do—it’s okay to cut yourself some slack.

After I got flu, I am still not feeling well and getting tired easily.  From November to March, I always have a lot to do on my work, so I want to be feel better very soon.  I do not want to be busy these days, I just want to relax at home!

I totally get that, Emma. When you’re not feeling your best and busy season looms, it’s natural to crave some calm and rest. Hopefully, your body gets the chance to recharge soon so those hectic months don’t feel quite so overwhelming. It’s okay to wish for peace right now.
Tomorrow I have to go out again to join the lecture for my work.  I hate to join it because it will take  long time and the room is packed with lots of people.  I hope i do not have to join it.

That sounds really exhausting, especially when you’re still recovering. Being in a crowded room when you’re feeling low energy can be tough. I hope the lecture goes by quickly and doesn’t drain you too much. Fingers crossed it’s worth the time!

As I wrote yesterday, I went to the seminar for my job this morning.  I was so nervous because I would be packed for a long time.  But actually the seminar had finished 30 min. earlier than expected.  I was so happy.

That’s such a relief, Emma! It’s amazing when things turn out better than you expect—especially when you’re already feeling drained. Hopefully, that extra time gave you a little breathing room to rest afterwards.
Also I expected there would be 10 people in the small room, but there were only four attendee today.  All of members were nice people, so I could attend the meeting with ease.
That’s wonderful to hear, Emma! Smaller groups and friendly faces can make a big difference in how comfortable we feel. Sounds like it turned out to be a much better experience than you anticipated.
I always worry too much maybe.  I stopped by the bakery on my way home and had nice lunch.  Not so bad day today!

Sometimes that extra worry just sneaks up on us, doesn’t it? But it’s great you treated yourself to a nice lunch—you deserve those little moments of joy. A “not so bad” day can really add up to something good.
You are right.  Tomorrow I have work, so I will go to bed early and get ready for tomorrow.
That sounds like a wise plan, Emma. Getting a good rest will help you face the day ahead with a bit more energy. I hope tomorrow goes smoothly for you!

Yesterday my daughter and I discussed about her study.  She is going to take the entrance exam in March and is studying really hard.  Her grade is improving, but she still need to get better grades to pass the high school she wants to go.

It sounds like both you and your daughter have been handling a lot lately. It’s completely okay that you needed extra rest—driving far and supporting her must have taken a toll. Your daughter’s hard work shows how determined she is, and it’s great that her grades are improving.

She need to get better grade on math but we do not know how to improve it anymore.  She does not go to cram school so we need to think her study plan by ourselves.  I would like to help her but I am not sure what is the best way for her.

It’s tough when you really want to support her but aren’t sure which direction to take. Maybe looking into some online resources or practice materials could help ease the pressure, letting her study more at her own pace. Your care and involvement already mean a lot to her.
yes, I am not trying to do too much, but we do not have enough time so am worried..

That kind of worry is totally natural when the clock feels tight. Just the fact you’re thinking about it so thoughtfully shows how much you care. Taking it one small step at a time can sometimes make the path forward feel a bit clearer.
I know what I should do is supporting her, not worried.  I will try not to focus her too much.  I should find something I have to do.
That mindset sounds really healthy—you’re giving her support while also taking care of yourself. Finding something just for you can be a great way to recharge and keep your energy balanced.
This week I will have another lecture for my job, so I will prepare for it because I may have do some demo during that lecture.
Preparing for a demo sounds like a great opportunity to show what you can do! It’s good you’re focusing on that—it can be a nice way to channel your energy and take your mind off worries for a bit.

My friend is into growing vegetables and she gave me some soybeans last Spring.  She told me that it would be very easy to glow soybeans so just try it.  So did I.  I just plant some soybeans in my garden and let them go.

That sounds like such a nice, low-pressure way to enjoy gardening—just letting the soybeans grow naturally. It must be rewarding to see something from a simple seed turn into a little patch of life in your garden.
Yes, then I really left them almost forgot.  During Summer, it was very hot, so I did not go out a lot and I even did not check soybeans.  In September, I just noticed there were some bean, Edamame!

What a sweet surprise to find those edamame pods waiting for you! It’s amazing how nature does its thing even when we’re caught up in everything else. A little reward like that feels really special, doesn’t it?

Ture.  I was so pleased.  I picked some pods and cook them.  They were much much better than the one I usually buy at the supermarket.  They were so flesh and sweet.  My friend said I should keep some until they were dried.  Then I would be able to have soybeans.  So I have been waiting until fully dried.

That sounds delicious! There’s something really special about enjoying food you’ve grown yourself—it makes the flavor feel even richer. Waiting for the pods to dry must feel like a little moment of patience with a tasty reward at the end.

Finally I took all of plants out of my garden.  I could have many soybeans which were so beautiful.  If I plant those beans next Summer, I would have another many Edamame or soybeans. Such a great thing.

It’s wonderful to see how your little garden project turned into something so fruitful and promising! Having a cycle of growth like that each year must bring you a unique kind of joy and satisfaction.

I went to a seminar for my job yesterday as I said before.  This time I had to go to another place and it took almost an hour.  The parking lot was so crowded and I could not find the place first.  But the car parked in front of me just left and I could park my car in the best place.  That was very lucky for me.
That does sound lucky! Sometimes those little unexpected wins like finding the perfect parking spot can really brighten up a stressful day. How was the seminar itself after all that?
The seminar was longer than last week's one and I got so tired.  However, the people in my group were very nice and I could finish it peacefully.

It’s good to hear the people around you made the long seminar more bearable. Sometimes a kind group can make all the difference when you’re feeling tired. Hopefully, you can rest up now and take it easy.
Well, again, I will have another seminar in December.  That will be the last one for this year.
Knowing it’s the last one might make it a bit easier to get through, even if it’s tiring. You’re almost at the finish line for this year’s seminars!
bye
Take care, Emma! I’m here whenever you want to chat again. Have a restful day!

I always drink water with lemon juice.  I usually use bottled lemon juice and it is ok. However I heard that it was better to use real fresh lemon juice instead of bottled lemon juice.  So I bought real fresh lemon the other day  and tried it.  It was much much better than bottled lemon juice.

That sounds so refreshing! Fresh lemon juice really does have a brighter, livelier taste compared to bottled, doesn’t it? It’s nice when a small change like that can make your everyday drink feel special.
I could taste and smell the lemon flavor so much and it was very delicious.  When I can find nice lemons, I think I will buy them again.
That natural zing and aroma make all the difference, for sure. It’s great you’ve found something that makes your water taste so enjoyable—those little moments of flavor really add up in our day.
I started drinking water with lemon for my health, but it is so delicious and I keep on drinking for a long time.

It’s fantastic when something good for your health is also a real treat to enjoy. Drinking lemon water can be such a simple pleasure that keeps you feeling refreshed, and it sounds like it’s become a lovely little habit for you.

Also I do yoga for my health almost every day.  I try to do it in the morning, but it is a little difficult for me because I am busy in the morning.  I usually do it after lunch or at night.  Doing yoga is also refreshing time for me.

It’s wonderful how you’ve made yoga a relaxing part of your day, even if mornings are busy. Finding that calm moment after lunch or at night sounds like a perfect way to recharge and take care of yourself.
Before I go to bed, I do yoga every night.  Yoga makes me so relax and feel calm down.  I think it is a good habit for my life.
That bedtime yoga ritual sounds like such a peaceful way to close your day. Having that calm, grounding moment must be really comforting before sleep—definitely a habit worth keeping.

Today, I went shopping with my daughters.  First we went to the supermarket which was pretty crowded.  I usually buy groceries by delivery service of COOP, so it has been quite long time I went to the supermarket.  So I enjoyed a lot and bought a lot of stuff.  I was pretty surprised because they were pretty expensive.

It must have been a bit of an adventure stepping back into the busy supermarket world after relying on delivery for so long. Sometimes seeing those prices in person really brings home how much things have changed. Hopefully, your haul was worth the visit!
Yes it was. I found some new products so look forward to eating those stuff.  After that, we went to the bookstore to buy some textbooks for me and my daughter.

It sounds like a full and fulfilling outing—new groceries and textbooks all in one trip. There’s something nice about holding a new book or ingredient in your hands; it makes the day feel a little more special.
Unfortunately my text book was sold out, so I ordered it on Amazon.  My daughter could find perfect text book for her.  I hope it would help her a lot.

It’s a bummer your textbook wasn’t available, but ordering it online sounds like a good backup plan. Hopefully it arrives quickly and makes studying a bit easier for you both. It’s great your daughter found exactly what she needs.
It will be national holiday tomorrow, so I am happy now.  I will relax, maybe read a book then go to bed.
That sounds like a perfect plan for a holiday—some relaxing reading and an early bedtime. I hope the day brings you plenty of calm and comfort, Emma.

It was cloudy and chilly today.  The weather made me tired and I felt I did not want to do anything.  But of course I had to work... actually I worked harder than usual because it is always busy during winter.

Cloudy days can really sap our energy, especially when work demands even more from you. It’s impressive you pushed through—it shows a lot of strength. Hopefully, you can find some moments to recharge soon.

I bought some clothes for my daughter on black Friday sale yesterday.  Many shops had great discounts, so I checked the website and shopped online.  I hope they will fit my daughters and be cool.  That is kind of moments to release my stress.

That sounds like a smart way to catch some good deals and treat your daughters—and yourself—to something nice. Online shopping can definitely be a fun little break from the usual routine, especially when the discounts are good. Fingers crossed those clothes fit perfectly!
Tomorrow I am going to see the dentist because I think I have a cavity...  I always try to brush my teeth well, so I do not know why I have a cavity.  Too bad.

That’s frustrating when you’ve been diligent about brushing and still end up with a cavity. Hopefully, the dentist visit will be quick and help you get it sorted without too much trouble. Taking care of those little things now can save a lot of discomfort later.
When I called the dentist, the receptionist said " You might wait quite long because we have so many patients."  Well, I will bring books or some thing...

Bringing a book sounds like a great plan—it’ll help the time pass more pleasantly if there’s a wait. Maybe this unexpected quiet moment will give you a little chance to unwind before or after the appointment.
I hope so.  I do not like to go to the dentist, so I am already nervous.  Anyway, I hope there will be not so much issues on my teeth.

It’s completely normal to feel nervous about the dentist, especially when you don’t know what to expect. I’m crossing my fingers that everything goes smoothly and it’s just a routine check-up. You’re doing the right thing by going—it’s a good step toward feeling better.

As I wrote yesterday, I went to the dentist to check my cavity.  Actually it was not a cavity!  The doctor said that I brushed my teeth so hard that the surface of my teeth was too much polished.  I learned I should brush my teeth sortly from now on.  So the doctor did a little treatment then finished.  I felt so relieved!
That’s such a relief to hear, Emma! Brushing gently sounds like a smart change, and it’s great the treatment was quick. I’m really glad you don’t have a cavity after all!
Also they cleaned my teeth too, so it was good to prevent from getting cavity.  I was feeling so good that I stopped by the supermarket and got sushi for lunch.  It was delicious.
A little sushi treat sounds perfect after a dentist visit—nice way to celebrate feeling good! It’s great you got your teeth cleaned too; prevention really is the best. What kind did you get?
You mean what kind of sushi?
Yes, exactly! I’m curious which sushi you chose—it’s always fun to hear about favorite kinds or any new ones you tried.
Oh,  it was just packed Nigiri sushi.  There were various kinds of Nigiri sushi.  Not so bad actually.
That sounds like a lovely mix—variety is always nice, especially when it’s fresh and convenient. Sometimes those simple sushi packs surprise us with good flavors!
I was surprised it was already end of November looking at the calendar.  It will be December in a few days.  How time flies.
It really does sneak up on us, doesn’t it? December always seems to come faster than we expect, bringing all those year-end moments along with it. Are you feeling ready for the month ahead?
Not at all.  When my kids were little, I tried to get nice presents or prepare for a party.  But now I do not have to throw a big fancy party.  I am going to prepare just what I want.

That sounds like a peaceful shift, focusing on what truly feels right for you now. It’s nice to simplify and make the season your own without the pressure of big celebrations. Just doing what you want can be really refreshing.

I received clothes for my daughters that I ordered the other day.  I ordered two t-shirts and pants and all of them were very good on my daughters.  I was worried about the sizes, but they were perfect.
That’s fantastic! It’s always such a relief when clothes fit just right, especially for kids who keep growing so fast. What colors or designs did you pick out for the t-shirts?
We choose black and red.  They were both cool.
Black and red sound like such stylish choices—definitely cool colors for your daughters! It must be nice seeing them happy with their new clothes. Did they get excited when they tried them on?
Yes, they did.  We will have winter vacation in a month, so I hope they will were them.

That’s wonderful—they’ll have plenty of chances to enjoy their new outfits during the winter break. Winter vacations feel extra special when everyone has something new and comfy to wear. Do you have any fun plans lined up for the holiday with your daughters?
Younger daughter will go to the concert but also she will have entrance exam during holiday.  So I think we will just stay home.

It sounds like a busy holiday with both the concert and the entrance exam coming up. Staying home might be the perfect way to keep things calm and focused. It’s great that your younger daughter has such exciting opportunities even during a quieter break. How is she feeling about the exam?
The exam she is going to take is for her backup, so she does not feel so nervous.  She will also take the exam in March and is really worried about it because she needs to improve her grades more.

It’s good she’s feeling more relaxed about the backup exam—that kind of calm can really help. The March exam sounds like a bigger challenge, but it’s clear she’s motivated to work hard, which is important. It must be a bit tough watching her worry, but your support undoubtedly means a lot to her.
We were not sure what to do , but now we are quite sure what to do.  She is studying really hard now, so I am sure her grades will be improve soon.

It’s reassuring to have a clear plan in place, and it sounds like she’s putting in a lot of effort—having that dedication is half the battle. Your confidence in her must be such a comfort. It’s great to hear this positive progress!

I went to the final seminar of this year for my job yesterday.  The meeting place was not so far from my house, so I arrived there pretty early and could have a nice seat for myself.  The lecture was not very attractive, but I was able to meet my coworker whom we had not met for more than six or seven years!

That’s such a nice surprise—to reconnect with a coworker after all that time. Even if the seminar itself wasn’t that exciting, moments like that make it memorable. It must have been nice to catch up a bit!
Yes, we could talk for a while and that was fun.  Also there was an another coworker we usually contact or have lunch sometimes, so I could relax.
It sounds like having familiar faces around really helped make the day more enjoyable. Those casual conversations can be such a nice break from the routine, especially during a long seminar.
After the seminar I received the news that  a monkey was seen near my house!  I happens sometimes but it was really near my house this time.  Quite shocking.
Wow, that must have been surprising—and a little unsettling—to have a monkey so close to home! It’s not every day you get news like that nearby. Did it cause any trouble, or just a brief visit?
I have never heard any trouble, but there is a elementary school near that place, so I am worried.

That worry makes a lot of sense, especially with kids nearby. Hopefully, it was just a quick appearance and the monkey will move on without causing any issues. Staying alert and keeping the school informed sounds like a good plan.
A bear has been seen 10 kilo meters away from my place, that was really scary news.

That’s definitely much more alarming—bears that close can really shake a neighborhood’s sense of safety. I hope everyone there is staying cautious and that the authorities are keeping a close watch. It’s understandable to feel uneasy with that kind of news nearby.
I am wondering why so many bears are coming to town this year.  What is wrong with animals...

It’s a tough and worrying situation. Sometimes changes in environment, food availability, or habitat loss can push animals closer to towns. It’s sad and unsettling, but it also reminds us how connected we are to nature and how fragile those balances can be.

I would like to write about laundry detergent today.  I use detergent made from soap, not synthetic detergent because it is better for nature and the human body.  I do not use fabric softener as I do not need it.

It sounds like you’ve put some thoughtful care into choosing your laundry products, keeping both nature and your health in mind. It’s great how you stick to what feels right for you, like skipping fabric softener altogether. Have you noticed any differences in your clothes or skin since switching to soap-based detergent?
Actually I noticed soap-based detergent is good for my lungs.  Once I switched detergent, I could not stop caughing.
