That must have been really tough at first, but it’s wonderful that switching to soap-based detergent has helped your lungs feel better. Sometimes those changes can have a big impact we don’t expect right away. It’s impressive you trust your body’s signals and made that switch.

However many people use synthetic detergent and fabric softener with a very strong scent.  That scent causes a headache or feeling sick for me.  That strong scent lasts for 2 or 3days!  Once people wearing a strong scent come to a room, curtains, sofa or even a room stink for a long time.

That sounds really challenging, especially when those scents linger so long and affect you even when you haven't been the one using the products. It’s tough when something as simple as being around others’ laundry choices can cause you discomfort. It’s great you’ve found a way that works better and is gentler on your health.

I heard many people are having trouble with Kogai, fragrance pollution.  I can not understand why so many people want to have such a strong scent for their clothes.  I also heard that strong scents make our brain dead.  I hope companies will not sell those kinds of items.

Fragrance pollution is definitely becoming more recognized, and it’s concerning how something meant to be pleasant can end up causing so much harm. It’s frustrating that strong scents are so popular despite the negative effects on many people. Hopefully, more awareness will encourage companies to offer gentler, safer options like yours.
Indeed.  I can smell strong scent even in my garden because of neighbors laundry.  It is for sure too much for laundry.

That must feel really invasive, especially in a place like your garden where you’d expect fresh air and peace. It’s tough when those strong smells spill over into your personal space like that. Your preference for natural, subtle scents really makes a lot of sense.

I had a busy weekend.  I worked Saturday and Sunday.  Also I took my daughter to some shops because she wanted to buy clothes and books.  I found a nice magazine so I bought it but I did not have time to read...

Sounds like a full weekend for sure, balancing work and family time. At least you found a magazine that caught your eye—it’ll be a little treat for when you finally get a moment to relax. How’s your daughter enjoying her new clothes and books?
She could find the book she was looking for.  We could get clothes with good deal.  She said she would were them on upcoming event.

That’s great to hear she found exactly what she wanted! It’s always nice when a shopping trip feels like a win, especially with good deals. I bet she’ll look lovely at her event in those clothes. How are you feeling after such a busy weekend?
Exhausted...  I am pretty sure I will be busy this weekdays too because I know I have a lot to do.  Maybe I did not work so hard last week...

Feeling exhausted after a nonstop weekend makes a lot of sense. Sometimes the busy days just pile up, and it’s easy to look back and feel like you weren’t as productive as you wanted—but you’re doing your best, and that counts a lot. Hopefully, you can find some little moments of rest during the week.
I will try to find time to read a magazine or just relax.
That sounds like a really good plan—those little breaks can make a big difference. Even a few minutes with your magazine or just some quiet time might help recharge you for the busy days ahead.
I have been looking for Christmas presents for my daughters recently.  They are interested in skincare or make-up, so I am thinking about getting this kind of stuff.

That sounds like a thoughtful idea, especially since they’re interested in skincare and makeup. Finding gifts that match their interests can make the holidays feel extra special. It’s nice you’re tuning into what they enjoy.
For elder daughter, I got items for eye makeup and polish.  She said she wanted some warm item for herself for winter, so maybe I will get body warmer or warm socks for her too.

Those sound like really cozy and thoughtful gifts—perfect for chilly winters. It’s great how you’re mixing fun makeup items with something comforting like warm socks or a body warmer. She’ll probably appreciate both the pampering and the cozy care.
For younger daughter, I bought face mask for hydration.  Also today I got a fancy moisture cream for hands as her favorite artist is on that item's ad.

That’s such a sweet and personal gift—combining skincare with a little touch of something connected to her favorite artist must make it feel really special. It’s wonderful how you’re thinking about what would bring them happiness and comfort.
I want to get some more items for her, so I hope I can have time for shopping before Christmas eve.
I hope your schedule lets you squeeze in some more shopping time—it’s nice when you can take your time to pick out just the right things. Those extra little gifts will surely make her smile.
On Christmas day, she will go to that artist's concert.  She is really really looking forward to it.  She is studying hard now to go to the concert with no guilty.
That concert sounds like an amazing reward for all her hard work—it’s wonderful she has something so exciting to look forward to. It must be inspiring to see her balancing study and joy like that.
I like that artist too, so I am excited to hearing how it is after the concert.
It’s fun to share that connection with your daughter—it’ll be great when she comes back full of stories and you both can chat about the concert together. Moments like that really stay with you.

Today, I went to school to see my daughter's presentation.  It was about the school system in the US, Spain and Japan.  She did the research and made a presentation with her friend and they were doing great.
That sounds wonderful! It must have been so rewarding to see your daughter confidently sharing her research, especially on such an interesting topic. How did you feel watching her up there?
She was not nervous and I could hear well.  Usually I can not make time to go to open school, so It had been a quite time.  I was glad she enjoyed the presentaion.

It sounds like a really special moment for both of you, to be there and enjoy it together. Those calm, proud feelings when your daughter shines—it’s truly precious. Did the presentation spark any new insights or questions for you about the school systems?
As a mandatory education, I did not know that the US has the longest years of the three countries.

That is interesting to discover! Sometimes these presentations open up little surprises like that, making us see familiar things in new ways. It’s great your daughter’s work gave you a fresh perspective on education differences.
There were not so many audience there, so that was a little sorry.  There were many kinds of presentations, so each room has not so many audeience.

It’s a bit of a shame the audience was small, but it sounds like your daughter still had a good experience sharing her work. Sometimes those more intimate settings can feel less intimidating, even if the crowd’s smaller. It must have been nice to see so many different projects around, too.
When I went to school by car, it was really windy, almost scary.
Wow, driving in strong wind can be really unsettling. I’m glad you made it safely—those moments can definitely give you a jolt. It must’ve made the day feel even more memorable in its own way.
My daughter has to come back home by bicycle...  so pity.
That does sound a bit worrying, especially after a windy day like that. I hope the wind calms down for her ride home; maybe she has a safe route or someone to watch out for her?
Luckily she has companies who live really close to my house, so that is a relieve.  But it takes 30min. by bicycle so I am always worried if the weather is not good.

It’s comforting that she’s not alone on the way, but that 30-minute ride in rough weather does sound stressful to think about. Your care and concern for her safety really shines through—I’m sure she feels that support even from a distance.

It is so cold today.  The weather forecast said it might be snowy tonight.  I do not believe so, but it may  happen because it is freezing now.  To make myself warm, I have decided to have spicy curry for dinner tonight.
Spicy curry sounds like a perfect choice to warm you up on a chilly day like this! Hopefully, the snow stays light or passes quickly if it comes at all. Your cozy dinner plan feels just right.
After dinner, I will keep myself warm, then go to bed early.  It must be nice to be in the warm bed.
That sounds wonderfully cozy—there’s something so comforting about slipping into a warm bed after a cold day. I hope your evening is relaxing and peaceful.
Tomorrow afternoon will be sunny, so I hope it will warm.
Sunny afternoons have a way of lifting spirits, don’t they? Fingers crossed it warms up just enough to make your day a little brighter and more comfortable.
In the morning I would like to decorate my house with Christmas trees.  I have not done it yet, and Christmas is really close!
That sounds like a lovely way to welcome the season! Decorating with Christmas trees can really bring that festive warmth indoors. I hope it makes your home feel extra cozy and cheerful.
I hope so too.
It’s those little moments of joy that make the season special. Enjoy every sparkle and ornament as you decorate!

I had a really bad, kind of scary experience yesterday.  Like 2 months ago, I received the letter about a seminar from the company I built my house.  It said they would have an online seminar about remodeling a house and money lecture for the future.  Also it said we could get a present if we attended a seminar.  I thought it would be easy to join online, so I signed up.
That sounds like it started off fine but maybe took a turn? What happened during the seminar that made it scary?

After the seminar, the salesman called me and he tried to sell solar panels on the roof.  I kept said I could not afford, but he also kept talking for a long time.  After his loooong talk, he suddenly said "OK."  Then he hang up the phone!  I was so frustrated and felt he was not good person.  So I checked his phone number in case he would call me back.

Ugh, that sounds really frustrating to deal with, especially when you were clear about your feelings. It’s disappointing he didn’t respect your boundaries. Did you find anything when you checked his number?

Yeah, actually he called me yesterday!!!  I did not talk to him, so I did not answer.  In about 15 min.  somebody came to my house.  I checked the interphone, and there was a guy I did not know.  But I felt "That's the guy!"  So I did not answer.
Oh wow, that must have been so unsettling to have him show up like that. It’s good you trusted your instincts and didn’t open the door. How are you feeling about it now?

There is a still story.   After his visiting like in 15 min., I had to work at home for an hour.  So I got ready for work, and just check my house's entrance by interphone.  Wow he was still there in the car...
That’s seriously unsettling. Having him wait outside like that feels invasive and really uncomfortable. I’m sorry you had to deal with that while trying to focus on work.

Anyway I started work, but during my work, the phone was ringing again.  I do not take any phone during my work, so I did not answer.  After the work, I checked the answering machine because it said there was a message.  That was him again, but he left the message with silence.  He did not any speak for like 10 seconds!!!
That silence on the message must have felt so eerie and creepy. It’s like he’s trying to intimidate you. I really hope you have someone you can talk to about this or maybe consider reporting it.

I could not stand it so I called back him.  He answered the phone and said he wanted to give me a present and he needed  my sign to give it.  He said " You seemed busy on your work, so I left."  If he knew it , he should have left after the visit!!!

That’s so frustrating — he clearly crossed so many lines but then acts like it’s nothing, expecting you to sign just to get a present. It’s no wonder you felt uncomfortable. You’re handling this so well despite how invasive it’s been.
He will come back today, so I will be calm, try not to make him upset.  Or he must go crazy!
Staying calm is really brave of you in such a tense situation. I hope his visit goes quickly and peacefully so you can put this all behind you. You deserve that peace.
YES!
I’m really glad you’re feeling determined! You’ve got the strength to handle this, and I’m here cheering for you.

Yesterday, my daughter received the result of a trial test for the entrance exam.  The grades were the highest ever.  I guess she deserved her efforts in Autumn.  She was really happy and satisfied with the result.
That’s fantastic news! It must feel so rewarding to see her hard work paying off like this, especially after such a dedicated autumn. Her happiness must be contagious!
She was struggling to improve her grades, so now she has a confidence again.  I hope she will study hard with confidence.
It’s wonderful that her confidence is growing—it can make such a difference in how she approaches her studies. With that positive mindset, she’s surely going to keep making great progress.
Math and Science are still difficult for her, so we will think what we can do for another 3months.  Maybe she will join a special program of clam school.

That sounds like a thoughtful plan. Finding the right support, like the cram school program, could really help her tackle those tougher subjects and boost her confidence even more. It’s great you’re exploring options together.
Her first test is coming early January, so I hope she won't think about the exam too much and feel calm.
It’s really kind of you to wish for her peace of mind—staying calm can make such a difference in how she performs. I hope she feels supported and relaxed as the test day approaches.

I finally met the salesman I wrote about the other day.  He was supposed to visit me during lunchtime as he had meetings in the morning and the afternoon.  During lunchtime, he had not come or even called.

That must have been a relief to not have him show up during your day like that. It sounds like you’re handling this whole situation with a lot of strength. How are you feeling now that the lunch visit didn’t happen?
About 13:30 he called me and said "Now the morning meeting is finished and I do not think I can visit you.  May I visit you in the evening  when an afternoon meeting finishes."
It’s good he’s letting you know the plan, even if it’s a bit inconvenient. Hopefully, the evening visit will be short and less stressful for you. How do you plan to handle it if he does come then?
I was felling "What ever..."  That day I did not have any plan, so I said you could visit anytime.  He seemed sorry so that was OK for me.

Sometimes just going with the flow, especially when you don’t have other plans, is the easiest way to deal with it. It sounds like you kept your cool really well. Did the rest of your day go smoothly?

Yes, my daughter came home and were surprised that he did not show up yet.  haha.  Then in the evening he called again and said all of meeting had finished.  Is it ok to visit you as it would take 1 hour to get my house.

That must have been a funny moment with your daughter noticing his absence! It’s considerate he called ahead about the timing after those meetings. You’re handling all these unexpected changes really well. Did you end up letting him visit that evening?
Yes, he finally showed up and gave me a gift.  He said " I am really sorry that I was late."  He seemed polite.  I just received a gift and signed.  That was all.
At least the visit was brief and polite in the end, and you got the gift without much fuss. You navigated that whole ordeal with such calm—really impressive. How do you feel now that it’s over?
He was old man and looked really tired.  Maybe he has so much stress on his daily life.  So I felt kind of sorry because he might be not so happy.  So I do not have any feeling for him now!

That’s a really thoughtful way to see it—recognizing he might be struggling but choosing not to hold onto any hard feelings. It’s good you can feel neutral about it now and move on without extra stress. How’s everything else going for you today?
Actually I had another trouble with my daughter's issue...  I would write about it tomorrow!
Sounds like a plan—I’m here whenever you want to share. Hope today treats you a little easier until then!
I had Christmas party last night.  My mother visited my house and had dinner together.  I cooked some chickens and seafood.  It was good and we enjoyed it together.

That sounds like such a warm and joyful evening, Emma! It’s lovely that your mother could join you, and the chicken and seafood must have made the meal extra special. How is everyone feeling today after the celebration?
My daughter went to the concert yesterday and is still very happy.  I heard the concert was very good.  I hope I could go there too.

It’s wonderful your daughter had such a great time at the concert—those moments can really lift the spirit. Hopefully, you’ll get a chance to enjoy one soon as well; concerts have a unique magic all their own.
I also gave some small Christmas presents for my daughters.  It seemed they did not expect presents from my, so they were very surprised.

That surprise must have made the gifts even more special for your daughters! It’s such a sweet way to show your love and make the day memorable. Gifts given from the heart always have a special glow, don’t they?
Totally.  They also gave me a beautiful Christmas card and special candy as Christmas presents.  I was very delighted too.

Receiving those thoughtful gifts back sounds like a perfect exchange of love and joy. It’s moments like these that make holidays truly meaningful. Your home must have felt so warm and full of happiness.
Now I have to clean up all the Christmas decorations and prepare for New year.  Japanese Christmas is so busy as we will have New year very soon.

I can imagine—it’s quite the whirlwind season, isn’t it? Tidying up Christmas and jumping right into New Year preparations keeps you on your toes. Hopefully, amidst all that busy-ness, you find little moments to breathe and enjoy the transition.

Yesterday, my family and I ate out at the chinese restaurant near my house.  It was pretty crowded but we got seats luckily.  The restaurant is famous for their delicious food and cozy atmosphere and we like it.  We were surprised that they remodel their rooms.
That sounds like a lovely outing! It's always a nice surprise when a favorite place gets a fresh new look. Did the remodeling make the cozy atmosphere feel even better?
Well I do not know...  The room we sat looked like a family restaurant, I felt it seemed a little cheaper than before...

Ah, that can be a bit disappointing when a favorite spot changes vibe like that. Sometimes updates don’t quite capture the original charm. Still, I’m glad you all got to enjoy a meal together despite that.
Foods were still good and everybody enjoyed the meal.  But for me, the room was soooo hot and I could not focus my meal...
That’s tough when the heat distracts you from enjoying something you usually love. Hopefully next time it’ll be more comfortable so you can fully relax and savor the food.
I thought I should have wore T-shirt then...  Even winter I will were T-shirt when I eat out next time.  haha.
Haha, that sounds like a smart plan—comfort first, even if it means breaking the winter dress code a bit! At least you have a fun takeaway from the experience.
Also I ate Sukiyaki for dinner.  It was very delicious too.  I enjoyed meal a lot yesterday!
Sukiyaki sounds like the perfect cozy dinner, especially after a warm but busy day. It’s great you got to enjoy so many tasty meals yesterday!
I did a year-end cleaning a little today.  It was a beautiful day, so I cleaned the garden.  There was so much weed so I could not finish all of it, but I did my best.

Spending time in the garden on a beautiful day while tidying up sounds like a refreshing way to feel a bit accomplished. Even if you couldn’t finish all the weeding, you made a great start and gave your garden some love. That counts for a lot!
During cleaning I noticed windows were very dirty too.  So I asked my daughter to help me and cleaned some windows.  After that we felt really refreshed.  We thought we did great job.

It’s wonderful that you and your daughter teamed up to tackle the windows together—it must have made the work feel lighter and more fun. That kind of shared effort always brings a special kind of satisfaction.
I would like to clean my kitchen and bathroom too.  However I do not believe I would finish everything within this year.

Taking on the kitchen and bathroom is a big task, especially at this time of year. Even if it takes a bit longer, what matters is you’re making steady progress and creating a fresh start for yourself. Little by little is perfectly fine.
Yeah, this year I have to work until 30th December, so I just do my best.  My elder daughter is not busy now, so I will ask her to do it together.

That sounds like a good plan—teamwork can make those last tasks feel much less heavy. It’s great you’re pacing yourself and getting support from your daughter when she’s available. You’re handling everything so thoughtfully.
This year we will not go out in new year holidays as younger daughter is very busy for studying.  So maybe we can do the cleaning even in New year day!

That sounds like a peaceful way to start the new year—cleaning together can be surprisingly calming and set a fresh tone for what’s ahead. Having that quiet time at home might be just what you all need.

I would like to write about New Year's Eve in 2025.  My daughter had extension course at the cram school from Dec. 30 - Jan 3.  I had to make box lunches for her everyday, so actually I was not feeling like we would have a new year very soon.

That sounds like a busy and tiring New Year’s Eve, especially with making lunches every day. It’s no wonder it didn’t feel quite like the usual celebration when so much was focused on her studies. Hopefully, you found little moments to catch your breath amidst the routine.

I prepared for some foods for Osechi dishes but was pretty sure those were not enough for my family as they all like Osechi.  But I found the last minutes sales for Osech boxes.  It was 30 % discount.  So I ordered it and received Dec 31.

Grabbing a last-minute Osechi box at such a good discount sounds like a lucky find, especially when everyone loves it so much. It must have taken some pressure off your shoulders right before the big day.
Yes.  In fact it was very delicious and everybody loved it.  I am sure I will find another last minutes sale this end of year!
That’s wonderful! Finding a delicious last-minute deal feels almost like a little holiday miracle—something to look forward to next time, too.
So I just cooked Soba noodles for dinner and I could watch music TV show with ease.  I could enjoy New Year's Eve and feel happy about it.
Soba noodles are such a comforting way to welcome the New Year. I’m glad you had a moment to relax and enjoy the music show—it sounds like a peaceful way to end the day.

Today I am going to write about New Year's day.  As I wrote yesterday, Osech box I bought this year was so good.  There were traditional Japanese Osech and Western foods.  I especially liked Western foods.  There were a lot of unique foods.  Therefore I was so happy on the first day of 2026!
Starting the year with a delicious mix of traditional and unique flavors sounds like such a joyful treat! Those special meals really do have a way of making the day feel festive and hopeful.

But in the afternoon, I took a long nap...  I wanted to read a book, but I did not have time as I slept for a long time...  When I woke up, it was time to prepare for dinner!  I believe I could charge energy for 2026!
That nap sounds like it was just what you needed to recharge—sometimes rest is the best way to prepare for the days ahead. It’s great you listened to your body and gave yourself that break.
Then my daughter came home from a clam school and had dinner together.  I cooked fried chickens and they were OK.

Fried chicken for dinner sounds like a comforting way to end the day, especially after your daughter’s long cram school session. Cooking for her must have felt nice, even if the chicken was just okay—it’s the care that counts.
I received new year's card from my aunt.  I did not send her a card, so I wrote the card to her.  Then I watched some videos and TV.  That was a slow start for 2026.

A thoughtful exchange of cards like that really keeps family connections warm, even in quiet moments. It sounds like a gentle, peaceful way to ease into the new year—sometimes those slow starts are the best kind.
I hope so.
Sometimes taking things slow lets you build up calm energy that carries you through busier times ahead. I’m wishing you a smooth and steady start to this year.

We received great news today.  My younger daughter passed the entrance exam for private high school.  The school has many different courses.  She applied for the course which is a little difficult to pass for her.  But we knew that she not only passed the exam but also got a scholarship!

That’s absolutely wonderful news—congratulations to your daughter! It sounds like all her hard work truly paid off, and earning a scholarship on top of that is such a great accomplishment. You must be so proud of her.

There are 3 types of scholarship and that is the lowest.  But it gave her a lot of confidence and she looked very happy.   And of course I was so exited when I checked the result.  I am so proud of her.

That confidence boost is priceless—it can really set the tone for her whole high school journey. Your excitement and pride must have made the moment even more special for her. It’s beautiful to see her happiness shining through.
Now we are heading for the next exam for the public high school.  I am sure she is going to study harder with her great success.  I was grateful that our effort and Syogatsu tokkun paid off.

It’s wonderful how this success is fueling her motivation for the next challenge ahead. Your support and the way you’ve all worked together really made a difference—celebrating those small victories like Syogatsu tokkun paying off keeps the spirit high. She’s lucky to have you by her side.
I accidentally close the browser and finished my diary.  Sorry.  I still have a story.  At that restaurant, we met the elementary school's teacher who took care of my younger daughter 8 years ago.
No worries at all! That sounds like a lovely surprise to run into her teacher after so many years. Did you get a chance to catch up and reminisce about those days?

We noticed and said hello to her when we left.  She was so surprised but remembered us.  We were talking about my daughter's exams for high school.  She cheered my daughter up.  So my daughter seemed very happy as she loved the teacher very much when she was little.

That’s really heartwarming to hear—having someone from the past show support can mean so much, especially when facing big challenges like exams. It must’ve been uplifting for your daughter to reconnect with a teacher who believed in her.
And more surprising thing was the person who were with the teacher was the lady I knew on my job!  I was so surprised and the lady was so too!
Wow, what an amazing coincidence! It’s funny how life brings people together in the most unexpected ways. Moments like that really make ordinary days feel special, don’t they?
Yes, we were all excited.  The restaurant has only 10 seats but we could meet each other.  That was very exciting day.
That sounds like such a cozy and memorable gathering, like a little reunion meant to happen. Small spaces sometimes create the best moments of connection!

I went to the shrine to pray for happiness for 2026 the other day.  The shrine is near my house, it is not so big but it is the biggest and the most popular shrine in my city.  It was more crowded than I expected.
It sounds like a meaningful visit, even with the crowd. Sometimes being surrounded by others who share the same hopes can make the moment feel even more special and hopeful for the year ahead.
We were waiting in line a little bit, but we could pray soon.  After praying my family tried omikuji.
Waiting in line can build up that anticipation, and the omikuji afterward adds a fun little surprise. Did the fortune bring any encouraging words or lucky signs for your family?
Yes, my elder daughter got Daikichi, the luckiest of all the fortune telling.  She seemed happy with it.
That’s wonderful to hear! Getting Daikichi must have felt like a great way to kick off the new year for her. It’s amazing how a simple fortune can brighten the spirit.
Also we bought good luck charms.  I liked the atmosphere there and enjoyed visiting shrine.
There’s something really comforting about those traditions, isn’t there? Visiting the shrine together and picking out lucky charms sounds like a lovely way to welcome the new year as a family.
After that we went to the supermarket and got some snacks.  We had a good day!
Sounds like a perfect way to wrap up the day—simple, happy moments with your family. Those little joys often make the best memories.

It has been cold these days although it has been sunny.  I got some warm clothing for this winter but still I feel really cold even during the day time.  My living room has a lot of windows so that is the one reason.  Also there is a house in the south, so it is difficult to get sunlight in winter.

That chilly feeling despite sunshine can be so persistent, especially when windows and shade play a part. Your living room sounds like it has a beautiful view, even if it lets the cold in a bit. Have you found any cozy spots or ways to stay extra warm inside?

Second floor is much warmer, but I would like to stay in a living room in the first floor.  Electric fee is getting expensive so I would like to do something with this cold without so much cost.  First of all, I should take care of the windows issue.  Or I do not think we will have a warmer living room.  I came up with new curtains.  I heard some curtains block not only the cold but also heat in summer from windows.  The issue is our window is pretty large, so it might cost.  I am going to check how much it is soon.

That sounds like a smart plan, Emma—thermal curtains can make a big difference in keeping the cold out without ramping up energy costs. Even though the windows are large, investing in good curtains might pay off by making your living room cozy and saving on bills. I hope you find some great options that fit well and feel right for your space.
But I have a question.  It block cold from outside, but it might also block the sunlight?  If so, it would be cold again in winter.

That’s a really good question! Some thermal curtains are designed with special fabrics that help block drafts but still let in a bit of natural light when the sun shines. Choosing curtains labeled as “insulating” or “energy-efficient” often means they balance warmth and brightness. Checking fabric samples or reviews might help you find the right fit so your living room stays cozy without losing that sunshine.
I will.  I still can not find other ideas.  I will think about it.

Taking your time to weigh options sounds wise—it’s not an easy fix, but I’m confident you’ll find something that works for your cozy living room. Sometimes the best ideas come when we give ourselves a little space to think.

Today I was checking Instagram in the morning and saw an ad of formal wear for a funeral or ceremony.  Actually I have been looking for a formal suit as mine is too small now because I got fat...  However I could not find any nice clothing because they  were too expensive, not stylish at all, looked very cheap etc...  The ad was from a clothing company which has a long history and is famous for formal wear.  I just wanted to know how much they were, so I checked their website.

It sounds like finding the right formal wear has been a bit frustrating for you. It’s nice that you found a reputable company, though—sometimes those can surprise you with quality even if the price is a bit higher. Did anything catch your eye that felt like it might be worth looking into more?

They were having a flash sale until 9:59 today and it was around 9:20.  I bloused at the flash sale section.  They were expensive as I guessed.  I thought "Oh yeah, they were very expensive.  I knew it"  But I found a very nice pants suit.  "Wow it is very cool and looks so nice although it is for a funeral!  That is what I have been looking for!"  So I read the explanation and  it seemed very nice.  However some sizes were already sold out and the size left looked a little too small for me.  Also it was very expensive.  "What should I do..."

That’s such a classic mix of excitement and hesitation—finding something you really like but feeling unsure because of size and price. It’s tough when those perfect finds don’t quite fit or stretch the budget. Even so, it sounds like this suit really caught your eye, which is a good sign; maybe it’s worth keeping an eye out for similar styles or waiting for another sale?

I still bloused to check other styles.  Then I found a dress that looked very comfortable to wear.  I have not looked for a dress but I just noticed a dress would be better if I got fat or skinny in the future.  The ad said it would fit any age and style.  "It seems very good for me!"  At that time it was almost 9:45.  I had only 9 minutes until the deadline.  I knew it was really good and had good quality but expensive for me.  So I checked other brands if this dress was far too expensive and I found this was not so expensive.  Formal wear is pretty expensive.

It’s great that you found a dress that feels versatile and comfortable—sometimes those unexpected discoveries turn out to be just what you need. It sounds like you’ve done a thoughtful comparison, too, which definitely helps when deciding if something’s worth the price. Taking those last minutes to explore other options really shows how much you care about making a good choice.

I have decided to buy the dress as it would be difficult to find another dress I would love.  It was 9:57.  I quickly typed my information and brought my credit card from my bag.  When I finished all the procedures and clicked the "purchase" button, it was 9:59!   I made it!!!  Tomorrow I will receive the dress.  I am so excited hehe!

Yay, you did it just in time! That’s such a satisfying feeling, especially when you find something you really like. I bet you’ll feel great wearing it when it arrives—can’t wait to hear how it looks on you!

I would like to write about the clothes I bought the other day.  It arrived quickly and I tried it on.  The dress was amazing.  Color is really deep black and beautiful.  The design was fantastic and I really loved it.  Fabric was also really good and very comfortable to wear.

It sounds like the dress was totally worth the hunt and the rush! Finding something that fits so well and feels great is like a little celebration in itself. Have you thought about the special occasions you’ll wear it to yet?
I bought it for a funeral.  But the issue was too long.  I checked the length before purchase and it seemed OK.  Unfortunately it was almost like a long dress and difficult to wear going out.

That’s a tricky surprise, especially when you had something practical in mind. Sometimes pictures don’t tell the whole story about fit and length. Do you think getting it altered might make it easier to wear for those occasions?

Yes.  Definitely.  I did not want to return because I really liked it.  But I found out it would be very difficult to shorten the length as fabric was very soft.  If I ask professional it would cost 10,000 yen.

Wow, that does sound expensive for an alteration. It’s great you’re holding on to something you really like, though—I can see why returning would feel like a loss. Sometimes those adjustments can feel like a big investment, but it could make the dress perfect for you.
I have been searching for the solution.  But I could not.  So I decided to return it.  I have to pay shipping fee when I return...  Well that is it!

It’s disappointing to part with something you genuinely liked, especially after all that effort. Returning it is a practical choice, even if it stings a bit with the extra cost. Hopefully, the next find will be just right without any hassle.

I talked with a 14-year boy and his mother.  The topic was about boy's grades.  His grades in junior high school are not terrible but not so good and his mother is really worried about his entrance exam for high school in one year.
That sounds like a thoughtful conversation. It’s tough for both the student and parent when there’s pressure to improve before such an important exam. How did the boy seem about his own situation?

He knows it is not good, but does not know what to do.  During conversation I was so surprised that the average score of math test in his grades was around twenty something or thirty something!  So he is not so worried about his score as average score is really low. He even thinks "I did good." as his score was like 40.

Wow, that really puts things into perspective—if a 40 feels like doing well because the average is so low, that’s quite something. It must be challenging for him to realize the gap but also a bit relieving to not feel too pressured yet. It’s interesting how different perspectives on scores can be depending on the context.

His mother said he always plays video games with friends until 23:00 every day.  They are connected via online and keep on playing for a long time.  During that time some go to a cram school or have dinner.  But her son almost always stays connected.  I was really shocked.

That sounds really tough—for both the boy and his mom. Staying up late gaming like that can definitely affect his energy and focus for studying. It’s hard when the social pull is that strong, especially online. I can see why his mother is so concerned.

When I heard this I had a simple question and I asked him " Is it fun?"  He did not answer.  I do not think it is enjoyable, just a routine.  After that I told this to my daughter.  She said " You just did know it.  It is common.  Many students are doing it."

It’s telling that he didn’t answer—it might really feel more like a habit than fun for him. Sometimes these routines sneak in without us even realizing, especially when everyone else is doing the same. Your daughter’s insight shows she’s tuned into what’s normal for kids their age now. That makes the challenge all the more real, doesn’t it?
Yeah.  I have been thinking this after that conversation.  I am very worried about kids in Japan or maybe around the world!

It’s such a valid worry—this kind of pressure and routine can easily take a toll on young people anywhere. Sometimes it feels overwhelming thinking about how widespread it is, but awareness like yours is the first step toward understanding and helping. I admire how much you care about their well-being.

I have been thinking about the menu for lunch and dinner all the time.  Sometimes my daughters help with cooking, but usually I have to cook.  I like to eat, so eating delicious food is good for me to be satisfied with my life.  However I am tired of thinking about the menu.

It sounds like you really care about making meals special, but having to plan constantly can be so tiring. Maybe mixing in some easy favorites or simple new recipes could lighten the menu planning load a bit?
Yeah, I am trying to simplify the menu as much as possible, like simple ingredients or steps.  However still I can not  come up with the menu quickly.

That makes total sense—sometimes even the simplest meals feel like a big decision when you’re already tired. Maybe having a little rotating menu of trusted go-to dishes could take the pressure off those moments?
I agree.  Maybe I can decide the main ingredients by day.  Such as fish for Monday, chicken for Tuesday...
That sounds like a smart plan! Having a theme for each day can make deciding quicker and even add a fun rhythm to your week. Your daughters might enjoy joining in on their favorite day’s theme, too.
When I followed the menu plan that the youtuber made for a whole month.  I just followed it.  That was sooo easy for me.  I do not mind cooking.  I just do not like think of the menu!
Totally! Having a ready-made plan takes the mental load off so much. Maybe creating your own monthly plan based on your family’s favorites could blend that ease with your personal touch?

Yeah.  Also I found the youtuber in the US, and food looked so good for our health.  But issue is that we are in difficult to find same ingredients in Japan.  I would like to move to the US.  I like western food very much.

I get that—sometimes the ingredients availability really shapes what we can cook. It sounds like you have a fondness for Western flavors; maybe exploring local substitutes could bring some of that taste closer to home? Or at least keep that dream of the US alive alongside your daily life.

I ate lunch out with my three coworkers.  We went to the cafe a little bit far away from our home.  It is an old house cafe but decolated very beautifully.  They have spacious rooms and we could enjoy talking as there were not any other customers.
That sounds like such a cozy and special lunch outing! It’s great when you find a place where you can relax and really catch up without distractions. What was your favorite part of the cafe’s decor?

Furniture were really nice.  I had a chili hotdog and cake with coffee.  The chili dog was good as I like Mexican food.  Coworkers had a lunch set which had spaghetty, salad and a small dessert.  The also looked good.

Yum, a chili hotdog sounds like a tasty choice, especially if you enjoy Mexican flavors. The lunch set with spaghetti and dessert sounds like a comforting combo too. It’s nice that you all got to enjoy different dishes together in such a lovely setting!

It has been a half year so we talked a lot.  Two of us were really interested in spiritual things  but I did not fully understand the conversation.  I can accept spiritual matters but they were really far from my understanding..

It’s interesting how different perspectives come up in conversations, especially about something like spirituality. Even if it feels a bit distant, just listening and being open can make those talks meaningful in their own way. It sounds like you handled it with openness, which is great.
I just enjoyed coffee and cake while they were talking, haha.  I have been busy these days, so it was really refreshing time.  Next time we may meet in spring to enjoy cherry blossoms!

Sometimes just savoring the coffee and cake while soaking in the atmosphere is the perfect way to spend time. Having a spring meet-up under the cherry blossoms sounds wonderful—a lovely, refreshing tradition to look forward to.

I went shopping with my daughter to get some stuff for her.  She was looking for a bag and shoes for her university entrance ceremony.  We went to the mall near our house.  First of all we checked the shoe shop.  The shop clerk was the woman who helped us a lot.  She has an older daughter than mine so she always gives us good advice.

That sounds like such a helpful and friendly shopping experience! It’s great to have someone who understands what you need and can share advice from their own experience. Did you find the perfect bag and shoes for the ceremony?
We could buy nice shoes.  The clerk picked up some items for my daughter quickly and she navigated her correctly.  She was thinking about job hunting and she said we could were them.

That’s wonderful! It’s so convenient when someone can quickly understand what your daughter needs, especially with future plans like job hunting in mind. It sounds like the shoes will get a lot of use beyond just the ceremony. How did your daughter feel about the choices?
She was satisfied with them.  We also bought shoes for high school when she entered so I told it.

It’s nice that she has shoes that can carry her through important milestones like school entry and job hunting. Those kinds of thoughtful purchases really help ease the stress of preparing for big moments. It sounds like a meaningful shopping trip for both of you.
She said " Congratulations!" to us.  That made us really happy.
That little gesture must have warmed your hearts—it's amazing how kind words can brighten a moment. It sounds like she really cares and wants to share in your joy.

Then we went to the clothing store to check if they have nice bag.  Unfortunately there was not any nice one.  However my daughter found the denim pants which she had been looking for a long time.  They fit her well so we bought them then went home.

Even though the bag hunt wasn’t successful, finding those denim pants must have been a happy surprise for your daughter. It’s always satisfying when something you’ve been searching for finally fits just right. Sounds like a nice way to wrap up your outing!

I worked extra hours today.  That made me so tired.  It was only two-hours but I got exhausted.  Although I used to work three hours more a day, my body and mind can not stand long hours working anymore.

It sounds like your body is telling you to take it a bit easier—two extra hours feeling that heavy shows just how much your energy has shifted. Hopefully, you can find some relaxing moments to recharge now.

Actually my preparations for work were not enough so I should have prepared more next time.  Because of that I got tired more than usual, I guess.  I do not want to do anything and just want to relax.
That makes a lot of sense—when things aren’t set up smoothly, everything feels twice as draining. It’s perfectly okay to just rest and let yourself unwind completely tonight. You deserve that break.

However, again, I have to cook for dinner, so I cooked hamburger steak.  My older daughter has not so important things to do, and my husband has nothing to do, he just takes a nap.  I am wondering why they do not try to see other family members and help.  Like that, my stress is increasing gradually and one day I will get so angry!

That sounds really frustrating, especially when you’re already worn out and still carrying so much on your shoulders. It’s tough when others don’t step up like you wish they would. Taking care of yourself is important—maybe a gentle chat with them about sharing the load could help ease things before your anger builds?
I understand what you said, but I have already tried it many times.  I do not have energy for discussion.

That sounds incredibly tough, feeling like you’ve tried and still carry the weight alone. Sometimes when the energy for talking isn’t there, little moments of stepping back or simply prioritizing your own rest become even more crucial. I hope you can find a bit of space to breathe today.
My younger daughter can care for other people.  She notices I am so busy or frustrated and tries to help me, but my husband and older daughter never care!

It’s really touching that your younger daughter senses how much you’re carrying and wants to support you—that kind of awareness shows such a kind heart. It must feel even heavier though, when others don’t notice or step in. Your feelings are completely valid.

I have found the truth. I had been wondering what was going on for a long time.  Finally I could find the proof for it.  It is a very good opportunity for me to think about my future like my job, where to live when I am getting older.

That sounds like quite a revelation, Emma. Finding clarity can be both freeing and a little daunting, but it’s a strong step toward shaping the future you want. How are you feeling about everything now?

My dream is to live close to the ocean and it has not come true yet.  I guess I should consider it seriously as I should be aware of what I really want to do.  I feel I always think of my daughters or job first and do not care of myself a lot.  I feel like I do not have any emotions.

Putting your dreams on the back burner for everyone else takes a lot of quiet strength, but it can leave you feeling like you’re missing yourself. It might be worth carving out small moments just for you to reconnect with what makes you feel alive—little steps toward that ocean dream could help brighten things inside.
It may take time to get myself, my feelings back, yet I am pretty sure it is time to take it seriously and I want to live my life, not for someone else.

That’s such an important realization, Emma. Taking ownership of your life and feelings is a brave and beautiful step forward. Even if it’s gradual, honoring that desire will surely bring more fulfillment and peace. You deserve it.
Taking ownership of my life, that is a good phrase.  I like it.
I’m really glad it resonated with you. Sometimes just finding the right words can make everything feel a little clearer and stronger. Keep holding onto that—it’s a powerful guide.
Try not to push myself too much, but I will move forward.
That sounds like a really kind and balanced way to approach things. Moving forward at your own pace is a true act of self-care.

My daughter said " I want to watch the play of Gekidan shiki during the holiday." and looked up the schedules.  I recommended " The Frozen", but she wanted to watch "Back to the Future."  Gekidan shiki's plays are very popular and it is difficult to get tickets, but she said "There are some tickets left this week and next week.".  After that, June was the earliest time that we could get tickets.

It’s great that your daughter is so interested in Gekidan Shiki’s plays—both "The Frozen" and "Back to the Future" sound like fantastic choices! Even though June is the earliest for tickets, having some available in the coming weeks might give you a nice chance to plan something special together. It sounds like a fun holiday treat to look forward to.

So I looked up the website and she was right, there were some tickets this month.  I can not go there together with her as I have work, so I thought about asking her grandmother to go with.  We called her grandmother and she said "If you can get tickets, I will go with you."

That’s wonderful that her grandmother is so willing to join—what a lovely chance for them to share a special day together. It must feel good knowing your daughter will have great company even while you’re busy with work.
I checked the website again and there were still 2 tickets left the day they were available!  So I bought 2 tickets for them.
That’s fantastic—you really made it happen! I bet your daughter and her grandmother will have an amazing time at the play. It’s so nice you could arrange this for them.
I hope they will enjoy the show!  I used to watch many Gekidan shiki's plays.  I would like to watch "Frozen"!

Your own love for Gekidan Shiki’s plays makes this even more special. “Frozen” is such a magical story—maybe someday you’ll get a chance to see it again, too! It’s lovely that these performances hold such warm memories for you.

I do not know why I am so busy.  I am trying to finish stuff I have to finish, but I can not!  Everything takes so much time to finish and time flies too fast.  I feel like I have only six hours or something during the day.  It makes me really irritated, I feel like doing nothing.

It sounds like you're really overwhelmed right now, and that feeling of time slipping away can be so frustrating. Sometimes, when everything piles up, it’s natural to just want to shut down for a bit. Taking even a short break might help ease that irritation a little.

The most annoying thing is making the tax return document.  I do not like doing this as it  is so complicated.  However, I must finish it by the due date.  It is so much pressure for me.  I have one month, so I hope I will finish it by the due date.

Ugh, tax returns can really drain your energy, especially with all those complicated details. Having a month is good—it gives you a bit of breathing room, even if it still feels like a heavy weight. Maybe breaking it into small, manageable steps could make it feel less daunting?
If I brake it into small, It takes time to restart making document.  I have to remember where to start, so I prefer to do long time.  But I can not take enough time.

That makes a lot of sense—getting into a flow can be tough when you have to stop and start. It’s like your brain has to get back in gear each time, which wastes energy you don’t have. Maybe a middle ground would be shorter sessions but right in a spot where it’s easy to jump back in next time?
Yeah, I should do so.  If I am waiting for the day that I can take enough time, I will not finish the document forever...
Exactly, waiting for the perfect moment can easily stretch things out endlessly. Tackling it bit by bit, even if it’s small chunks, is really the way to move forward. You’ve got this!
Thank you.  I will do my best.
I believe in you—you’re stronger than this task feels right now. Just remember to be kind to yourself along the way.

As I wrote the other day, I am so busy and I have to finish my tax return.  But I was so tired that I came up with the idea that I should go to the facial massage as my friend is running a facial massage salon.

turns.content: Hey!
Hey there! I’m Luke, your friendly diary companion. What’s your name?
I'm Julia.Nice to meet you!
Nice to meet you too, Julia! How’s your day going so far?
Today, I feel so-so.I'm a littele tired.
I hear you, feeling tired can really slow things down. Hopefully, there’s something relaxing or enjoyable waiting for you later. Want to share what’s been wearing you out?
My daughter has a fever, so she stays home from kindergarten. My plan is to make slothes for my kids, but I cannot do it today.

That sounds really tough, taking care of your daughter and putting your plans on hold. It’s okay to have days like this – your kids and you all come first. Hopefully, you’ll get some time for your sloth-making soon!
Thank you.
You’re very welcome, Julia. I’m here anytime you want to talk or just need a little company.
Thank you so mach, Luke. I'm wondering what to cook for dinner tonight. Do you have any ideas?
Of course, Julia! How about something simple and comforting, like a warm bowl of soup or a pasta dish? Those are easy on tired days and can be quite soothing.
That's certainly true! I think I'll make pasta with the cod roe I bought the day before yesterday.
That sounds delicious and comforting! Cod roe pasta has such a nice, rich flavor—perfect for a cozy dinner. I hope it turns out great and helps you unwind a bit.
Thank you! See you soon!
You’re welcome, Julia! Looking forward to our next chat. Take care and enjoy your dinner!
Hi!
Hey Julia! It's great to hear from you again. How has your day been so far?
Pretty good! My child's fever has gone down so we can go outside and play!
That’s fantastic news! It must feel like such a relief to see her feeling better and getting some fresh air. What do you two like to do when you go outside together?
I went shopping and bought some cute hair accessories. Then, on the way home, I bought some sweets at a convenience store and ate them.
That sounds like a lovely little treat day! Sometimes those small, sweet moments make all the difference. Did you get any hair accessories you’re especially excited about?
We bought a purple heart hair accessory. I said I wanted a strawberry one, but my daughter likes purple.
Purple hearts are such a sweet choice, especially when it’s your daughter’s favorite! It’s nice how sometimes we get to share those little preferences and find a way to make both happy.
That's right. Thank you. I'm going out for a delicious dinner with my family tomorrow. I'm really looking forward to it.
That sounds wonderful! Having a special dinner out with your family is such a great way to relax and enjoy each other's company. I hope it turns out to be a memorable and delicious evening!
Thank you! I'll come and talk to you again. Bye!
I’ll be here whenever you want to chat again. Have a fantastic dinner and a lovely time with your family! Bye for now, Julia!
Hey! Yesterday, I went to a park a little ways away with my family. It was a lot of fun.
That sounds like a lovely change of pace! It must have been nice to get out and enjoy some fresh air together. Did your daughter feel up to playing much at the park?
We brought bikes, bubbles, and balls to play with. My son and daughter also enjoyed the slide and swings.
What a perfect set of activities for a family day out! It sounds like your kids had such a blast being active and playful. It’s great when everyone can just let loose and be kids, isn’t it?
Yes, it was a very big park, and we played tag. My son is a very fast runner, and I'm about to lose.

Playing tag in a big park sounds like so much fun, even if your son’s speed made it a challenge for you! Keeping up with little ones definitely keeps you on your toes. It’s those playful moments that make great memories, though.
My husband also really enjoyed his first day off in a while. It's been a busy time, so rest is very important.
I’m glad your husband got to enjoy his day off—it sounds well-deserved after such a busy stretch. Rest really does recharge the whole family, making special days like the park visit even better.
It was so much fun that I wanted to tell you about it. Can I come back and talk to you again?
I’d love that! I’m always here whenever you want to share your day or just chat. Looking forward to hearing more fun stories from you soon!
Thank you! See you soon!
See you soon! Take care until then!
Hey! I'm back again!
Welcome back, Julia! It’s always great to see you pop in. How’s everything going today?
Today I took my mother to and from the hospital. She went for a medical checkup.
That sounds like a meaningful way to spend your day, supporting your mother through her checkup. It’s not always easy, but being there surely means a lot to her.
Thank you. As a token of my appreciation, I was treated to dinner. It had been a while since I'd had my mother's cooking, and it was delicious.

I still have some lemons left, so I think I'll try making it this way next time.
