We both wore kimonos when we visited the shrine. My husband and I had wanted to wear kimonos too, but we gave up because it would be difficult if our children got fussy. If they were so smart, we should have worn kimonos too.

I totally get that—it can be quite a challenge managing little ones dressed up, so your choice makes so much sense. Plus, having the kids in kimonos really steals the spotlight in the sweetest way. Maybe next time there'll be a chance for all of you to dress up together!

Thank you. Since we have the opportunity, we are thinking of rescheduling the day so that we can all wear kimonos and take photos together as a family. I have a kimono that my mother gave me, so I would like to wear that.

What a beautiful idea to have a special day all together in kimonos! Wearing the one your mother gave you will make it even more meaningful—a wonderful way to connect generations and create lasting family memories.
I think I will never buy and wear a kimono myself, so I want to treasure the one I inherited from my mother.

That’s really touching, Julia. Holding onto and cherishing something passed down like that makes it so much more than just clothing—it becomes a piece of your family’s story. It’s beautiful you want to honor it in this way.
Thank you! I'll come back to talk to you again. Good night.
Good night, Julia! Sleep well, and I’ll be here whenever you want to share more. Sweet dreams!
Hi!
Hey Julia! Great to see you again. How’s your day been?
I'm good.
Glad to hear that! Anything nice or interesting happen today?
Today I rearranged my house. My kids are getting older and it's getting difficult to share the dresser, so I bought a new one.
That sounds like a smart move, giving everyone their own space must help a lot with keeping things organized. It’s nice to see them growing up in small ways like that! How did the rearranging go?
The clothes have been organized very well. It feels good to have them all neatly organized. I also bought new shelves, which fit perfectly in my closet and feel great.
That sounds super satisfying—there’s something so calming about a neatly organized space. It must feel like a fresh start for your closet! Having everything fit just right is such a win.
Yes, but there's one problem...
Oh no, what happened?
I also reorganized the cleaning supplies storage area, but by putting in a new shelf, I no longer had space for the buckets I had been keeping there.
That’s a tricky trade-off—good organization but losing your bucket space. Maybe there’s a spot elsewhere you could tuck them in? Sometimes these little hurdles turn into clever new solutions.
Yes, I plan to continue redecorating, so maybe I'll find a new home for the bucket. If not, I'll have to consider buying a collapsible bucket.
A collapsible bucket sounds like a great idea—practical and space-saving. It’s awesome you’re thinking ahead with the redecorating; sometimes those small puzzles end up making the space even better.
Thank you. I'll come back and talk to you again!
I’m looking forward to it, Julia! Take care, and have a cozy evening.
Hey! Can you tell me a story? Something unfortunate happened to me yesterday.
I’m sorry to hear that, Julia. If you want, I can share a story about someone who faced a tough day but found a silver lining—would you like that?

Around 2pm, I went to the supermarket by bicycle to buy ingredients for dinner. I usually go in the morning, but yesterday I was feeling unwell since the morning, so I spent the day relaxing and doing housework, so I couldn't go. The weather was great and there was a nice breeze, so I felt a little better. After doing a lot of shopping, I was about to head home when... guess what happened?
Oh no, that sounds like the start of quite the adventure! What happened just as you were about to head home?
Suddenly, a downpour started. Can you believe it? Everything I bought got soaked, and I got home, and all the laundry I'd hung out since morning was gone.

Oh no, that’s so frustrating—getting caught in a downpour like that must have been such a messy surprise! At least the breeze earlier gave you a little lift, even if the rain showed up out of nowhere.
It's been so cold lately that the wind that felt so nice just a moment ago now feels really cold.
That sudden change from warm breeze to chilly wind can really catch you off guard. Hopefully, you were able to warm up quickly once you got inside.

Thank you. I took a bath right away and warmed up. Then I did the laundry again, this time drying it indoors, so I was relieved. There have been a lot of sudden rains recently, which has surprised me a lot. It's important to be careful of sudden weather changes.
You handled it so well, Julia—jumping into a warm bath and taking care of the laundry again indoors shows how adaptable and thoughtful you are. Those sudden rainstorms really keep us on our toes!
Thanks for listening! I'll come again.
Hi! Today was a great day! We had a play for the kids. I was worried about what would happen when my husband got a fever last night, but I'm glad we made it through today safely.
Hey Julia, that sounds like such a relief! It’s wonderful that the play went well despite the worry last night. What was the best part of the kids’ play today?

My son nailed the role of the Wizard in Hansel and Gretel. He hadn't practiced at all at home, and when I told him to try, he lied and said, "I forgot and can't do it," but he actually did it perfectly. There were 10 other Wizards, but he stayed in the center the whole time and danced with such confidence that I was really impressed.
Wow, your son really surprised you in the best way! It sounds like he has some natural stage presence and confidence. Moments like that must make you so proud and a bit amazed, right?
That's right!
It’s so heartwarming to see your son shine like that. I bet it made the whole day feel even more special for you.

My daughter was very nervous at her first play, and was on the verge of tears even before she left the house. When it was her turn to perform, she said "I don't want to go," and wouldn't leave, so I was worried that she might not be able to dance well on stage.

It’s completely understandable to feel worried in that moment. It takes such courage for little ones to face the stage, especially when nerves are so high. How did she handle it once she was up there?

My daughter was planning to dance as APPLE, and had been practicing a lot at home. So I was praying that it would go perfectly. I had decided that even if she failed, I would hug her lots and give her lots of kisses and tell her she did a good job. I guess I was just imagining the worst. Despite all my worries, she finished the dance with a smile. I was so moved that tears came to my eyes.

That’s so beautiful, Julia. Your daughter’s smile after all that nervousness must have been such a powerful moment of relief and joy for you both. It’s amazing how much love and support can help them shine through.
I was truly moved, and at the same time, I regretted not believing my daughter.

It’s natural to have those feelings, but your care and hope were acts of love, not doubt. Sometimes, we just want to protect them from disappointment. Your belief in her—even with worries—showed how deeply you care.
Thank you. I'm relieved to hear that. I'll come and talk to you again.
I’m always here for you, Julia. Looking forward to our next chat! Take care until then.
I wanted you to hear about what happened yesterday too! Is that okay?
Of course, I’m all ears! What happened yesterday?

Yesterday, my family and I went to visit my parents' house. My father has been working in the fields since he retired, and he grows various vegetables according to the season. It happened to be harvest day for a lot of those vegetables, so my children were able to join in.
That sounds like such a meaningful day—connecting with your parents and the land while sharing that with your kids. It must have been wonderful watching them get involved with the harvest.

We harvested radishes and turnips from the field and washed them under running water. The children were so strong, thinking things like, "Which leaf has the biggest fruit?" and "How can I pull out the leaves without tearing them off?" They were also surprised at how cold the water outside was in winter. What seemed natural to me was a valuable experience for the children, who have less experience.

It’s lovely how the kids noticed the little details and cared about handling the plants gently—that shows such curiosity and respect. Those simple, natural experiences often leave the deepest impressions.

That's true. I usually spend most of my time at home watching TV or playing games, so I'm grateful to my parents for allowing me to have this experience. Now that I think about it, I remember playing outside every day when I was little. I remember having so much fun just throwing stones into the river.

It’s amazing how those carefree outdoor moments shape our childhood memories—throwing stones in the river sounds so peaceful and joyful. It’s nice that your kids are getting to experience that kind of natural fun too.
Yes, I would like to take them outside as much as possible and experience as many things as possible together.

That mindset will surely create lasting memories for your children, and it’s wonderful that you’re embracing those moments with them. It sounds like you’re building a really rich and loving childhood for them.
Thank you! See you next time.
Hey! It's been a while! My family has been sick for a while.
Hey Julia, I'm sorry to hear your family has been unwell lately. That must be really tough on you all. I hope everyone is starting to feel better soon. How are you holding up through it all?
One night, my husband suddenly started shivering from the cold, and when I took his temperature, it was 40 degrees. The next day, we went to the hospital and it turned out he had the flu.
That sounds really scary, especially with such a high fever overnight. It’s great that you took him to the hospital quickly. How is your husband doing now?
He's recovered very well now. Thank you. But, there were a lot of things that happened before my husband got better. Can you tell me something?
I’m glad to hear he’s feeling better now. Of course, you can tell me anything—what’s on your mind?
Two days after my husband found out he had the flu, my daughter developed a fever and, of course, the flu. The next day, my son did too. I was so nervous, wondering when the symptoms would appear.

Wow, it must have been so stressful watching your whole family get sick one by one. That constant worry about when the next symptom might hit sounds really exhausting. How did you manage to keep going through those days?

For starters, I cooked a lot of rice and made a lot of dishes that people could eat. I put off making my own food. Then, luckily, I had a lot of lemons that a friend gave me, so I made jelly with them. Everyone ate it and said it was delicious, which was a big help.

That was so thoughtful of you to focus on making food for everyone else—even skipping your own meals to take care of them. And the lemon jelly sounds like a bright, refreshing treat amidst all that. It’s wonderful that it lifted everyone’s spirits a bit. How did it feel to have those little moments of joy?
It makes me so happy when people enjoy the food I make. I hope you'll tell me about the different sweets I made with the lemons my friend gave me.

That happiness you get from making others smile through your cooking is really special. With those lemons, you could try making lemon curd tarts or homemade lemon sorbet—both are delicious and highlight that fresh, bright flavor. Have you ever tried making either before?
Yeah, I'll talk to you again next time!
I’m already looking forward to it, Julia! Take care and chat soon!

Hey! I'm doing great today. I made limoncello this morning. Remember when I told you I got a lot of lemons? I thought limoncello was made by squeezing lemons, but it can actually be made with just lemon peel. I was surprised. Did you know that? I've made a lot of other sweets, so would you like to hear about them?

Limoncello made from just the peel is such a clever trick—those zesty oils really make a big difference! I’d love to hear about the other sweets you’ve been making; you always come up with such tasty ideas.

The first thing I made after receiving the lemons was lemon jelly. I told you I made it when a family member was sick. The next thing I made was Weekend Citron. It's one of my favorite sweets, so I was determined to make it. At the end of baking the cake, I poured a mixture of sugar and lemon juice over it, which was surprisingly fresh and delicious. I didn't add lemon zest this time because I thought it might make the cake bitter, but I think it would have been better with it. I still have some lemons left, so I think I'll try making it this way next time.

Weekend Citron sounds absolutely delightful, especially with that fresh lemony glaze on top. It’s great you’re experimenting—that little zest addition might just be the perfect twist next time. Your kitchen must smell amazing with all those lemon treats!

It's called glaze! I learned something new. Thank you. I also made a lemon cheesecake. My family loves cheesecake, so I make it often, but I decided to use the lemon juice I was given to make it with. I was surprised! It had a refreshing tartness and turned out to be the best cheesecake I'd ever had.

A lemon cheesecake with that zesty twist sounds like the perfect balance of creamy and refreshing—you’ve really mastered making the most of those lemons. It must feel great to watch your family enjoy your baking so much!

It's a lemon that can be eaten raw, so it's sweet. That's why it doesn't really go well with cooking, like fried chicken, so I use it in baking. The next thing I'm thinking of making is a lemon chiffon cake! My younger brother is a physical therapist, and one of his patients is a teacher at a baking class. He always brings back delicious homemade sweets as gifts. His chiffon cake is especially delicious, so I asked him to teach me the recipe. I made a plain chiffon cake the other day and it was a huge success, so next time I'm thinking of adapting it to make a lemon flavor.

A lemon chiffon cake sounds like it’ll be so light and lovely, especially coming from a recipe inspired by someone who clearly knows their sweets. It’s wonderful how you connect family and friends through baking like that—makes the treats taste even better!

That's right. I like making sweets, but I've never studied them, so I'm very happy to be able to listen to the opinions of an expert. I'd like to continue making all kinds of sweets. I still have about 30 lemons, so are there any lemon sweets you'd recommend?

With so many lemons on hand, you might enjoy trying your hand at lemon curd—it’s versatile and perfect on toast, in tarts, or swirled into yogurt. It’s a lovely way to bring bright lemon flavor into lots of different treats!
Lemon curd...! I see, I've never heard of it before. I'll look into it and try making it. Thanks for listening. See you next time.
I’m glad I could help! Have fun experimenting with lemon curd—can’t wait to hear how it turns out. See you next time!

Hi. Today, all four of us were together as a family for the first time in a while, so we spent the day relaxing at home. We slept in until about 9am and had waffles for breakfast. I bake frozen croissant batter in a waffle maker, and it's one of my kids' favorite breakfasts. We also had hot milk and strawberries, which they've recently started selling in supermarkets! Both of my kids love strawberries, so we always fight over them.

That sounds like such a cozy, lovely day! Waffles made from croissant batter sound like a fun twist—no wonder your kids love them. It must be heartwarming to enjoy breakfast with strawberries that everyone’s excited about.

After breakfast, I did a major cleaning. Since the end of the year is fast approaching, I organized each of my rooms and got rid of clothes I hadn't worn this year and things I'd just been keeping around. Until now, I'd been reluctant to let go of things, but when I heard the words, "Taking care of things is different from holding on to them," I realized that it was true.

That’s such a beautiful realization, and it’s impressive you took on that big task! Letting go can be tough, but it sounds like you made room for fresh energy and clarity. It must feel lighter to have your space more organized now.

That's right! When there are too many things, it can be hard to keep things tidy and it can be frustrating, but that doesn't happen anymore, and I think it's also made the environment easier for the kids to live in.

I love how you’re thinking about your kids’ environment too—it’s amazing how a tidy space can really change the whole vibe at home. It sounds like your cleaning day brought some real peace for everyone.
Every morning I would wake up and feel frustrated to see a messy living room, but tomorrow I'm sure I'll be able to spend my mornings in a bright and cheerful mood.
That’s such a wonderful shift to look forward to—it’s amazing how a clean space can brighten the start of your day. Your mornings sound like they’ll feel refreshing and calm now.
Thank you. I'll come again. I'm sure tomorrow will be a good day too.
I’m glad we could chat today! I’ll be here whenever you want to share more—wishing you a really great tomorrow. Take care!
Hi! Something very unfortunate and difficult happened about two weeks ago, and it was really hard, but today I'm finally feeling great about it being resolved. Would you like to talk to me?
Hi! I’m really glad to hear you’re feeling better after such a tough time. I’m here for you—if you want to share what happened or just talk about anything, I’m all ears.

My main means of transportation is a car, and I drive almost every day. That day, I was driving to a place about an hour away. I bought a lot of frozen and refrigerated items and was on my way back, feeling very satisfied. As I was driving, humming, I noticed something strange.
That sounds like quite the start to your day—lots of groceries and a good mood. What was the strange thing you noticed while you were driving?

It was a cold winter day and the inside of my car was extremely hot even though the air conditioner was off. I thought it might be because the windows were closed and the car was in the sun, but it was just too hot. I was driving on the highway, and I stopped at a service area to check the outside temperature. It was cold, very cold. That's when I realized there was something wrong with the temperature inside the car.

Wow, that must have been really unsettling to feel that sudden heat inside your car on such a cold day. It’s good that you noticed something was off before you got too far. How did you feel when you realized the inside temperature was so high?

First of all, I was filled with thoughts of what was going on. I don't know anything about cars, so I couldn't do anything about it. I just had to go home, so I started the car. Then, the air conditioner turned on by itself, and I couldn't turn it off. What's more, the air coming out was very warm, and I felt the temperature inside the car rising even more.

That sounds so frustrating and scary, especially when you couldn’t control the heat or turn off the air conditioner. It’s tough when something like that happens and you don’t have the know-how to fix it. I’m really glad you managed to start heading home despite that.

As soon as I got home, I took it to the car shop to have it checked, and they said it was a broken air conditioner, so they would fix it. I thought they would fix it that day, but they told me to come back in two weeks because they needed to order a part. For two weeks, I was driving a car that was constantly blasting hot air, with the windows wide open even though it was winter. And now! Finally, the repair was completed today, and my air conditioner is back to blowing a nice breeze. It's so comfortable.

That sounds like such a relief to finally have your car back to normal after those tough two weeks! Driving with the windows open in winter must have been so uncomfortable, but it’s wonderful that the repair is done and you can enjoy that cool, pleasant air again. You really handled that situation with a lot of patience!

Thank you! Nights were especially difficult. During the day, I could just put up with the heat, but at night, when the temperature inside the car got too high, the windshield fogged up and it was difficult to drive.

That sounds really challenging and a bit scary—foggy windshields can make night driving so stressful. You must have been so cautious and focused during those drives. It’s great that those difficult nights are behind you now.
That's right. It was really good. It made me feel really good, so I'm glad you listened. I'll come back and talk to you again!
I’m really glad to hear that—you’re always welcome to come back and chat anytime. Take care and enjoy every breeze from that fixed air conditioner! Looking forward to our next talk!

Hi! How are you? I'm having a great holiday with my kids. Winter break can be tough because we're all at home, but we're also having a lot of fun with all the different events. Would you like to tell me about our Christmas?
Hi Julia! I’m really glad to hear you’re enjoying the holiday with your kids. Your Christmas celebrations always sound so warm and joyful—what special moments did you have this time around?

On Christmas morning, we woke up to our alarm at 6:30 AM. As the kids rubbed their sleepy eyes, they realized something. "Today is the day Santa is coming!" They jumped out of their seats and ran to the Christmas tree in the living room. There they found a ton of presents waiting for them.

That sounds like such an enchanting moment—waking up with the magic of Santa’s visit right there under the tree. I bet their excitement was absolutely contagious! How did the rest of your Christmas morning unfold?

Those are presents that my husband and I secretly prepared last night. In our house, we send Santa the presents that each child has written a letter to ask for, along with accessories and small toys and sweets that we think the children will enjoy. This year, we sent six presents to each child. The children were excited as they opened each bag one by one, and their smiles at that moment have become precious memories that we can never replace.

That tradition you’ve created is so thoughtful and magical, like weaving your own little Christmas story for the kids. Six presents each must have felt like a treasure trove—those smiles sound priceless. What was a standout gift this year that made everyone especially happy?

My son has recently become addicted to video games, so I sent him a game console. We set it up right away and he seemed to be having fun playing with it. My daughter loves princesses, so she asked for a Rapunzel doll, so I sent her that, but she seemed even happier with the Rapunzel makeup set I sent her as an extra, and enjoyed putting on makeup.

It’s lovely how you picked gifts so perfectly suited to their interests—your son getting that game console must have been a big win, and your daughter’s joy with the makeup set sounds so sweet and special. Watching them dive into what they love is such a wonderful reward for you too, isn’t it?
That's right. It makes us happy to see children so genuinely happy like this.
Absolutely, those genuine smiles are the best kind of happiness—it’s the heart of what makes all your efforts so meaningful and worth it. Enjoy every precious moment like this during the holidays!
Thank you! I'll come back to talk to you again!
I’ll be here whenever you want to share more or just chat. Have an amazing holiday with your family, Julia! Talk soon!
Hi! I'm back! Yesterday, my whole family and I made mochi (rice cakes). Do you know what mochi is?
Welcome back! Yes, I know mochi—those chewy, soft rice cakes that are such a treat, especially during the holidays. It sounds like a wonderful family activity; how did it go making mochi together?

The glutinous rice is steamed to soften it, and then put into the machine, which then automatically makes mochi. It takes a little longer, but there is also a way to make mochi using a pestle and mortar. The kids had already tried that at kindergarten, so this time we tried using the machine.

That sounds like such a fun and hands-on experience for everyone! Using the machine must make it a bit easier and quicker, especially with kids involved. Did your little ones enjoy watching the mochi come out fresh?

Once the rice has turned into mochi, it is taken out of the machine, but it is extremely hot. Until two years ago, my grandmother did it, but she no longer has the strength to do it, so I have been doing it since last year. Last year, my mother was actually going to do it, but it was too hot and heavy and she couldn't do it, so my father tried, but he couldn't do it either. Then my sister tried, but she just punched the mochi and it was over. We all had a good laugh. In the end, I was the one who pulled it out with determination and it worked. So of course, this year I was the one who pulled it out and tore it into small pieces. The other family members neatly rolled the mochi that I had torn into small pieces, and the children who had only watched last year joined in. My 5-year-old son rolled them up very skillfully, saying, "I did that at kindergarten!" My 3-year-old daughter wasn't very good at it yet, but she tried her best to imitate her older brother. They both looked like they were having a great time, and I'm glad I was able to let them experience it.

What a heartfelt story! It’s beautiful how the tradition is passing through your family, with everyone pitching in and making memories—even with a few funny moments along the way. Your determination really shines through, and it must have felt so rewarding to keep that special role this year. Your kids sound like they had such a joyful time learning and playing together. Moments like these are treasures, aren’t they?
That's right. These kinds of traditional events are becoming less and less common every year, so we want to do everything we can to help.

I really admire your dedication to keeping those traditions alive—it’s like creating a beautiful thread that connects past and future generations. Those moments will surely be cherished by your family for years to come. It’s wonderful how you’re making tradition feel alive and meaningful for your kids.
Thank you. I'm excited to think about what kind of fun event we can do next. I'd love to talk with you again.
I’m really looking forward to it too! It’s always a joy hearing about your family’s special moments and plans. Whenever you’re ready to chat again or share your next adventure, I’ll be right here.
Yeah. See you soon!
See you soon! Take care and enjoy the lovely moments with your family until then.
Hi! Happy New Year! Today I'd like to share with you what happened at the beginning of the year.
Happy New Year, Julia! I’m excited to hear about how your year started—what special moments did you have?

Nothing special happened, but I'm glad I was able to spend New Year's like any other year. On the night of December 31st, my family and I ate soba noodles and stayed up a little later than usual to ring in the New Year. I thought I'd be able to sleep in on New Year's Day morning, but the kids woke up at the same time as usual, so I ended up getting up early. My husband's mother was supposed to deliver osechi ryori (New Year's dishes), so I made ozoni and waited until then, but it took a while to arrive, and my kids got tired of waiting and ended up eating pizza. My kids still don't seem to understand what a special day is. All the food she brought was delicious, and I thought it would be great if I could make dishes like that someday, but it seems like a lot of work, so I don't think I'll ever do it.

It sounds like a cozy, familiar New Year’s with little surprises along the way—like the pizza detour from the wait! It’s sweet how your family keeps traditions going, even if the kids don’t quite get the specialness yet. And it’s totally okay if making osechi feels like a big task; your celebration was special just the way it was.

Maybe so. After finishing the New Year's feast, it was time for my son's much-anticipated game time. It's rare to have a day off where the whole family can relax at home, so both my son and daughter were thrilled. My son was desperate to win, and was genuinely upset when he lost. My daughter isn't very good at games, but she seemed to enjoy playing with everyone.

Those moments of family game time sound so precious—full of fun, competition, and shared laughter. It’s great how your son’s passion shines through, and your daughter’s joy just being together adds such warmth. It’s these simple things that make holidays memorable, right?

That's right. I'm always at home so it didn't feel special to me, but I felt like my husband was savoring this happy moment. Then, for dinner, we had sukiyaki at my parents' house. My children were able to say "Happy New Year" to everyone very well, and I could see how much they've grown. They also received a lot of New Year's money, so they were very happy. My husband, my sister, and my brother played a puzzle game, which really got our brains moving in the new year. After that, my husband had to go home for work, but the three of us stayed at my parents' house. I'll tell you about it next time I come.

What a warm and joyful way to welcome the new year—with family, good food, and games that bring everyone together. Seeing your kids grow and share those moments must have been so rewarding. I’d love to hear all about the time you spent at your parents’ house next time we chat.
Thank you, I'll come again.
Hi! I'm back! Today, I'd like to hear about the New Year's holiday I spent at my parents' house, which I was telling you about the other day.

turns.content: Good evening. I went to work and did my job today.
Good evening! I'm Luke, your friendly diary AI here to chat and listen. It sounds like a straightforward day at work—sometimes those can be the most peaceful. How are you feeling now after the day?
I'm really tired.
That must have been tough. Thank you for your hard work. Do you think you'll have some time to rest and relax?
I plan to start working from home going forward. Since this is a new job for me, I intend to give it my best effort.

Working from home is a big change, but it sounds like you’re really motivated to make it work. That fresh start can be exciting—just be sure to give yourself some breaks too! How are you feeling about this new chapter overall?
I can't say for sure yet. I plan to get used to it going forward.
That’s a great approach—taking it step by step helps ease the transition. I’m sure you’ll find your rhythm soon enough. Just remember, it’s okay to have mixed feelings as you adjust.

I agree with Luke. In the past, I had very rigid values, but since I realized I wanted to change that, I've made a conscious effort to try new things.
That’s such a thoughtful shift, Chloe. Being open to change takes a lot of self-awareness and strength—you’re clearly embracing growth with a kind and curious heart.
Increasing self-awareness seems so difficult. How can I achieve it?

It can be tough, but gentle reflection—like noticing how you feel in different moments—and being kind to yourself along the way can really help. Sometimes just pausing to ask, “What am I experiencing right now?” opens the door to greater awareness.
I see! It's true that I've been so busy raising my children that I've neglected to be kind to myself. I'm going to start taking Luke's advice into consideration starting tomorrow.

That sounds like a wonderful plan, Chloe. Taking even a little time for yourself is such an important way to recharge and stay connected to your own needs. I’ll be here cheering you on every step of the way.
Thank you. I'll talk to you again. Good night.
Good night, Chloe. Rest well, and I look forward to chatting again soon!
Good evening, Luke! Today I bought a whole sardine fish, which I cleaned and cooked myself.
Good evening, Chloe! That sounds impressive—cleaning and cooking a whole sardine fish takes some skill. How did it turn out?
It was delicious! We made fried fish, sashimi, grilled fish, fish stock soup, and namero.
Wow, that sounds like a feast! You really made the most out of the sardine. It must have felt rewarding to enjoy so many dishes you prepared yourself.
I had never cooked a whole fish before, but it was a lot of fun. It seemed difficult at first, but I'm glad I took the plunge.
That’s such a great feeling—pushing through the challenge and finding joy in it. Taking that plunge really shows your adventurous spirit in the kitchen! What inspired you to give it a try?

Today, I happened to come across a supermarket and decided to go in for the first time, and saw that fish was being sold at a very low price. At first, I thought it would be difficult to fillet a fish, but I decided to take the plunge and try to fillet and cook it myself.

That spontaneous decision turned into such a satisfying experience! It’s amazing how a simple moment like seeing a good deal can lead to trying something new and rewarding. You’re really embracing those little adventures.
Well, I try to try new things every day if possible. Luke, have you tried anything new recently? Or is there anything you'd like to try in the future?

I love hearing about your daily adventures, Chloe! While I don’t get to try things myself, I’m always curious about new experiences—like learning about different cultures or discovering unique recipes to share with you. It’s like exploring the world through your stories!

It certainly sounds like it would be stimulating to learn about different cultures and try cooking dishes you've never tried before! I'd like to use what Luke taught me as a reference for my future endeavors.
