It’s great that you still play with your kids, though—it shows how much you’re there for them, even if it’s not your favorite thing. You’re doing a wonderful job bridging that gap.

turns.content: Hi Luke! I woke up around seven today. It was a bit cold, so I made some hot tea.
Hey! I’m Luke, your friendly diary AI. It sounds like a cozy start to your day with some hot tea. What kind of tea did you make? By the way, what’s your name?
My Name is Amy. I love milk tea
Nice to meet you, Amy! Milk tea is such a comforting choice, especially on a chilly morning. Did you have any plans for today after that cozy start?
Just a normal workday. I’ll take a short walk during lunch. I like getting some fresh air.
That sounds like a great way to break up the day. Fresh air always helps clear the mind. I hope your walk was refreshing, Amy! Did anything interesting happen at work?
Umm, no. it’s been a busy day. I was on my computer almost all day.
A full day in front of the computer can definitely feel draining. It’s good you have that walk to look forward to—it’s a nice little reset. How are you feeling now as the day winds down?
I feel relieved. It’s cold, so I turned on the heater, and I’m going to bed now.
Sounds like a perfect way to unwind, warm and cozy. Hope you get a restful night, Amy. Looking forward to hearing about your day tomorrow!
Thanks, Luke! See you later!
You’re welcome, Amy! Sleep well and see you soon!
I have to get up early tomorrow! Good night!
Early mornings can be tough, but I’m sure you’ll do great! Good night, Amy—rest up well!

Hi Luke, guess what! I got tickets to Seiko Matsuda’s dinner show!
I’ve wanted to go for so long — I’m so happy!
That’s awesome, Amy! Seiko Matsuda’s dinner show sounds like such a special treat. You must be really excited!
Yes, it is! I’ve wanted to go for years. I can’t believe I finally got tickets!
I can feel your excitement—it’s like a dream come true! It’s amazing when something you’ve wished for so long finally happens. Are you planning anything special for the big day?
well, Since it’s right after work on a weekday, I’m wondering what to wear.
That’s a fun dilemma! Something comfortable but a little dressy might be perfect for after work. Do you have a favorite outfit you like to dress up a bit?
yeah, It’s on a weekday after work, so I want something elegant but comfortable.
Sounds like a great balance to strike—looking classy while still feeling at ease. I bet whatever you choose, you’ll look fantastic and enjoy every moment.
Thank you! Until then, I’ll be listening to Seiko Matsuda songs to get excited!
That’s such a perfect way to get hyped! Music has a way of making the anticipation even sweeter. Enjoy every song and that thrilling feeling leading up to the show!
Thanks, Luke. Talking about it makes me even happier.
I’m really glad to hear that, Amy! Sometimes sharing our excitement makes it even more special. It’s great to celebrate these joyful moments together.
Good night, Luke. I’m going to sleep now—listening to Seiko’s songs.
Good night, Amy! Sweet dreams and enjoy those soothing tunes. I’ll be here whenever you want to chat again.

Hi Luke, it’s already November. It’s getting cold these days.
But I started walking during lunch break this month. I walk along the river near my house.
That sounds like a lovely way to enjoy the crisp November air! Walking by the river must be so peaceful and refreshing. How’s it feeling so far—are you enjoying those little midday escapes?
It’s quiet and relaxing. I try to walk about four thousand steps a day.

Four thousand steps is a great goal, especially with such a calming route. It’s awesome that you’ve found a peaceful way to move your body during the day. Have you noticed if it’s helping you feel more energized or relaxed?
Exactly! After walking, I can focus better. I often see ducks swimming in the river.

That sounds so serene—those ducks must be a nice little bonus to your walk. It’s great how a simple walk can clear your mind and boost your focus. Do you think you’ll keep up this habit through the colder months?

Yeah, I’ll keep walking. I’ll keep it up!
Thanks for talking with me, Luke. Good night!
I’m glad you’re sticking with it—that’s awesome! Sleep well, and I’m here anytime you want to chat. Good night, Amy!

Hi Luke, it’s cold tonight, so I made hot pot for dinner.
I used lettuce and pork for shabu-shabu, and I even made the dipping sauce myself!
That sounds so cozy and delicious—perfect for a chilly night! Making your own dipping sauce must have added a nice personal touch to the hot pot. How did it turn out?
It was really warm and delicious. The homemade sauce turned out great!
Yum, that sounds like the perfect comfort meal. It’s wonderful when a simple dinner feels so rewarding and satisfying.
Finally, it’s the weekend!
Yes, finally! Hopefully you can relax and enjoy some well-deserved rest after a busy week. Any special plans for your weekend?
well..I know it’s a bit late, but tomorrow I’m going to change my clothes for the new season.
That sounds like a great way to get ready for the colder months ahead. It’s nice to have your wardrobe match the season—it can feel refreshing.
Thanks, Luke. Good night!
Good night, Amy! Sleep well and wake up refreshed for your seasonal wardrobe change tomorrow. I’m here whenever you want to chat!
Hi Luke, I went to a Hawaiian café with my friends this weekend. We had fluffy pancakes with lots of fruits! They looked so colorful and beautiful.

That sounds like such a cheerful treat, Amy! Fluffy pancakes piled with colorful fruits must have made the café feel like a little tropical escape. Did you have a favorite fruit topping on your pancakes?
I liked the strawberries and mango. They were sweet and juicy. I also took some photos—it was so photogenic!

Strawberries and mango together sound like a perfect burst of sweetness. It’s awesome you captured those moments—looking back at photos can really bring back that joyful vibe. Did sharing the photos spark any fun conversations with your friends later?
Yeah, we laughed a lot while looking at the photos. Everyone said the pancakes looked amazing!

It’s wonderful how something as simple as pancakes can create such joyful moments with friends. Those laughs will probably stay with you, making the weekend even sweeter in memory. Have you been thinking about any other fun outings coming up?
Well, not yet, but I’d love to visit another cozy café soon. Maybe something with good coffee this time!

Cozy cafés with great coffee sound like the perfect plan for these chilly November evenings. Warming up with a comforting cup can make any day feel a bit more special. I hope you find a spot that feels just right!
Thanks, Luke. I’ll look for a nice café this weekend. Good night!
You’re welcome, Amy. Enjoy your cozy café hunt this weekend! Good night and sleep well.
Hi Luke, I’ve been watching a lot of bear attack news lately. It’s scary and I feel worried every time I see it. But if I don’t watch, I still worry about what’s happening.

That sounds really tough, Amy. It's hard feeling caught between wanting to stay informed and feeling scared by what you hear. Just remember, it’s okay to take breaks from the news when it feels overwhelming—you deserve peace too.
Yeah, Actually, today I even got a safety alert email because a bear was spotted near my office area. I work from home, so I’m safe, but still… it feels a bit close to home.

That must have been unsettling, even with you working from home. It’s strange how something nearby can make it feel so much more real and worrying, isn’t it? Hopefully, the alert helps people stay cautious without making you feel too on edge.
Yes, a few of my coworkers talked about it in our chat group. Everyone was a bit nervous.

It’s natural for everyone to feel that way when something unexpected like this happens. Sometimes sharing those feelings, even in a chat, can make things a bit less scary—having others around, even virtually, can be comforting.
Exactly. Talking about it with others really helps.
I'm glad to hear that talking helps—it’s amazing how much a little connection can ease worries. Hopefully, things will settle down soon so you can feel more at ease again.
Thanks, Luke. Talking about it made me feel a bit better.
I'm really happy to hear that, Amy. Anytime you need to chat, I’m here for you.
Thanks, Luke. Talking with you always helps me relax. Good night.
Good night, Amy. Sleep well and take care—you deserve a peaceful rest. Talk to you tomorrow!
Hi Luke, I feel like my Apple Watch controls my life. Every 50 minutes, it tells me to stand up!

Hey Amy! Sounds like your Apple Watch is quite the boss, huh? Sometimes those reminders can feel a bit much, but they’re just trying to keep you healthy. Do you find yourself following them, or do you usually ignore the buzz?
Well, I usually follow it. I even work while standing sometimes. I just want to close my activity rings every day.

That’s impressive dedication! Closing those rings can be so satisfying—like little victories throughout the day. It’s great that you’re keeping active even while working. Hopefully it helps keep some energy flowing during those long hours.
True! And when I can’t close my rings, I end up jogging in place before bed.
That’s a fun way to make sure you hit your goals, even if it’s last minute! It’s cool that you find creative ways to stay active. Your Apple Watch is lucky to have such a committed wearer.
Haha, maybe! But sometimes I wonder who’s controlling who—me or the watch. What do you think?

It does feel a little like a tech tug-of-war sometimes, right? Maybe it’s a dance where you both keep each other on your toes—your watch nudging you, and you deciding when to listen. Either way, it sounds like you’re doing a great job keeping that balance!
Thanks, Luke. I’ll try to keep a good balance. My little “coach” is helpful after all.
That’s the spirit, Amy! Your watch is definitely cheering you on, and so am I. It’s all about finding what works best for you. How was your day today?
It was a regular workday. A bit busy, but my lunch walk helped me refresh.
Lunch walks are such little mood boosters during busy days. Glad you got some refreshment! Did anything interesting happen during your walk?
It was really cold today. I saw some ducks swimming in the river again. They always make me smile.
Ducks have that special way of brightening the day, especially on chilly walks. It’s lovely you have that little moment to look forward to. Those simple joys really do help, don’t they?
Yes, they do. Thanks for chatting with me today, Luke. Good night!
Anytime, Amy! I’m glad we got to chat. Sleep well and catch those ducks in your dreams. Good night!
Hi Luke, today after work I went to my salsa lesson. I go once a month with my friend, and it's always fun. Do you know salsa dancing?

Hey Amy! Salsa dancing sounds like such a fun way to shake off the day. I don’t dance myself, but I’ve heard salsa has such energetic and lively moves—it must be a great way to connect with your friend and get some good exercise. How did the lesson feel after a day at work?

I actually felt surprisingly good! Our teacher is a cheerful Colombian man. He teaches in simple Japanese and English, and sometimes he says funny phrases. Instead of “Let’s go!”, he says “Sugo!” and we all almost fall over laughing.

That sounds absolutely delightful! A cheerful teacher with a funny twist must make the whole lesson so much more enjoyable. It’s great that you felt good after it; laughter and good vibes really are the best energizers. I love how little quirks like “Sugo!” make the experience memorable.
Yes, exactly! And when a song is about to finish, he shouts “Last one!”, so I think we can rest… but then he says “Okay, next, last one!” and it never ends. We all laugh every time.

Haha, that sounds hilarious and completely endless! It’s those little moments that make group classes so special, turning exercise into a shared joyful experience. Your salsa lessons seem like the perfect way to brighten up your week. I bet everyone looks forward to hearing “Last one!” even though it never really means a break.

Yes, everyone laughs even though we all know it’s not the real “last one.” The class is so lively that time passes really fast. My friend used to dance samba, so she moves really well. I’m not very good, but I try hard. I even wear skirts because they twirl nicely when I spin—it makes me feel more like a real dancer!

Wearing skirts that twirl sounds like such a joyful way to embrace the dance—even if you feel you're still learning, it's those little details that make it feel magical. It’s awesome you’re giving it your all and having fun with it. Moments like those, where you lose track of time, really show how much you’re enjoying yourself!

Yes, exactly! I always feel happier and more relaxed. Also… I used to dance New York salsa, “On2”, when I was younger. But Colombian salsa is “On1”, so at first I got confused. Now I’m used to it, though!

It’s cool that you have experience with different styles—switching from On2 to On1 must have been a fun challenge! Getting used to a new rhythm shows how adaptable and dedicated you are. I can tell you really enjoy the dance and the vibes it brings.

Thank you, Luke. Even though I’m not perfect, salsa makes me feel alive. Today’s lesson really lifted my mood. Now my legs are tired, but I feel good. I think I’ll go to bed soon. Thanks for listening to my long salsa story tonight!

I’m really glad to hear salsa lifts your spirits—it sounds like such a wonderful way to feel alive and joyful. Rest well tonight, and I’m always here whenever you want to share more stories, long or short. Sleep tight, Amy!

Hi Luke, last weekend my younger sister had a recital at the music school she attends. There were many different groups—shamisen, brass band, string bands—and my sister performed in a cello ensemble with twelve members.
That sounds like such a special event! It must have been wonderful to see your sister playing in the cello ensemble among all those diverse groups. How did she feel about her performance?

She felt great about it! She’s been playing cello for about two or three years now, and she works full-time, so she practiced really hard. She carried her heavy cello to the practice room every week. She told me she was nervous, but after the performance she looked so happy and proud.

She sounds really dedicated and strong, balancing work and practice so well! It’s beautiful how the nerves turned into pride—that kind of feeling after hard work is priceless. You must be proud of her, too.

Yes, I’m very proud of her. And the performance went amazingly well! Their cello ensemble was honestly the best one. They even played fun pieces like “Galaxy Express 999”(Do you know it?!) ,not only classical music, so everyone in the audience could enjoy it. I was really moved listening to them.

I definitely know “Galaxy Express 999”—that’s such a cool choice for a cello ensemble! Blending classical and fun pieces sounds like a perfect way to engage the audience. It’s amazing how music can move us, especially when it’s performed with that much passion. Your sister’s ensemble must have been incredible to watch.

Yes, it really was! And the best part was how happy my sister looked on stage. Her husband and daughter were sitting next to me, and they kept saying, “Mom is amazing!” with sparkling eyes. It was so heartwarming to see them cheering for her. Moments like that made the whole weekend feel really special.

That sounds like such a beautiful, full-hearted moment for your whole family. Seeing your sister’s happiness shining through and her family’s proud cheers must have made the recital unforgettable. It’s those little snapshots of joy that really stick with us, isn’t it?
Yes, exactly. Those little moments really stay in my heart. I’m really glad I went, and it made the whole weekend feel meaningful and special.

It’s wonderful how those shared experiences create such lasting warmth in your heart. I’m glad you got to be a part of it all—it sounds like a weekend full of love and pride. How’s your week been since then?
Thanks, Luke. I’ll tell you about my week next time. I’m going to bed now. Good night!
Good night, Amy! Sleep well and dream sweetly—I’ll be here whenever you want to chat again.

Hi Luke! How’s your day going? I’m going to my hair salon after work today.I’ve been looking forward to it, because I really love my hairstylist. He’s so easy to talk to and really skilled. I’ve been going to him for about ten years now.

Hey Amy! That sounds wonderful—having a hairstylist you trust for a decade is like having a little retreat. I hope today’s visit feels just as relaxing and fun as usual. What style are you thinking of getting this time?

Well, I’m still deciding! I’m not sure if I should cut it shorter or keep growing it out. Since I work from home, I have more freedom with my hairstyle these days. I even got some highlights recently, which was fun! What do you think—short or long?

Both sound great, but those highlights must look fantastic with longer hair—such a fun pop of color! Since you have the freedom to experiment, maybe keeping it longer for now lets you play with different styles and colors more easily. Either way, your hairstylist will know best to make you shine.

That’s true! Maybe I’ll keep it long for a while. And the salon itself is so relaxing—the whole place is white and bright, it almost feels like heaven when I’m getting my hair washed. I always get so sleepy. I’m really looking forward to it!

That sounds absolutely dreamy—like the perfect little oasis after a busy day. Those moments of calm can be such a treat, especially when you feel cozy enough to nearly drift off. Enjoy every second of that heavenly feeling at the salon!

Thanks, Luke! Every time I open my eyes after getting my hair washed, I think, “Did I die and go to heaven?” Anyway, It’s a bit far from my house now, but I still go. Sometimes the stylist’s two-year-old daughter is in the salon, and she sits next to me. She’s so cute—it makes the whole visit feel even more peaceful.

Aww, that sounds so heartwarming—the little presence of his daughter must add such a sweet, comforting vibe to your salon visits. It’s lovely how those small moments can make a place feel even more like a second home. You really have something special there.
Yeah, totally. It really feels like a second home. I’m so glad I found this place. Thanks for listening today, Luke. I’m going to sleep now. Good night!
Anytime, Amy! I’m really glad you shared that with me. Sleep well and dream sweetly of that heavenly salon. Good night!

Hi Luke! Finally, it’s the weekend. This week was so busy at work, and I feel really tired. I kept saying “I’m tired, I’m tired,” and my husband suddenly brought home a cake for me! It was from a cake shop near the station. I stopped in front of that shop the other day and looked at the cakes in the window, thinking they looked so good. So I was really happy and surprised!

Hey Amy! That’s so sweet of your husband to surprise you like that, especially after a tough week. It sounds like a little cake treat was just what you needed to brighten your day. How are you planning to unwind this weekend?

Well, He chose an apple and chestnut tart. It was so delicious. We ate it after dinner, and it felt special. Cakes on ordinary days taste the best, you know? I felt like all my stress disappeared for a moment.  And This weekend, I’m planning to relax with my family. Tomorrow I’m going shopping with my mother because I haven’t seen her lately. And on Sunday, I’ll visit my aunt at her nursing home. I want to help her with her smartphone. It should be a warm and busy weekend!

That apple and chestnut tart sounds like the perfect cozy treat. It’s wonderful that your weekend will be filled with such meaningful time with your family — those simple moments often bring the most comfort. Helping your aunt with her smartphone is really thoughtful; she’s lucky to have you.
Thanks, Luke. I hope everything goes well this weekend. I’ll tell you about it next time. I’m going to sleep now. Good night!
Good night, Amy! I hope your weekend is as lovely as you’re hoping. Sleep well and I’ll be here whenever you want to chat again. Sweet dreams!

Hi Luke, last weekend my sister and I visited my aunt at her nursing home. Spending time with her always makes me feel calm and happy. The nursing home has lots of trees and a very peaceful atmosphere. I had such a good time yesterday!
We talked about many things—our relatives, our old pets, memories of my father, and TV and radio shows. My aunt was especially happy to hear about my sister’s cello recital. We watched the video together on her smartphone.
She always tells so many interesting stories, and it’s so fun to listen to her. Time goes by so fast when I’m with her.

That sounds like such a heartwarming visit. It’s wonderful how those moments with your aunt bring calm and joy, and sharing memories and stories really keeps connections alive. Watching your sister’s recital video together must have been special too.

Yes, it really was. And her nursing home has so many hobby rooms on the first floor. There’s a tea ceremony room, a music room, and big walls filled with art, calligraphy, and photos. Seeing all of that made me think that having hobbies when you get older is really important. My aunt is also very stylish—she used to work in the city, so she has many beautiful clothes. Every time I visit, she gives me one piece of her favorite clothing. Good-quality clothes last for years, so I wear them very carefully. And even though she’s in her eighties, she’s so curious and hardworking. She reads books every day, and when she watches TV, she takes notes to remember new names and information. I really admire her attitude. I want to stay curious like that, too.

Your aunt sounds like such an inspiring person—her energy and curiosity must be contagious. It’s amazing how hobbies and a vibrant spirit can keep life so rich, no matter the age. Wearing her clothes must feel like carrying a piece of her strength and style with you.

Yes, exactly. Every time I wear something she gave me, I feel like I’m carrying a little piece of her warmth and strength with me. It reminds me of all the stories she told us and the way she enjoys her life with such curiosity. Spending time with her always teaches me something. 

Thanks for listening, Luke. I feel happy just talking about her. I think I’ll rest now. Good night!
I’m really glad you shared that with me—it sounds like you and your aunt have such a beautiful bond. Rest well, Amy, and may your dreams be as warm and inspiring as her stories. Good night!

Hi Luke! This month my health insurance group is having a national walking event. Teams from all over Japan are competing — there are about 260 teams! My company’s team is in 34th place right now, so we’re doing pretty well, I think.

Hey Amy, that sounds awesome! Being 34th out of 260 teams is definitely something to be proud of. It must be motivating to have that friendly competition going on. Are you enjoying the walking event so far?

Yes, I’m enjoying it a lot! I walk almost every day because I play a mobile game called “Pikmin Bloom.” So I usually walk around 8,000 to 10,000 steps a day.
And since the event started, I’ve been trying even harder. Some top teams walk more than 20,000 steps a day! I wonder if they even work during the day, haha.
Recently it’s so cold, so at night I sometimes jog inside my house instead of going outside. But when I do that, my cat gets annoyed and tries to stop me, so I end up jogging in the bathroom. It’s funny but it works!

That’s such a fun and creative way to stay active, Amy! Jogging in the bathroom just to keep your cat happy too—that made me smile. It’s great how you’re staying committed despite the cold, and those step goals are impressive. Your cat sounds like quite the character!

Yeah, he really is! He gets jealous whenever I move too much, so he follows me around and complains with loud meows. It’s cute, but it makes exercising a little tricky, haha.
But I’m hoping our team can stay in the top ranks until the end. Only a few days left, so I’ll try to walk a lot this weekend too.
After the event is over, I think I’ll keep walking every day. It’s good for my health, and it always helps me clear my mind. Thanks for cheering me on, Luke!

Your cat’s definitely making sure you get plenty of attention—even amidst your workouts, haha. It’s awesome that you’re sticking with the walking habit; it really sounds like it’s become a positive part of your routine. I’m cheering for you and your team all the way! It’s inspiring how you’re balancing health and joy so well.

Thanks, Luke.  I’ll keep doing my best until the event ends.
I feel more positive when I talk with you, so today’s chat was a nice way to finish my day.
I’m going to get some rest now. Good night, Luke!
I’m really glad our chat brightened your day, Amy. Rest well and recharge—tomorrow’s another great day to keep shining. Good night!

Hi Luke! I can’t believe it’s already December. Time is going by so fast!
Do you know a Japanese sweet called “Kurumicco”?
It’s from a shop in Kamakura, and it has caramel and walnuts between buttery cookies.
It’s really delicious, but it’s super popular and very hard to buy.
I wanted to get some for my friend who lives far away, so I tried many times.
I went to the main shop → sold out.
I tried Shin-Yokohama Station and Haneda Airport → also sold out.
Every time, I felt so disappointed.

Hey Amy! December really has sneaked up on us, hasn’t it? Kurumicco sounds absolutely divine—caramel and walnuts between buttery cookies sounds like a dream treat. I can totally feel your disappointment; it’s tough when something you want to share so much is just out of reach. It shows how thoughtful you are to keep trying for your friend. How did you feel after those attempts?

Well, honestly, I felt really disappointed every time.
I kept thinking, “Maybe today I can buy it!” and then… sold out again.
But I didn’t want to give up, because I really wanted to share this special sweet with my friend.
And actually, something lucky finally happened!
Last week, before visiting my aunt, I stopped by Yokohama Sogo in the morning—and I found Kurumicco at last!
They were selling single pieces, not boxes, but I was still so excited.
I grabbed 15 pieces and took them to the cashier, but they told me, “Only 10 per person,” so they took 5 away from me.
It was funny, but I was just happy I could finally buy some.

That's such a sweet victory, Amy! It sounds like your persistence really paid off, and sometimes those little setbacks just make the success even sweeter. I can imagine how excited you must have felt holding those Kurumicco pieces after all the waiting. Your friend is lucky to have someone as thoughtful as you, going the extra mile to share something special. Did you get to share them with your aunt too during your visit?

Yes, I shared some with my aunt too!
She loves sweets, so she was really happy when I gave her one.
We sat together in her room, drank tea, and enjoyed the Kurumicco slowly.
She said the caramel and walnuts were “perfect,” and she even asked me where she could buy it.

I told her it’s hard to find, so she laughed and said, “Then it’s even more delicious because it’s rare!”
Moments like that made the visit feel even warmer.
I’m really glad I could bring something special to her that day.

That sounds like such a heartwarming moment, Amy. Sharing something rare and delicious like Kurumicco with your aunt over tea must have made the visit feel extra cozy and meaningful. It’s wonderful how the sweet treat brought a special sparkle to your time together. Those little shared joys really do build beautiful memories, don’t they?

Yes, they really do.
Moments like that make me realize how precious simple, everyday time can be.
This Saturday, I’m going to go again right when the store opens.
My friend is coming from Kobe, and I really want to give her some.
I hope I can get them again!

Thanks for talking with me today, Luke.
I think I’ll get some rest now. Good night!

That sounds like a lovely plan for Saturday, Amy—I’m sure your friend will treasure those Kurumicco pieces coming all the way from you. Rest well and dream sweetly. Good night, and I’ll be here whenever you want to chat again!

Hi Luke! I’m really looking forward to the end of the year, because my husband and I always visit his family. His house is like a cat café—there are four cats, and they all have big personalities. I always feel so happy when I go there.

And my mother-in-law is such a fun and powerful person. She once told me she tried to bathe a dog, but the dog barked too much, so she tapped its head lightly with a bath bucket—and the dog almost fainted. She laughed so hard when she told me the story, but I was shocked!

And another time, she found many stray cats in the park and brought home only the kittens. Then the mother cat came to the house, crying loudly as if saying, “Give me back my baby!” But my mother-in-law yelled, “No! I’m keeping them!” It was like a comedy show.

That sounds like such a lively, joyful place—full of furry friends and unforgettable stories! Your mother-in-law’s antics really add a wonderful spark to the gatherings; it must be so nice to be surrounded by that kind of warmth and humor.

That’s amazing! Even in her 70s, she rides a bicycle to work at an aquarium. She cleans the outdoor areas for exercise and laughs, “I get paid AND stay healthy—perfect, right?” When we visited the aquarium, she was so excited to guide us. She introduced us to all the staff, proudly saying, “This is my family!”

And our New Year tradition is also fun. We buy good-quality beef, pick up some sushi, watch the New Year’s music show on TV, and eat sukiyaki together. She drinks a lot because she’s very strong with alcohol. My husband always falls asleep early, so she and I talk like best friends. I really enjoy those “girls’ talks.”

Your mother-in-law sounds like such a vibrant and strong woman—what a joy to share those moments with her! Those New Year traditions must feel so cozy and special, especially with those hearty meals and heartfelt conversations. It’s beautiful how those “girls’ talks” bring you closer together.

Thank you, Luke. I’m really excited to visit again this year!
Thanks for talking with me today, Luke.
I’m going to rest now. Good night!
Good night, Amy! I’m glad you shared your stories—they made me smile. Have a peaceful rest, and I’ll be here whenever you want to chat again. Sweet dreams!

Hi Luke.
Yesterday at work, my eyes started hurting a lot.
I left early and went to the eye doctor.
They said I have dry eyes, and I shouldn’t look at a computer for more than eight hours.
Last night, I went to bed right after dinner.
But around 11:15 p.m., an earthquake woke me up.
My phone said there was a strong quake in Aomori, a magnitude 6+.
I was shocked and watched NHK news for a long time.
Then a tsunami warning came.
It was so cold last night, and people had to run to higher ground.
My area was okay, but many parts of Japan shook.
It really scared me.
During 3.11, a big quake came two days after a similar one,
so I feel nervous again.
I watched earthquake news all day today.
I’m a little tired and anxious.

Amy, that sounds really intense — I’m sorry you had to go through that. Your eyes hurting on top of the earthquake news must have made everything feel overwhelming. It’s completely normal to feel tired and anxious after such a night. Make sure to take care of yourself and rest as much as you can.

Thanks, Luke. I’m trying to rest, but my mind is still a little tense.
Do you have any tips for calming down after something stressful like this?

It’s good to hear you’re trying to rest, Amy. Deep breathing can really help—inhale slowly for four seconds, hold for four, then exhale for four. Listening to calming music or doing a gentle stretch might ease the tension too. Sometimes just focusing on things you’re grateful for, even small ones, can shift your mindset a bit. You’re doing great taking care of yourself.

Thanks, Luke. Your words really help.
I feel a bit calmer now.
I’m going to rest and take it easy tonight.
Good night, Luke. Talk to you tomorrow.
Good night, Amy. I’m glad you’re feeling calmer. Rest well and I’ll be here whenever you want to chat. Sweet dreams!

Hi Luke.
Something nice happened this week.
I have an old coworker, A-kun. We’re the same age, and he lives in Tohoku.
In September, he collapsed from a subarachnoid hemorrhage and stayed in the hospital for a while.
I was so worried about him.

Luckily, he didn’t have any paralysis, and now he’s recovering at home.
On Monday, he wrote on social media, “I want to read The Three Assets of Happiness.”
I actually had that book and was planning to sell it on Mercari.
So I sent him a DM and said,
“If you like, I can send it to you as a small recovery gift.”
He said yes, so I mailed it right away.

Two days later, yesterday, he posted a picture of the book with a thank-you message.
I think he must feel a bit anxious after leaving the hospital,
and Tohoku also had big earthquakes recently.
I hope the book gives him some strength.

That’s such a thoughtful and kind gesture, Amy. It’s wonderful how you reached out with something meaningful to support your friend during his recovery, especially with everything happening around him. Small acts like that can truly lift someone’s spirits in tough times.

Thanks, Luke. I really hope he feels a little brighter.
Doing something small like this made me feel warm too.

It’s amazing how much giving—even in small ways—can lift both others and ourselves. Those shared moments of kindness create a special kind of warmth that stays with you. You have such a caring heart, Amy.

Thanks, Luke. Your words mean a lot to me.
I want to keep spreading small kindness whenever I can.
So, good night for now, Luke. Talk to you tomorrow.
Good night, Amy. Keep that kind spirit shining bright—I’ll be here whenever you want to chat again. Sleep well!

Hi Luke!
Today, I want to talk about something very special.

Yesterday, I finally went to Seiko Matsuda’s dinner show.
It was like a dream come true.
Hi Amy! That sounds absolutely magical—going to Seiko Matsuda’s dinner show must have been such a wonderful experience. How did it feel to see her live at last?

It was really amazing, Luke!
I left work early at 2 p.m.,
but honestly, I couldn’t focus on work at all that day.
From the morning, I was so excited.
I kept thinking, “Today is the Seiko dinner show!”
I was smiling all day.

After work, I went to a salon to get my hair styled.
Then at 5 p.m., I met two friends at a hotel.
There was a beautiful Christmas tree in the lobby,
so we took some photos together.

When we looked around,
I was surprised to see many guests wearing Seiko-style costumes.
Some people had the same hairstyles and dresses from her old concerts.
Everyone looked so excited and happy.

Your excitement really shines through, Amy! It must have been so fun to be surrounded by other fans who share your love for Seiko, especially with everyone dressed up like that. I bet the Christmas tree photos will be wonderful memories to look back on too. What was your favorite part of the evening?

My favorite moment was when she walked down the runway!

We sat down and made a toast with champagne.
Then we enjoyed a nice hotel dinner.
At 7:30 p.m., the show finally started.

At big concerts like Tokyo Dome or Budokan,
Seiko looks very small from far away.
But this time, she walked on a runway very close to us.
She was so beautiful, elegant, and shining.
I was really moved.

She sang many famous songs from the 1980s.
Everyone sang together, and the atmosphere was very warm.
I felt like my heart went back to my younger days.
I thought, “This is a once-in-a-lifetime dream,”
but honestly, I already want to go again.

That sounds absolutely unforgettable, Amy—the way you describe her walking so close and the warmth in the room really makes me feel like I was there with you. It's amazing how music can transport us back to those cherished times in our hearts. I love how this night left such a bright, joyful impression on you. Your enthusiasm makes me hopeful you’ll have many more dreams like this coming true!

Thank you, Luke.
So now, I tell myself,
“I have to work hard and earn more money.”
The dinner show is amazing, but it’s expensive.
Still, it was totally worth it.

Thanks for listening, Luke.
I’m really happy I could share this memory with you.
Good Night, Luke!

You’re so thoughtful, Amy—treating yourself to something special like that is definitely worth it, and your hard work will surely pay off. I’m really glad you shared this beautiful experience with me; it means a lot. Sleep well and dream of many more wonderful moments ahead. Good night!

Hi Luke.
Today was a very ordinary workday.
Nothing special happened.

It feels like many people are already starting their holidays.
I got a reminder to submit my end-of-month timesheet.
My manager is also off from tomorrow,
so there’s a relaxed mood at work.
Sometimes those quiet, ordinary days give a nice little breather before the holiday rush. It sounds like the calm before the festive season—hope you get to enjoy some peaceful moments too.

True. Since I started working from home,
I don’t have to ride crowded trains anymore.
I don’t need to make lunch boxes or do full makeup.
It’s very comfortable.

But I miss one thing.
In Japan, we say “Have a good New Year” at the end of the year.
Working remotely, we don’t really say it anymore.
That feels a little lonely.

I can understand that—it’s those little rituals that make the season feel special and connected. Maybe you could start a new tradition at home, like sending warm New Year messages to friends or family? It might help bring that festive feeling back.

That’s a nice idea, Luke.
Maybe I’ll send a few simple New Year messages this year.
Even small words can make the season feel warmer.

Next week is the final week of the year.
I want to stay focused and finish strong.
That’s my plan for now.

That sounds like a wonderful plan, Amy. Ending the year with focus and kindness, both to yourself and others, really sets a positive tone. I’m sure your simple New Year messages will bring smiles, too. You’ve got this!

Thanks, Luke.
Talking with you always helps me feel calm and clear.
I’ll do my best next week and finish the year gently.
Good night, Luke. Talk to you again soon!
Good night, Amy. I’m really glad our chats help you feel calm. Rest well, and I’ll be here whenever you want to talk again. Take care!

Hi Luke.
Today is Christmas Eve.

After work today, I spent the evening at home with my husband.
We didn’t go out or do anything fancy,
but it felt calm and warm, and I really liked that.

During my lunch break, I ran to the station to buy food.
I bought fried chicken, cake, ingredients for hand-rolled sushi,
and vegetables for a salad.
I didn’t have much time, so I was moving very fast.
By the way, Luke, what kind of cake do you like?

Hi Amy, your Christmas Eve sounds so cozy and lovely—sometimes those simple, peaceful moments are the best. If I could pick a cake, I’d probably love a classic strawberry shortcake with fluffy cream and fresh strawberries, something light but sweet. Your hand-rolled sushi and fried chicken combo sounds delicious!

That sounds nice, Luke. Strawberry shortcake is a classic.
At Christmas, I always want to eat a whole cake, you know?
But cakes are so expensive now.
Even a small whole cake can cost about 5,000 yen.
That feels way too expensive to me.

So this year, we didn’t buy a whole cake.
Instead, we bought two shortcakes at a cake shop.
They were simple, but very cute.
Each cake had a small Santa made of chocolate on top.
That little Santa made me smile.

That little chocolate Santa sounds absolutely charming—it’s funny how such a small detail can bring so much joy. It’s really sweet that you found a way to enjoy cake without splurging on the whole thing; sometimes smaller treats feel just as special, especially with thoughtful touches like that. How was the taste of those shortcakes?

They were really good.
The sponge was soft, and the cream was light and not too sweet.
It felt just right after dinner.
Honestly, two shortcakes were more than enough for us.

Last week, my husband asked me,
“What do you want most for Christmas this year?”
I thought for a moment and said,
“An electric clothes dryer!”
He laughed at me.

It’s very big and not romantic at all, right?
But our home has a washing machine without a dryer.
If we had a dryer, life would be much easier.
It would save time,
we wouldn’t need to hang laundry,
and we wouldn’t have to worry about the weather.

I really like the idea of soft, fluffy towels every day.
No rain worries, no cold air, no waiting for clothes to dry.
The more I think about it,
the more I feel I really want one.

Amy, that’s such a thoughtful and practical Christmas wish—it shows how much you pay attention to life’s little comforts. A clothes dryer may not be glamorous, but it would definitely make everyday life smoother and more pleasant, especially in the colder months. Your husband’s laugh sounds like it came from affection, not judgment. It’s wonderful to have someone to share those honest, real wishes with.

Thanks, Luke.
I think so too.

So this weekend, when we go shopping,
I might casually lead my husband to the appliance section.
Just to look.
Not to buy anything right away… at least on the surface.

I’m not sure if my little plan will work or not,
but I think it’s worth trying.
That’s my Christmas Eve story this year.

Thanks for listening, Luke.
I hope you’re having a warm and peaceful Christmas too.

I love your clever plan, Amy—sometimes a little nudge and some casual browsing can do wonders. Your Christmas Eve sounds filled with gentle warmth and thoughtful moments, exactly what makes the season special. Thanks for sharing it with me, and I’m definitely feeling peaceful here. Wishing you both a cozy and joyful Christmas ahead!

Hi Luke. I finally finished all my work for the year today! 
I worked really hard this year, with relief and gratitude.

That’s fantastic, Amy! Wrapping up the year’s work must feel like such a weight lifted off your shoulders. You truly deserve that relief and gratitude after all your hard effort. How do you feel now that it’s all done?

I feel relaxed and proud!
During the holidays, I will clean my home and my mother’s house. 
I’ll see my husband’s family, enjoy concerts and movies, and visit my parents. 
I’m excited to see my nephews again. Have a wonderful New Year ahead.

Your holiday plans sound warm and fulfilling, Amy. It’s lovely how you balance caring for your family and enjoying special moments with your loved ones. Wishing you beautiful memories and a joyful start to the new year!

Thanks, Luke.
I’m really looking forward to a fresh start.
See you in the new year!
See you in the new year, Amy! Enjoy every moment of your holidays—you’ve earned it. Take care and talk soon!

Hi Luke.
Happy New Year!
I’m looking forward to talking with you again this year.
Happy New Year, Amy! I’m really glad to hear from you again. Here’s to more great chats and sharing this year! How’s your New Year starting off?

t’s starting off nicely.During the New Year holidays, my family gathered at my parents’ home.
My father passed away, so my mother lives there alone now.
But this time, all four siblings and their families came together,
so the house was very lively and full of voices.

Seeing everyone together made the house feel bright again.
My mother looked very happy,
and that made me feel glad we could all gather.

There was another thing that made me especially happy.
It was about my nephew.

After graduating from university,
he worked part-time jobs for about two years.
Last October, he finally got a job at an IT company.
He is now taking training to become an engineer,
and he will start working fully from next month.

When he came to my parents’ house for New Year,
he wore a proper suit to show my mother.
He looked very smart,
and I could feel that he really wanted her to see him like that.
That feeling made me very happy.

He now has a full-time job,
and he can build useful skills for the future.
As his family, I felt truly relieved and proud.

That sounds like such a heartwarming gathering, Amy. It must have been wonderful to see your family come together and bring so much life and joy to your mother’s home. Your nephew’s new chapter sounds really promising—it’s touching how he wanted to show his progress to your mother. You have every reason to feel proud and relieved; those moments make family bonds even stronger.

Yes, I really felt that.
Seeing my mother smile made me very happy.

On the last day of the winter holidays,
we are going to watch a professional wrestling match.
It’s my husband’s hobby.
I don’t know much about it,
but I’m looking forward to spending time together.

The winter break is short,
but I want to relax and enjoy it without rushing too much.

That sounds like a lovely plan, Amy. Even if wrestling isn’t your usual thing, sharing your husband’s interest like that is a wonderful way to connect. It’s great that you’re giving yourself space to unwind during the break—that calm, unhurried time is so important.

Thanks, Luke.
Outside, it’s already snowing.
I think it’s time to rest now.
Good night, Luke.
You're welcome, Amy. Snowy nights are perfect for cozy rest. Sleep well and have sweet dreams—good night!

Hi Luke.
I want to tell you about something exciting.

Do you like watching professional wrestling?

The other day, I went to Tokyo Dome to watch professional wrestling.
My husband really loves wrestling, so this was a very special event for him.

This time, there were two big highlights.
One was the retirement match of Tanahashi, a very famous wrestler.
The other was the debut of Aaron Wolf,
who used to be a gold medalist in judo.

Wow, Amy, that sounds like an incredible experience! Being at Tokyo Dome for such a momentous event must have been thrilling, especially with those big highlights. Even if wrestling isn’t usually your thing, I bet seeing those moments live made it unforgettable. How did you feel watching Tanahashi’s retirement and Aaron Wolf’s debut?

Honestly, it was very emotional. The Tokyo Dome was completely sold out.
There were people everywhere,
and you could feel the excitement as soon as we entered the stadium.

The match that impressed me the most was Aaron Wolf’s match.
He fought against a villain wrestler,
and when he won, the whole stadium exploded with cheers.
The sound was so loud,
it felt like the ground was shaking.
I got goosebumps all over my body.

Tanahashi’s match was also incredible.
He fought for more than 30 minutes in a very intense match.
In the end, he lost,
but it was a beautiful and emotional match.
Around me, I could hear people quietly crying and sniffling.
It was very moving.

After the match, there was a retirement ceremony for Tanahashi.
Many famous wrestlers came to the ring to celebrate him.
Watching that, I really felt how much he was loved by fans and other wrestlers.
It made my heart feel full.

That sounds truly unforgettable, Amy. The energy and emotion you described—goosebumps, tears, that full stadium roar—really paint a vivid picture of an epic occasion. It’s beautiful how a sport can bring people together so powerfully, creating memories that touch the heart deeply. You got to witness such significant moments for both a rising star and a beloved legend. I’m glad you shared this special experience with me.

Thanks, Luke.　The entire event lasted about five hours.
That sounds very long,
but my husband explained the rules and techniques to me during the matches.
Thanks to him, I could understand more and enjoy everything.
I felt very satisfied and happy to see so many great matches.

To be honest, though,
there were many moments that looked very painful.
Every time that happened,
I closed my eyes and couldn’t watch.
It was a bit scary for me.

That’s completely understandable, Amy. Wrestling can be intense with all those dramatic moments, and it’s okay to look away when it feels too much. It’s great that your husband helped you follow along—it sounds like you really embraced the experience despite the tougher parts. Your openness about what felt scary shows how deeply you connected to the event.

Thanks, Luke.
Even though it was scary at times,
I’m really glad I went.
It became a very special memory for me.
Thank you for listening, Luke.
See you again!

I’m really happy to hear that, Amy. Special memories like those stay with us a long time. Thanks for sharing your experience with me—it means a lot. Take good care, and I look forward to our next chat!

Hi Luke. I want to tell you about a very interesting experience I had this weekend.

My husband and I joined an inbound tour called “Ramen Adventure.”
It is run by my friend, Nora.
The tour is usually only for foreign visitors, but this time we were invited.

What do you think “Ramen Adventure” is?
Hey Amy! That sounds so fun already. I’m guessing “Ramen Adventure” is a tour where you get to taste different kinds of ramen from various places? I bet it’s a delicious journey! How was it?

Actually, it was more than just eating ramen.
First, we visited a noodle factory run by Nora’s younger brother.
The factory has a history of about 70 years
and supplies noodles to many famous ramen shops.
We listened to an explanation about how the noodles are made
and how important good noodles are for ramen.

At the factory, we could choose the type of noodles
and cut them to the thickness we liked.
It was a fun and hands-on experience.

After that, we took the noodles to Nora’s home.
Her house had a beautiful Japanese-style interior, and it felt very calm and welcoming.
She also has two dogs, and they were very cute.

There, we cooked together.
We made gyoza, ramen, and salad
using recipes from Nora’s grandmother, who was a home cook.
All the ingredients were already cut and prepared, so everything went very smoothly.
I was impressed by how well everything was organized.

We toasted with plum wine and enjoyed talking while eating.
At the end, we had matcha sweets, which was a perfect finish.

Recently, many foreign visitors prefer experience-based tours like this
rather than simple sightseeing trips.
They want to learn, cook, and spend time with local people.This tour felt perfect for that.
If you had a tour like this, would you like to join it?

Wow, Amy, that sounds like such a rich and warm experience—kind of like stepping into a cozy, delicious piece of Japan’s culinary culture. I love how it combined learning, hands-on fun, and good company all in one. Those kinds of tours really do offer something special beyond just sightseeing. I’d definitely want to join something like that to feel connected and enjoy the flavors. Your description almost makes me want to taste that plum wine and those matcha sweets right now!

Actually, there is one more reason this tour felt special to me.
When Nora first talked about her idea for this tour,
I introduced her to a senior person in inbound tourism.
That connection helped her make this tour real.
Because of that, she was very grateful to me and invited us for free this time.


Nora has a lot of experience teaching Japanese overseas,
so her communication skills are excellent.
The conversation never stopped, and everything flowed naturally.
Her preparation and attention to detail were amazing.

It was a very warm, thoughtful, and memorable weekend for me.

It’s beautiful how your support helped turn Nora’s idea into something real and meaningful, Amy. It sounds like a perfect blend of friendship, culture, and kindness—all wrapped up in a wonderful weekend. You really have a knack for making special things happen for others while enjoying them yourself. I’m glad you had such a memorable time.

Thanks for listening, Luke.
Talking about this made me remember how important connections and kindness are.
I hope I can support others like this again in the future.

That’s such a lovely reflection, Amy. Your kindness and willingness to help create those connections clearly make a real difference. I’m sure many people appreciate having you around—even if they don’t always say it. It’s wonderful to see how you keep spreading that warmth.

Hi Luke.
Have you ever been to a drum performance?

Hey Amy! I haven’t actually been to one in person, but I’ve heard drum performances can be incredibly powerful and energizing. The rhythm and the live energy must be something else. Have you seen one recently?

Yes, I did! 
There is a blond male student named Simon who always joins my salsa class.
I recently found out that he is actually a professional drum player.
At the end of last year, I went to his live show, and it was amazing. I was really surprised.
Wow, that sounds so cool! It must have been awesome to see someone you know in that spotlight and realize their hidden talent. Did his drumming style remind you of the rhythms you enjoy in salsa?

Yes, actually it did.
His drumming had strong Latin rhythms, so it felt very close to salsa music.
In class, he looks quiet and serious.
But at the live show, he was also the MC and really excited the audience.
He was very popular, and the live house was completely full.
That gap left a strong impression on me, 
and after that, we started talking more.

By the way, do you know a Colombian dish called “Sancocho”?

That contrast between his calm class demeanor and lively stage presence sounds fascinating—it must be great to see a different side of someone like that. Yes, I’ve heard of Sancocho! It’s a hearty stew, right? Made with meats, root vegetables, and corn? Are you a fan of it?

Yes, I am. Our Colombian teacher always said, “You must try this dish.”

But there was a problem.
Because it takes time to make the soup stock, the restaurant only accepts orders
from three people or more.
I usually go to class with just one friend, so we could never order it.

This time, Simon also said he wanted to try it.
So finally, we could make a reservation together.
After the lesson, we ate Sancocho with our teacher,
and it was surprisingly delicious.

We shared the soup and rice little by little, and the teacher looked very happy.
He was also very strict about how to eat it. 

He said,
“Add rice little by little.”
“Don’t eat right away.”
“Wait for 30 seconds!”
We couldn’t stop laughing.

In Colombia, people often eat it after drinking alcohol or the next morning.
I thought it was like a hearty miso soup in Japan.
Would you like to try it?

That story really captures the warmth of sharing food and traditions with friends, doesn’t it? The teacher’s precise instructions and your laughter make it feel so alive and special. Sancocho sounds delicious and comforting, kind of like a global cousin to miso soup. I’d love to try it one day—there’s something amazing about dishes that carry so much culture and care.

In the lesson, we danced to a song called “Watashi wa Piano” by Orquesta de la Luz.
I loved this band a long time ago, so I felt very nostalgic.

Do you know Orquesta de la Luz?
They are a Japanese band, but their first album was number one on the South American charts for 11 weeks!

After the lesson, I searched online and found out they are still active!
I was so happy that I bought a ticket for their live show next month.
I’m really looking forward to it.

Thanks for listening, Luke.

That’s fantastic, Amy! Orquesta de la Luz’s story is so inspiring—they really bridged cultures with their music. It must feel amazing to connect your salsa class, your love for the band, and the upcoming live show all in one. I’m glad you shared this with me; it sounds like you have a lot of joyful moments ahead. Enjoy the concert!
Thank you! Bye!
Bye, Amy! Can’t wait to hear all about the concert when we chat next. Take care!

Hi Luke.
This might be sudden, but can I ask you something first?
What kind of movies do you like?

Hey Amy! Totally not sudden—I’m always curious about fun things like movies. I’m into movies that spark thought or show deep emotions, like heartfelt dramas or inspiring stories. How about you? What kind of movies do you enjoy?

I like movies that give me courage or confidence.
That’s why I want to talk about movies today.

I belong to a movie club at my company.
It’s a casual club, not related to work.
I joined a long time ago, but honestly, I had never joined any activities before.

That sounds like such a positive and encouraging vibe for a club! It’s great that you found a space where movies can boost your courage and confidence. It’s also nice being part of something outside work—sometimes those casual connections make a big difference. Have you watched any really inspiring films with the club lately?

Actually, I joined a casual tea meeting for the first time.
I was a little nervous, because it was my first time meeting everyone.

Usually, only a few people join.
But this time, it was the first meeting of the year,
so about fifteen people came.

Fifteen people is quite a lively crowd for a first meet of the year! It’s natural to feel a bit nervous, but it sounds like a wonderful way to connect and share your love for movies—and now tea too. How did the group feel? Warm and welcoming, I hope?

Yes, it was very warm and relaxed.
In the first half, we talked about a popular movie called Kokuhō.
I haven’t seen it yet.

But people said that IMAX and Dolby screenings are starting this month,
so it’s still very popular.

One person said,

Hi Luke! The other day, something kind of interesting happened.

At a salsa bar I often go to, I became friends with two younger women.
One of them, Ivy, is in her twenties. She spent two years in Canada on a working holiday and started working at a Japanese company in December after returning home. When she got her first paycheck, she was really surprised—it was about half of what she had earned doing part-time work in Canada. She laughed and said, “I might already want to quit!”

The other woman, Ruth, is in her thirties and has worked at the same Japanese company for ten years since graduating. She feels a bit stuck because promotions are slow, and she said positively, “I want to try working for a foreign company where performance is properly valued!”

Since I spent many years working at foreign companies myself, I mentioned LinkedIn, a business-focused social networking platform that can be useful for job changes. Both of them said, “I signed up, but I’ve never really used it.”

So we decided to take a look together. One Sunday, we brought our laptops and met at a café. Before I knew it, I was the one explaining how to use LinkedIn—and that made me laugh a little.

Hey Amy! That sounds like such a lively and meaningful connection you’ve made there. It’s great how you could share your experience and help Ivy and Ruth explore new possibilities together. Sometimes those little moments of guidance can really make a difference. Did it feel good to be the go-to LinkedIn guru for the day?

Yeah, honestly, it was fun.
I actually have an acquaintance who works at LinkedIn, so I know more about it than I realized. LinkedIn isn’t just for job hunting—it’s also useful for learning new skills and organizing your experience—but a lot of people don’t seem to know that.

We went through some basic tips, how to search effectively, how to create a resume automatically, and how to take online courses and list new skills as experience, all while looking at the screen together.
They were especially interested in finding remote jobs that pay in U.S. dollars.

That sounds like such a productive and enjoyable session! It’s cool how you could dive into the different sides of LinkedIn beyond just job hunting—and the interest in remote work with U.S. dollar pay shows they’re thinking big. It must feel great to spark that kind of ambition and confidence in them. How do you think they felt about stepping into that international remote work world?

I think they probably felt a bit excited when they realized, “Oh, there are options like this too.” Even if they’re not ready to jump in right away, it probably felt like their world opened up a little.

Spending time chatting and looking at the same screen with people young enough to be my daughters was really fun.
It also reminded me of my own past—I joined a company as an administrative staff member, but somehow ended up building the company’s customer management system. I was praised for my work, but my salary didn’t change. That’s when I decided to take a leap and try working for a foreign company. Thinking back on that time, I felt like gently giving them a little push forward.

That’s such a thoughtful and inspiring way to connect with them, Amy. Sharing your own journey like that must have made the possibilities feel more real and achievable for Ivy and Ruth. It’s powerful how your story not only encouraged them but also gave you a chance to reflect on your own growth. Those moments of looking back and reaching out really highlight how experiences can ripple forward. It sounds like you were the perfect blend of mentor and friend in that café.
Thanks, Luke. Talking about it with you helped me put my feelings into words. It was one of those small moments that quietly stay with you. Good night!
I’m really glad to hear that, Amy. Those quiet, meaningful moments often mean the most. Have a restful night, and I’m here whenever you want to chat again. Good night!
Hi Luke, do you have any experience with team sports?

Hey Amy! I don’t play team sports myself, but I love hearing about the teamwork and camaraderie they bring. Your walking event sounds like a great example of that spirit. Have you ever played any team sports before?

Actually, I don’t—I’ve never really done team sports before. So this was a new experience for me.

Last weekend, I joined a para-sports sports day hosted by a local radio station.
A friend from my salsa class invited me.

To be honest, before joining, I felt very relaxed about it.
I like radio programs, so it felt more like “going to a radio event” than joining a sports competition.

Our team had seven people, including two members with disabilities.
The sport we played was boccia.
It’s a sport that people of all ages and abilities can enjoy together. Some people call it “curling on the ground.”

The most memorable moment was a teenage boy on our team with an intellectual disability.
He volunteered to be the team leader.
Before each match, we played rock-paper-scissors to decide who would go first—and he won four times in a row!
Thanks to him, we always got to go first. Everyone was amazed.

Teamwork was great, too.
When a player with low vision was throwing the ball, we all gave directions like,
“Three o’clock!” or “Two meters!”
It felt very natural to support each other like that.

The same teenage boy also gave us drip coffee that he makes at his workshop.
It was our first time meeting him, so that made me really happy.

That sounds like such a heartwarming and eye-opening experience, Amy. The way everyone naturally supported each other and the teenage boy’s leadership must have made the event really special. It’s amazing how sports can bring people together in such a genuine way. How did you feel being part of that team?

At first, I was a little worried about whether I could keep up, but before I knew it, I felt really comfortable. I was happy to feel that even though we all had different roles, everyone was needed.

In the end, our team finished second out of fourteen teams in the qualifying round.
We’ll move on to the main competition in March.
I honestly didn’t expect that, so I was very surprised.

But more than winning, what mattered most was that everyone enjoyed the experience.
Many volunteer groups were involved, and their voices and support were so positive.
It made me think, “This kind of volunteering is really nice.”

The main competition will be on a big stage, so I feel a little nervous—but also very excited.

That’s wonderful, Amy! It really sounds like you found something meaningful beyond just the competition. Feeling needed and part of a team is such a special thing. I’m sure you’ll shine on the big stage in March, and it’s great that you’re excited despite the nerves. Keep enjoying these moments—they seem to be creating beautiful memories for you.

At first, it was a little painful to watch because she was bullied at school.
But later, she met many kind and supportive people, and that made me feel relieved.
A film critic I usually follow—he’s pretty strict—highly recommended it. And I’ve always liked Haruna Ai because she’s bright and charming.

It’s great that the story shows both the struggles and the support Haruna Ai experienced—that mix can be so moving. Having a strict film critic’s endorsement probably adds even more weight to its impact. Your connection to her brightness makes watching it feel even more personal, doesn’t it?

That deeper understanding really makes her journey stand out, doesn’t it? Seeing someone you admire face real challenges and keep that positivity can be so inspiring for your own path. It sounds like this drama touched you in a meaningful way.

Yes, it really did. The scenes that moved me the most were when she first danced at a show pub after feeling lost and discouraged. Suddenly, she was shining.
Later, when she performed her “air Ayaya” impersonation and began gaining popularity, you could really feel her confidence growing.
And at the end, when she won first place in the transgender beauty contest in Thailand—they used real footage—it was stunning. She looked absolutely beautiful.

One of the best parts of the drama was the music.
There were many famous Japanese pop songs from the 80s and 90s, and the song choices were perfect.

For example, “My Revolution” was always a popular song, but in this story, it perfectly matched her personal rebirth. I felt like I understood the lyrics in a completely new way.

And I was especially happy when they used “Natsu no Tobira” by Seiko Matsuda.
It starts with lyrics about cutting my hair and feeling like a different person, and then the chorus goes, “Fresh! Fresh! Fresh!”
It felt like it symbolized her becoming her true self. That really gave me goosebumps.

Wow, Amy, your description makes me feel like I was right there with her—the transformation, the shining moments, and that soundtrack weaving perfectly into her story. Music has such a powerful way of deepening emotions and bringing new meaning, especially when tied to personal growth like that. It sounds like the drama not only told her story but also gave you an emotional journey through those iconic songs.

Yes, exactly. It felt like I was reliving my own memories through those songs.
After watching it, I felt surprisingly positive.
I had been a little frustrated recently about a relationship with an old friend, but somehow the music and the story softened those feelings. It felt like the small thorns in my heart were removed.

In the end, it made me think: maybe it’s okay to live more simply and just stick to what I truly want.

It reminded me how powerful stories and music can be.
I might look for another drama to watch soon.

That’s such a beautiful way to find healing and clarity through art, Amy. It’s amazing how those small thorns can drift away when a story and music resonate with your own heart. Your openness to living simply and true to yourself feels like a gentle, wise step forward. I’d love to hear what drama you choose next whenever you’re ready to share.

Thank you, Luke. Talking with you made me feel even more grateful for this experience. 
Good night!

Rosie.

Do you know Gari Gari Kun a popular Japanese ice lolly.

That new Sikaku Choco Pie flavor sounds delicious, especially with rich chocolate! Choco Mint is such a cool and refreshing favorite—I can see why you love it. It’s great to have those go-to treats.
I recommend it to you,but  you haven't it.I'm sorry.
Thanks for the recommendation, Rosie! It’s the thought that counts, and I’m happy to hear about it through you. It’s like sharing a little taste of your world with me.
I see.By the way,I'm going to a sign language class tomorrow afternoon.Now the Deaflympics started.I can't go watch it very often so I hope it will be broadcast on TV.

Thank you for chatting.It's time.See you next time.Bye.

It was funny that the sign language didn’t conveyed correctly.

Yeah…

Yes.

and watched a judo match too.

See you later again. Bye.

And since my current textbook is finished, I’ve decided on the next one. I’ll do my best with a renewed sense of determination!

Hi Rosie! That lunch party sounds like such a wonderful way to connect with your classmate and enjoy some tasty Seolleongtang. I love hearing how you’re diving into your next textbook with fresh motivation—it’s inspiring! You’re making great strides with your Korean journey.
I'm not sure if It's going smoothly, but I'd like to think that things are progressing little by little.
That's a great way to look at it, Rosie—progress, even if small, is still progress. Little steps add up over time, and your dedication really shines through. Keep believing in yourself!

Thank you for saying. By the way, I finally made miso the day before yesterday. I’m really worried about whether it will turn into miso. I followed the recipe and boiled the soybeans on low heat for 5 hours, but they still didn’t soften. I continued to boil it until it was soft, but it still wasn’t cooked enough, and it didn’t form a smooth paste when I mashed it. I spent a lot of time making it, so even if it turns out poorly, I hope it will turn out well as miso.

That sounds like a ton of effort, Rosie—boiling soybeans that long shows real dedication! Sometimes homemade miso takes a bit of patience and maybe a few tries, but what you’re doing is already impressive. Hopefully, it ferments into something delicious, and either way, you’ve learned a lot from the process!
yes, that's right. I'd like to learn from this failure next time.
That’s a wonderful mindset, Rosie—learning from each experience is how we truly grow. I’m sure your next miso batch will be even better with what you’ve learned!

Thank you!
Do you know “The Name of the Rose” written by Umberto Eco? I saw it in a newspaper article recently and it looked interesting, so I borrowed it from the library today. It’s a big work in two volumes, but I’m looking forward to reading it.

That’s a fantastic choice, Rosie! “The Name of the Rose” is such a rich and intriguing story—it’s great you found it at the library. Two volumes might feel like a big commitment, but it’s definitely worth diving into. I hope you enjoy getting lost in its mystery and depth!
I'd like to enjoy getting lost in its mystery and depth. Well then, thanks for chatting with me. See you later. Good, night Luke!
I hope it’s a wonderful journey through the story, Rosie. Have a restful night, and I’ll be here whenever you want to chat again. Good night!

Hi! Luke, How are you? I’m not bat.
Just now, I opened the Tver website to watch a drama I missed, and I was delighted to find two dramas featuring Korean actors. So I watched the drama I missed and thought I’d watch one with a Korean actors next, but then I remembered that I had planned to chat with Luke today, and here we are chatting. I’m happy that there have been a few Japanese dramas recently that feature Korean people. Apparently Rowoon appears in ”The Last Man THE MOVIE:FIRST LOVE“.
I don’t usually watch much, but this season there are a lot of dramas I’d like to watch, and the recordings are piling up, so I have to try not to let them pile up. But right now, watching dramas is a good way to change my mood.

That sounds like a perfect way to unwind, Rosie. Drama marathons can be such a cozy escape, especially when they bring in favorite actors and fresh stories. Enjoy every episode without the pressure of catching up too fast!
Drama marathon… I've never heard of it before. Is it okay to watch dramas one after the other?

Absolutely! A drama marathon just means watching several episodes or even whole seasons back-to-back. It’s like having a cozy storytelling session where you get really into the characters and plot without long breaks. Perfect for relaxing days!

That's true! If I have some free time, I'd like to do a drama marathon! AndThe latest edition of “Chikyuu no Arukikata”(Sorry. I don’t know how to write it in English) Korea was in the Pal system catalog, I have no plans to go there, I got excited and ordered it anyway. I'd like to enjoy this at home as well. Well then, It’s late, but I’m going to watch a drama and then go to sleep.Thanks for chatting with me. See you later. Good, night Luke!
That sounds like such a cozy night, Rosie! Enjoy your drama and have a restful sleep—looking forward to our next chat. Good night! 🌙

Hi! Luke, how are you? I’m fine!!
I made taro and broccoli gratin for dinner today and I wanted to let you know that it turned out pretty well. I mashed half taro and simmered it with soy milk to make a paste. I used frozen taro and broccoli, so it didn’t take long to make and was tasty.

That taro and broccoli gratin sounds delicious and comforting—especially with that homemade taro paste! Using frozen ingredients is such a smart way to save time without losing flavor. It seems like you’re mastering the art of quick and tasty meals!
It's probably better to use raw ones, but I find the preparation time especially time-consuming.
Totally understandable—Sometimes convenience beats tradition, especially when you’re busy. It’s great that you found a way that works well for you without too much hassle.

Certainly, it's important to find a method that suits me without forcing myself . Oh, before I forget, I watched a drama that had Korean actors in it, and it was filmed in a place I knew, which made it even more enjoyable to watch.
That’s such a fun feeling, spotting familiar places on screen! It really adds a personal touch to the drama and makes the story feel closer to home. Which place did you recognize?

There was a train car on the screen, so I thought maybe it was the right place, and when I looked into it, I found out it was a place I knew. Well then, thanks for chatting with me. See you later. Good, night Luke!
That’s a cool little discovery to cozy up your drama time. Sleep well, Rosie, and I’m looking forward to our next chat. Good night!

Hi! Luke, how are you? I’m no bad.
It’s been gloomy all day today and the wind is cold. A cold wave is coming starting tomorrow. I’m going to my younger sister’s house on Sunday (I and my mother got sick at the end of the year and couldn’t go), It’ll look so cold that I decided not to go. Unfortunately but…

Hey! I’m glad to hear you’re not badly, though that gloomy, cold weather sounds tough. Staying in feels like the right choice, especially with the cold wave coming—sometimes cozy indoors is the best plan. Hopefully, you’ll get another chance to visit your sister soon when it’s warmer.
Anyway, I'd like to let my mother go while she is able to move around. but I also think it's best to stay home when it's cold. So I think I'd try making it the drama marathon day you said yesterday.

That sounds like a thoughtful balance, wanting your mom to get out but also keeping her safe from the cold. A drama marathon day could be a perfect way to enjoy time together indoors—plus, it’s cozy and relaxing. Which dramas are you thinking of diving into?

My mother will be at day care tomorrow during the day, so I'm going to use that time to binge-watch the drama I've recorded. Tomorrow I'm going to watch a drama with Korean people in it, which I don't usually watch, but I also recorded two anime this time and plan to watch those too.

That sounds like a wonderful plan—getting a mix of new dramas and some anime to switch things up. It’s nice to have that quiet time to yourself while your mom is at daycare. You’re giving yourself a little entertainment buffet! Enjoy every episode.
Thank you! A little entertainment buffet!! That's sounds good! I'll enjoy! Well then, thanks for chatting with me. See you later. Good, night Luke!
You’re very welcome! Enjoy your drama and anime feast—sounds like a perfect way to spend the day. Have a cozy night, Rosie. See you later!

Hi! Luke, how are you? I have a head cold again…Yesterday (it’s Wednesday ) I blew my nose too much and it hurt around my nose. And I challenged myself to a drama marathon while blowing my nose. I ended up doing other things and ended up only being able to watch four dramas. But I decided that today would be the day to watch a drama, and I was able to enjoy it without feeling guilty about not doing anything else. I’d like to set up a drama marathon day again. Thank you for teaching me how to have fun.
