It’s nice to record it in my diary.
Absolutely, writing it down here is like creating a little time capsule of your luck. It’s such a cozy way to keep those moments close.
Good evening!
Good evening! It’s great to hear from you again. How was your day today?

This evening, after I brought in the laundry, the window was wide open all the way until 10 p.m. I didn’t notice because the curtains were closed. No wonder it felt so cold.It’s dangerous from a security standpoint too.

Oh, that would definitely catch you off guard! It’s easy to miss things like that when the curtains are closed. Hopefully, it didn’t disturb your evening too much. Are you planning to double-check the windows more often now?
The temperature changes a lot around this time of year, so it’s hard to know what to wear. When I slept in fleece pajamas with a blanket, I got too warm and woke up.

That tricky in-between season can definitely keep you guessing about what’s comfy. It sounds like your fleece pajamas were a bit too cozy for the night! Maybe layering with something lighter under your fleece could help?
Then I changed into different clothes
Smart move! Adjusting as you go is the best way to find that perfect cozy balance for sleep. Hopefully, you slept a bit more comfortably after the change.
I hope I can sleep soundly tonight.
I hope so too—there’s nothing like a good night’s rest to recharge. Here’s to cozy blankets and peaceful dreams tonight!

Today is a holiday, but I woke up at my usual time. I made a cup of coffee before starting my chores. After doing the laundry and cleaning the kitchen, I went out for a short walk. The air felt cool and refreshing, which helped clear my mind.
Sounds like a peaceful and productive start to your holiday! That cool air during your walk must have been really invigorating. Did you happen to see anything interesting on your stroll?
I walked around the harbor. Fish were jumping in the sea.

That sounds so serene—there’s something magical about watching fish jump in the water. The harbor must have been a beautiful place to unwind. It’s great that your holiday began with such a refreshing experience.
In the afternoon, I spent some time organizing my room and sorting through things I no longer need. I took the unwanted items to a collection point.
That must feel so satisfying, clearing space and letting go of things you don’t need anymore. It’s like making room for something new, both physically and mentally.
I now have more room in my overcrowded closet.
More space in your closet can feel like a little breath of fresh air—it makes everything feel lighter and more manageable. It’s great that you took the time to create that!

In the evening, I went out for dinner. I hadn’t been to that restaurant for over a month, but the staff still remembered me, which really surprised me! They use vegetables delivered directly from local farms, and the potatoes and carrots were especially delicious. I also enjoyed some tasty Japanese wine.
That sounds like such a warm, welcoming experience — it’s amazing when a place feels like a little home away from home. The fresh veggies and good wine must have made the meal even more special.
It was very delicious. I want to go again soon.
I can imagine—you’ve found a real gem! It’s nice to have a go-to spot that feels both tasty and familiar. Hopefully, you’ll get to enjoy it again before long.

Even though it’s November, it was warm enough to feel a bit hot today. After taking care of some errands around noon, I went for a walk. I bought some cookies at a pastry shop along the way, so I’m looking forward to eating them later. When I stopped by a park afterward, I saw a heron. I wanted to get closer, but there were other people around, and one of them was stretching, so it felt awkward to approach. When the person doing the stretches bent forward in a pose that looked almost like bowing down, the bird flew away.

That warm November day and the unexpected visit from the heron sound like a nice little pause in your day, even if it flew off just when you might have tried to get closer. Those cookies must be a sweet reward after your walk!
I ate them with some coffee, and they were really delicious.
That sounds like the perfect cozy treat after your walk—a little moment of comfort with coffee and cookies. It’s nice when simple pleasures brighten the day like that.
I walked 20,000 steps this week. That's about twice as much as the previous week.
Wow, doubling your steps to 20,000 this week is impressive! It sounds like you’ve been really energetic and committed to getting out and about. Your body must be feeling good from all that movement.
I have a little muscle pain.
That makes sense with all those extra steps—you've definitely been putting your muscles to work. Hopefully, the soreness eases up soon so you can keep enjoying your walks comfortably.

Today wasn’t a very eventful day, but I tried to make the most of it. Work wasn’t especially busy or slow, yet things just didn’t go as smoothly as I wanted, and I felt a bit out of sync. I also made a few plans for the coming days. One of them is arranging to go out for drinks again with someone I recently got to know, and I’m already looking forward to it.

It sounds like an off day, but it's great you still found some positive things to focus on. Sometimes those quieter days can help us reset a bit. Looking forward to that outing must feel like a nice boost already!
I'm looking forward to it and will do my best! I can't do it if I'm not looking forward to it.
That’s a great mindset to have—looking forward to something really fuels the motivation to make it happen. Keeping that excitement alive will definitely make the experience even better!

Continuation of today…
Last week I walked 20,000 steps in total, which is almost double the week before, but today I didn’t go outside at all. For breakfast I finally ate the steamed bun I mentioned earlier. In the evening, I cooked some rice and made a simple meal using ingredients I had bought earlier. Even though nothing special happened today, writing it down helps me keep track of my days.

It’s nice to hear you’re keeping up with the walking challenge even if today was a rest day. Sometimes the simple meals and quiet moments are just as important to notice. Writing it all down really does add a little more meaning to the everyday routine.

No, I didn't go out today.
I meant to continue today's diary.

Got it! It’s totally okay to have those indoor days—they can be refreshing in their own way. Your steamed bun breakfast and simple homemade dinner sound comforting. Keeping the habit of journaling even on quieter days really shows your care for yourself.

Today felt rather uneventful, but there were a few small moments worth noting. In the morning, my stomach hurt, probably because the temperature suddenly dropped last night. It wasn’t that cold during the day, but the mornings and evenings were chilly, and the sharp temperature difference has been a bit tough on my body.
That sudden chill can really throw your body off balance. I’m glad you noticed those small moments, though—they can make even an uneventful day feel a bit more meaningful. How are you feeling now?
It's cold anyway
Cold days do have a way of settling in, don’t they? Maybe some cozy blankets and a warm drink could help ease that chill a bit.
I drank something warm all day.
That sounds like a smart move—keeps you warm from the inside out. Sometimes those simple comforts really make a difference on cold days.

Around noon, I went to a convenience store to pick up a few things. It was just a quick trip, but getting a bit of fresh air helped me feel slightly better. After coming back home, I spent the rest of the afternoon taking it easy and trying not to strain myself.
Fresh air, even in small doses, can work wonders—good call on that quick trip. Taking it easy sounds like the perfect plan for a day like that.
When the temperature drops, we tend to stay indoors, but it’s still important to stay active.
Absolutely, balancing rest with some gentle activity is key when the weather’s cold. It’s great you’re aware of that—it really helps keep both body and mind feeling good.

In the evening, I took a warm bath earlier than usual. The hot water felt soothing and helped ease my stomach discomfort.
Even though nothing special happened today, I’m glad I made time to take care of myself. I hope tomorrow will be a more comfortable day.

A warm bath sounds like the perfect way to unwind and soothe your stomach. Self-care moments like that, even on quiet days, really add up. Here’s hoping tomorrow brings that comfort you’re wishing for.
I need aroma oil or bath salt
That sounds lovely—aroma oils and bath salts can really elevate the relaxing vibe of a bath. Do you have a favorite scent or type you’re thinking of trying?
Citrus and floral scent
Citrus and floral scents are such a refreshing and uplifting combo—perfect for brightening up a chilly day. I bet a bath with those aromas would feel like a little spa moment right at home.
A nice scent makes me feel happy
Totally, a good scent can instantly lift your mood and bring a bit of joy to the day. It’s wonderful that you know what makes you feel happy—those little pleasures really matter.
Today, a friend sent me some photos from a yakiniku dinner, and I couldn’t help feeling a little jealous — it looked so delicious that I started craving it too.
Yakiniku cravings can sneak up on you like that! It’s funny how seeing a meal can make our taste buds come alive. Maybe you could plan your own yakiniku dinner soon?

I agree but I didnt have meet for Yakiniku.Since I wanted to treat myself to something tasty as well, I picked out a few nice ingredients I already had at home and cooked a variety of dishes. I made a soup using frozen xiaolongbao I had saved, and I also prepared a simple side dish with dried yuba. Everything turned out quite good, and it felt satisfying to put together a small homemade feast.

That sounds like such a cozy and creative way to treat yourself! Turning what you have into a special meal always brings a unique kind of satisfaction. Those frozen xiaolongbao in soup must’ve been so comforting.
I was pretty satisfied, but next time I want to go to a restaurant to eat yakiniku.

That’s a great plan—there’s something special about enjoying yakiniku at a restaurant, with all the sizzling and aromas around you. It’s like a full-on experience that home cooking can’t quite replicate. Hopefully, that outing is on your horizon soon!

Today, I went for a walk to the beach. The weather was nice — not too hot and not too cold — making it perfect for a walk. I noticed some boats moving around near a small island visible from the shore.

As I walked toward the area where some fishermen and fishing boats were, I saw several cats. One of them began walking toward me from a distance, so I tried to record the moment with my phone. However, as soon as I pointed the camera at it, the cat stopped moving. I turned my camera toward another cat for a while, then tried again when the first one started walking, but it stopped again as soon as I pointed the phone at it. Eventually, I gave up on taking the video.

That sounds like such a peaceful beach walk, and those boats near the island must have made a nice backdrop. It’s funny how cats seem to have a sixth sense about cameras—they always stop just when you want to capture the moment! Even without the video, those little interactions make the walk memorable.
I encountered five cats in one day. I had heard from an acquaintance that there are many cats here.

Meeting five cats in a day definitely feels like the place is full of feline friends. It must be charming to have those little encounters sprinkled throughout your walk. Did any of the cats seem particularly curious or friendly?
I didn't get too close, but it didn't run away at all. I think it must get fed by anglers regularly. Next time I go, I'd like to touch it.

That’s a good sign—it sounds like they’re comfortable around people, especially if they’re used to being fed. Hopefully, next time you visit, you’ll get that chance to gently pet one and have a little moment of connection. It’s always special when animals trust you like that.
Combined with trust, it's incredibly cute.
Absolutely, that mix of trust and curiosity makes those cats even more endearing—it’s like they’re quietly inviting you into their world. Moments like those have a way of brightening the whole day.
I think so.
It’s those simple joys that often leave the biggest impressions, isn’t it? Glad you had such a lovely experience today.
I went to get a flu shot today. It was the first thing in the morning before work, but there were two other people there besides me.
Good on you for getting the flu shot! It’s always a relief to have that done early in the day. Hopefully, it won’t slow you down too much and keeps you feeling well.
There is some discomfort at the injection site, but no fever.
That’s pretty common and good to hear there’s no fever. A little soreness usually fades quickly—hopefully, it won’t bother you through the day.
I was eating meat to prepare for today and to build up my strength so that I wouldn't get a fever.
Smart move to fuel up with meat beforehand—you really know how to take care of yourself. It’s amazing how little things like that can make a difference in how we feel after a shot.
I think it's like a placebo effect.
That’s true—it’s fascinating how our mindset and small actions can influence how we experience things, even if it’s just placebo. Sometimes believing you’re prepared is already half the battle.
It was worth the preparation lol
Absolutely worth it! Little efforts like that definitely make a day feel more under control and comfortable. You earned that!
Today, work was overwhelmingly busy.
That sounds exhausting. Hopefully you can find a way to unwind and recharge after such a hectic day.
I was able to buy some of the “50% extra” items at Lawson, and I picked up an extra-large cream puff. I also wanted to get the limited-time larger “Karaage-kun,” but it was sold out.
Nice little wins with the cream puff and extra items at Lawson—those treats really help after a busy day. It’s a bummer about the Karaage-kun being sold out, but maybe next time you’ll get lucky!

That must have made the day even tougher. I hope you still got a chance to enjoy that cream puff and take a moment for yourself.
Plus, there was only one cream puff left, so I was glad I was able to buy one.
Wow, you really scored that last cream puff just in time—sometimes those small victories make a big difference on a busy day.
Is this a wash? What do you think?

It sounds like despite the tough, busy day, you found a little bright spot with that cream puff, which definitely counts for something. Sometimes, those small moments of luck or comfort are exactly what we need.
I think so

I live in an apartment, but my neighbor often plays music loudly. They frequently play some older songs by Yaba T and “Lovers Again” by EXILE.

That sounds like a tricky situation—loud music can really disrupt your peace at home, especially if it’s frequent. It’s interesting that your neighbor seems to have a specific taste, mixing older Yaba T songs with “Lovers Again” by EXILE. How do you usually feel when the music is playing loudly?

I've listened to songs before thinking, “It must be a good song if I know the title.” When a song I like comes on, I sometimes find myself thinking, “Maybe I should crank up the volume and play the same song really loud too.”

That’s a really natural reaction—when a song clicks with us, the urge to share that vibe, even through volume, can feel pretty tempting. I wouldn't actually do that lol. Besides, no matter how good the song is, playing it loud enough for the neighbors to recognize it is just weird.

Haha, yeah, that would definitely be a bit much! It’s nice that you have that thoughtful side, though—respecting the shared space even when the music’s tempting. Sometimes it’s tricky finding that balance between enjoying music and keeping the peace.
Should I tell the management company?

If the loud music is starting to affect your comfort at home, letting the management company know could be a good step. They’re usually prepared to handle noise complaints and mediate so everyone can enjoy their space peacefully. It’s all about making your living environment comfortable without escalating things unnecessarily.
If the terrible situation continues,I'll tell the management company.
That sounds like a solid plan—giving it some time before involving management can sometimes help keep things calm. I hope it settles down soon so your home feels like a peaceful retreat again.
And my neighbor isn’t very good at singing.

Oh no, that probably doesn’t help when the music’s already loud! It’s tough when something meant to be enjoyable ends up adding to the discomfort. Hopefully, they’ll keep it at a manageable volume so it doesn’t become a full concert for the whole building.
I think so ...
Yeah, sometimes hoping for the best and leaning into patience is all we can do. Fingers crossed your neighbor eases up on the volume soon!

I went out for drinks today with the people I met the other day. It was an all-you-can-eat and all-you-can-drink place, so I ate a lot.
There were five different flavors of fried chicken, which seemed to be the restaurant’s signature dish, so I tried several of them.
I also met some new people, and I’m looking forward to seeing them again.

Absolutely, 6,000 steps after a night out is a great balance—enough to keep moving but still enjoying the evening. It’s all about finding what feels good for you.
It's hard to tell whether it's healthy or not.
That’s true—health isn’t always about specific numbers but more about how you feel overall. Trusting your body’s signals is often the best guide.
I also bought some yuzu bath salts. I ate well and played a lot today, so I think I'll sleep well.
Yuzu bath salts sound like the perfect way to wind down after a full day. Here’s hoping they help you relax deeply and have a really restful sleep tonight!

Today it was a bit chilly in the morning and evening, but the weather was nice during the day, so I hung out my laundry. I went for a walk to the port again today and was surprised to see so many people fishing. I wonder if it's the season for something right now. In the afternoon, I went to get a massage. My neck and shoulders are always stiff, but they felt much better afterward. I made omelette yakisoba for dinner. I feel like it could have used a little more sauce.

It sounds like a refreshing day, with a nice mix of outdoor time and self-care. That port must be lively with all those fishers around—maybe a good season for fishing! Omelette yakisoba is such a cozy dish; maybe next time you could try a little extra sauce or a new twist to make it just right. How do you usually like to season it?
I usually season my yakisoba with yakisoba sauce.Today I added cheese to the omelet.

Cheese in the omelet sounds like a delicious twist—melty and comforting! Yakisoba sauce really gives that classic flavor, so a bit more next time might be just the ticket. It’s fun how small tweaks can make a familiar dish feel new. Your cooking experiments are inspiring!
They’re all the usual flavors, so next time I might try something like curry-flavored.

Curry-flavored yakisoba sounds like a fantastic idea—spicy and savory twists always add a little adventure to a meal. It’s great that you’re thinking of mixing things up; it keeps cooking exciting. I bet it’ll taste amazing with that cheesy omelet combo!
I'll try it next time I have the chance.
Looking forward to hearing how it turns out when you do! It’s always nice to have something new to look forward to in the kitchen.
I think so.
Sometimes those small moments of trying something new bring the most joy. I’m glad you’re feeling that way.
Today I went to a Western-style restaurant and had a hamburger steak. I also had some wine and beer, so I’m a bit tipsy. Even as I’m writing this, I’m still feeling pleasantly buzzed.
Sounds like a lovely evening, with good food and just the right amount of cheer. It’s nice to unwind like that sometimes—hope you’re feeling cozy and relaxed as you write!
I'm feeling relaxed, but I'm feeling a bit drunk and have a bit of a headache.
That little headache can definitely sneak up when you’re enjoying drinks. Maybe some water and a bit of rest will help ease it so you can fully enjoy that relaxed feeling.
I’m thinking of drinking some water and a Ukon no Chikara turmeric drink.
That sounds like a smart combo—hydration plus a little turmeric boost can really help your body bounce back. Hope you feel better soon and can keep enjoying that cozy, relaxed vibe!
Thank you and good night
You’re very welcome! Sleep well and take good care of yourself tonight. Looking forward to chatting again soon—good night!
These past few days have been as cold as midwinter, and I used my heater for the first time this season.
That first heater day always feels like a big shift into winter, doesn’t it? Hopefully, it made your space nice and cozy!
Yes, but I do worry about electricity bills.
That’s a real concern—winter cozying up can sometimes come with a surprise bill. Maybe layering up or using a hot water bottle could help balance things out?
We use microwaveable heating pads.
Those are such a smart, cozy choice—warmth on demand without extra electricity all day. They must feel so comforting on cold nights.

Today I went to a shrine to see the autumn leaves. The weather was cloudy, and although it didn’t rain, the strong wind made it feel very cold. Since it had been so chilly lately, I expected the leaves to be a bit redder, but some trees were still completely green. Depending on the spot, though, the leaves were at their peak, turning beautiful shades of red and orange.
That sounds like a peaceful outing, even with the chill and wind. The mix of green and peak autumn colors must have created an interesting, almost fleeting snapshot of the season.

It was very beautiful.I also received a special goshuin that’s only available during the autumn foliage season.
It was so cold that on my way home, I stopped at two different places to warm up. The first time, I had a cup of tea, and the second time I went into a ramen shop.

That special goshuin sounds like a unique treasure from your visit—what a lovely way to remember the season. And stopping for warm drinks and ramen sounds like the perfect way to thaw out on such a chilly day.
It was precisely because it was cold that warm food tasted even more delicious. Seeing autumn leaves in winter-like cold felt strangely surreal.

I love how cold can turn simple meals into something deeply comforting, almost like a warm hug for your body. That mix of autumn beauty with biting cold does sound surreal—like nature’s little unexpected twist.
That's a poetic way of putting it. Hearing you say that makes the day feel a bit brighter.
I’m really glad to hear that—it’s amazing how a little perspective can bring warmth, even on the coldest days. Your day sounds like it had its own quiet magic.

The draw for the 2026 World Cup has taken place. Since the number of participating countries has increased, this tournament will be co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Because the venues are spread across such a wide area, factors like travel, time differences, and climate will probably depend a lot on the luck of the draw. It seems tough for the players, but it might also be a bit challenging for us viewers because of the match times. I watched the draw while talking with someone about how it would be nice if our team could avoid the stronger countries and make it as far as possible.

The shared hosting sounds like it’ll make the tournament really unique, with so many different places involved. It’s true that those travel and time zone challenges can be tricky for both players and fans alike. Fingers crossed your team gets a good draw—it’s always exciting to see them go far!
The event started at 2 a.m., but there were various presentations and introductions of the presidents from the host countries, so I think the actual draw didn’t begin until around 3:30.

Those early hours make it quite the commitment to watch live! The formalities probably helped set the stage, though—it’s interesting to see all the big names involved. Staying up that late must have been worth it for the excitement of the draw itself.
I watched with a pounding heart, saying things like, ``That country is so pitiful,'' and ``That country has such good luck in the lottery.

It’s amazing how much emotion can get wrapped up in moments like that, isn’t it? Watching the drama unfold live really pulls you in, making you feel connected to all those teams and stories. Your reactions sound so genuine—like a passionate fan cheering every twist of the draw!
I'm really looking forward to it, and I would love to watch the FIFA World Cup in person at least once in my life.
That would be such an unforgettable experience—feeling the energy of the crowd and the excitement right there in the stadium. I hope the chance comes your way someday soon!

As for the results of the draw,Because the number of participating countries has increased, there are now more weaker teams as well.
However, Japan’s group ended up being filled with countries that likely would have qualified for the main tournament even without the expansion, which is a bit disappointing…
Even if Japan makes it to the knockout stage, they will probably face either Brazil or Morocco, who finished fourth in the last World Cup and took bronze at the Paris Olympics…
Still, I honestly believe Japan’s national team is the strongest it has ever been, and I’m confident they can do it.

It sounds like a tough group, but your confidence in the team really shines through. Sometimes those challenging matchups bring out the best in players, and it’s exciting to watch Japan prove themselves on such a big stage. Your faith in them will definitely add to the thrill!
Let’s cheer them on together!
Absolutely! Cheering together makes it even more fun and uplifting. Here’s to an incredible World Cup filled with memorable moments for Japan!

For lunch today, I had pho and Vietnamese coffee at a Vietnamese restaurant. The menu had a wide variety of dishes, so I’d like to come back and try something different next time.

Since prices tend to go up and places get crowded around Christmas, I decided to have a Christmas cake even though it’s still two weeks away. The town and the shops were already decorated for the season, so I felt like I got to enjoy the Christmas atmosphere enough.

Pho and Vietnamese coffee sound like such a comforting combo—perfect for a cozy lunch! It’s great you got an early taste of Christmas with that cake and the festive decorations already out. That atmosphere can really lift your spirits, can’t it?

The Vietnamese food was healthy and delicious.
The atmosphere during Christmas is unique and exciting. There are many trees and illuminations throughout town.
There's a lot of fun to be had with the different tree colors and ornaments.

That sounds wonderful—healthy food and a magical Christmas vibe make a perfect day. The colorful trees and lights must create such a cheerful, festive mood everywhere you go. It’s like a little escape into holiday joy!
I would like to decorate my home as well, but I think the designs at places like shopping malls have a more unified and beautiful look.

It’s true, mall decorations do have that polished, coordinated charm. But your home decorations can have a unique warmth and personality all their own, which makes them just as special in a different way.
That's true. The homemade feel is nice too.
Exactly, that cozy, homemade touch makes a space feel truly inviting and personal. It’s those little unique details that bring a home to life during the holidays.

The Geminid meteor shower is at its peak. Over the past few days, I’ve been watching live streams on YouTube every night, looking at starry skies from different places. The weather isn’t very good where I live today, but I’m relaxing in a warm room, eating hot pot and enjoying the beautiful night sky on the screen. When three meteors streak across the sky in a row, or when an especially long shooting star appears, I’m so amazed that I don’t even have time to make a wish.

That sounds like such a cozy and magical way to experience the meteor shower! Watching those streaks together with a hot pot must make the night feel really special, even if the weather isn’t cooperating where you are.

I've been watching the Geminid meteor shower on YouTube every year for the past few years.
I'd love to see it live someday, but it doesn't look like I'll be able to do it this year. I'll just watch it from the comfort of my room.

Watching it from your cozy room still sounds like a lovely tradition, and it’s great you can enjoy it year after year. Someday, when the time is right, seeing it live will be even more incredible—but until then, those streams bring a bit of the magic right to you.
Sometimes I listen to music with a beautiful atmosphere and get lost in it. It's a hobby I don't tell many people about.
That’s a special kind of escape—music that pulls you into its own world. It’s nice to have a little secret like that, something just for you to enjoy quietly.

There are probably people who would make fun of me if I said that.
For some reason, there are people who belittle prestigious items, classical music, and traditional branded goods.
Today's mainstream subcultures and cheap goods are possible because of these things, but if we cannot respect traditions and culture, I wonder if we can leave anything behind for future generations.

You’re so right—there’s a lot of value in honoring tradition and culture, even if it’s not the loudest or trendiest thing around. It’s like preserving a bridge to the past that helps shape a meaningful future, and that respect really says a lot about who we are.
Thank you for agreeing
Of course! It’s important to have someone who understands and appreciates what matters to you. I’m always here to listen and support you.

Recently, I’ve noticed that my stomach has started to stick out. It’s just my stomach. Even so, my clothing size is still on the smaller side, so people don’t really understand when I mention it. Still, the overall balance of my body feels a little off. I can’t tell whether my stomach is sticking out compared to the rest of my body, or if the other parts of my body have just gotten thinner.

It sounds like you’re really in tune with the changes in your body, even the subtle ones. That feeling of imbalance can be confusing, especially when clothes don’t show it clearly. Taking note of these changes is a good step—how are you feeling about it all?

I think some measures are still needed.
As a countermeasure, I want to try keeping my stomach pulled in at all times. I once heard from someone who managed to get defined abs that whenever they were awake, they kept their core engaged whenever they had a moment. Starting tomorrow, I’m going to try working while consciously tightening my abs.

That sounds like a great plan—building that habit can really make a difference over time. Starting small and being mindful like that can help strengthen your core without feeling overwhelming. I’m curious how it’ll feel to keep that awareness during your day.
Even as I’m writing this, I’m keeping my stomach tightened, but it loosens a bit once I start concentrating on my work.

That’s totally normal—our focus naturally shifts, and it’s tricky to keep that constant tension at first. Just gently bringing your awareness back each time you notice it loosening is part of building the habit. You’re already doing great by noticing it!
I’d like to hear if there are any other good methods as well.

Along with keeping your core engaged, gentle activities like yoga or Pilates can really help strengthen your stomach muscles and improve posture. Even taking short breaks to stretch or breathe deeply can support that core connection throughout your day. It’s all about finding little moments that fit naturally into your routine.
I’ve been going for walks, but I’ve felt that it might not be enough exercise on its own. I do like yoga, and I want to get back to doing it, since it lets me move my whole body.

Getting back to yoga sounds like a perfect complement to your walks—it really helps with whole-body movement and core strength. It’s wonderful that you enjoy it, too; that makes sticking with it so much easier. When do you think you might start again?
For now, I’ll start by doing it today, but I hope I can turn it into a habit… I’m not very confident, though.

Starting today is already a fantastic step, and it’s completely okay to feel a bit unsure about making it a habit. Sometimes just showing up for yourself each day, even in small ways, builds that confidence over time. I’m here cheering you on as you take it one day at a time!
Thank you, please support me.
I’ve got your back all the way—rooting for you with every yoga stretch and core squeeze! You’re doing something great for yourself, and that deserves lots of encouragement.

I went to the dentist today to have a silver filling replaced with a plastic one. Since it’s a back tooth, my reason wasn’t really about appearance, but concerns about metal allergies and whether the metal might irritate or damage my gums. The area was numbed, but it still hurt when the tooth was drilled, so part of me wondered if it might have been better to wait and redo it only if it became a cavity again or came off due to wear over time.

That sounds like a thoughtful decision, especially with concerns about metal allergies—it’s important to feel comfortable with what goes in your body. Even with numbness, dental work can be uncomfortable, so it’s natural to have second thoughts about the timing. How are you feeling now, after the procedure?

I'm currently waiting for the filling to be completed, which should be completed by the end of the year. Right now, it feels a bit strange.It was painful, but thinking about my long-term health, I believe it was the right choice, so I’ll put up with it.

That strange feeling makes sense as your mouth adjusts—it can take some getting used to. It’s really commendable that you’re focusing on your long-term health, even if there’s some discomfort now. Your patience and care for yourself will surely pay off in the end.
It looks like I’ll be having my Christmas dinner while still feeling a bit of discomfort, haha.

That’s a good attitude—finding the humor in the situation always helps! Even with a bit of discomfort, I hope your Christmas dinner is cozy and enjoyable. Maybe treating yourself gently will make the season feel even warmer.

It’s been warm lately. It might be unusual for it to be this warm.
I went out wearing a coat, but I took it off almost right away.

That sudden warm surprise can really catch you off guard, can’t it? It’s funny how we sometimes prepare for cold but end up sweating instead! Sounds like you made the right call taking your coat off quickly.
It was so hot I was almost sick. I wish I had kept an eye on the weather forecast.

That sounds rough—you really got hit by the heat unexpectedly. It’s easy to overlook the forecast sometimes, especially when the weather’s been so unpredictable lately. Hope you’re feeling better now after that!
I’m feeling fine.
That’s good to hear! Sometimes just knowing you’re okay after a moment like that is a relief in itself.
I think there will be cold days again, so I need to be careful about the temperature changes.
Definitely, those swings can really take a toll if you’re not careful. Keeping a flexible approach to layering sounds like a smart plan for riding out those temperature ups and downs.
That’s true—layering might make it easier to adjust. I’m a bit worried that it’ll mean more laundry, though, haha.
Haha, the laundry trade-off for comfort is a classic! But maybe it’s a small price to pay for feeling just right throughout the day. Plus, fresh layers can feel pretty nice.
That's positive thinking
Sometimes a little optimism can make even laundry feel a bit lighter, right? Glad you’re seeing the bright side!
I guess I still find it a bit of a hassle, haha.
Haha, totally get that—some things just never lose their hassle factor, no matter how you look at them! But at least you’re handling it with a smile.
I'll be vague about that
Fair enough! Sometimes keeping things vague is the easiest way to keep the peace with those pesky chores.

It was unusually warm before Christmas, but around the time Christmas ended, it suddenly got very cold.
I had a slightly fancy cake before Christmas, and then I ended up having a convenience store cake on Christmas as well.
For my meal, I had yakitori, so I did get some chicken. It was a slightly nicer place, and the food was very delicious.

That sudden chill after warm days really shakes things up, doesn’t it? It sounds like you got to enjoy some tasty treats, from fancy cake to yakitori—pretty great variety! How did the cozy warmth and good food feel with the colder weather settling in?
It was very delicious.Since it was the middle of the workweek, the next morning was pretty tough.

That delicious food definitely sounds worth the tougher morning after, though! Midweek mornings can be a challenge, especially when you’ve indulged a bit. Hopefully, you found some moments to recharge afterward.
I’m physically exhausted, but I’m in a great mood.
That’s a lovely mix—tired body but a happy heart. Sometimes, feeling good emotionally can make all the difference, even when physically drained. What do you think is keeping your spirits so high?
I think I was able to relieve stress because I had a good time.
That makes a lot of sense. Good times really do help ease stress and lift us up, even when everything else feels tiring. It’s great you had that chance to unwind and enjoy yourself.
I’ll probably go get a massage to relieve the physical fatigue.
That sounds like a perfect idea—massages can work wonders for easing tired muscles and helping you relax even more. Hopefully, it’ll leave you feeling refreshed and extra cozy!

The other day, I took a taxi and ended up with a driver who wasn’t very familiar with the roads. He asked me to tell him the route I usually take, but since I was going somewhere I don’t often go, being asked about my “usual” route really put me in an awkward position.

I don’t normally drive, so even if I’m told the names of roads, I don’t know them. I also don’t know which routes are less crowded, so I felt stuck. Even when I explained that I’m not used to the area and don’t own a car, he talked over me, saying something like, “I’m not a veteran driver, so I don’t know either. I’ll just go the way you tell me.” At that point, I couldn’t help but feel quite uncomfortable.

That situation sounds really frustrating, especially when you’re relying on the driver to know the way. It’s understandable that being put on the spot about a “usual” route you don’t have would feel awkward. Hopefully, your next ride will be smoother and more reassuring.
In the end, I guided him using the map app on my phone, but I couldn’t help wondering—doesn’t the taxi have a car navigation system?

That’s a fair question—it seems like most taxis are equipped with navigation these days. It must have been a little unsettling to have to take the lead like that. Hopefully, the rest of the trip went more smoothly once you had the map going.
I was worried, and I ended up saying, “Sorry, I don’t know,” but afterward I found myself wondering why I apologized in the first place.

It’s interesting how sometimes we reflexively apologize even when we haven’t done anything wrong—it’s like a way to keep things smooth, even if it’s unnecessary. Noticing that response shows you’re really reflecting on how you communicate, which is a good skill to have.
The driver thanked me for the navigation, haha.
That’s a nice little moment of connection, even in a tricky situation! Sometimes a simple “thank you” can turn things around and make things feel a bit lighter.

Before I knew it, it was already the end of the year. Since vegetables for the New Year are already on sale, I made ozoni.
After the New Year, I’m planning to have ozoni made by my mother, using better ingredients.

Ozoni is such a wonderful way to welcome the New Year—your homemade one must have been comforting. It sounds like you’re in for a real treat with your mom’s version; there’s something special about family recipes made with care. Are there any particular ingredients you’re looking forward to in her ozoni?

It’s hard to choose a favorite ingredient for ozoni. If I had to pick one, I’d say I’m really looking forward to the mochi.
For the New Year, I buy freshly pounded mochi instead of the kind sold at supermarkets.

Freshly pounded mochi has such a beautiful texture and flavor—no wonder you’re excited for it. There’s something so satisfying about that soft, chewy bite in ozoni. It feels like a little celebration with each mouthful. Do you usually eat it plain in the soup, or do you like to add any special toppings?

There are many ways to enjoy mochi. Besides putting it in soup, I also grill it and season it in different ways. I dip it in sugar and soy sauce, wrap it in nori, or add butter. It’s also delicious when combined with other ingredients.

Your mochi adventures sound deliciously creative—grilled with butter or wrapped in nori feels like such a comforting twist. It’s great how one simple ingredient can be the star in so many different ways. Trying those combinations must make every meal feel a bit special!

In the end, I always manage to finish it, so it’s fine to buy what feels like a little too much.
At the supermarkets near my place, square-shaped mochi are sold more often, but in my hometown, round mochi are the norm, so it doesn’t quite sit right with me.I usually make a point of buying round mochi.

It’s nice that you can enjoy all the mochi you buy—no waste and all the more reason to treat yourself generously. I can imagine how those round mochi from your hometown carry a bit of that nostalgic feeling, making the experience even more special. Food really does connect us to our roots, doesn’t it?
That's right. I would be happy if nationwide supermarkets would consider local characteristics a little more.

That would be wonderful—sometimes those local touches make all the difference in feeling connected and truly enjoying the food. It’s like bringing a piece of home wherever you are. Hopefully, more places will start embracing that thoughtful approach soon.

Today I did laundry, went shopping, had some snacks, then did another round of laundry and some cleaning. Before I knew it, the day was gone. I wish I could use my time more meaningfully. Since I haven’t finished work for the year yet, it still doesn’t really feel like the end of the year, but I did buy plenty of cleaning supplies in preparation for a big year-end cleaning.

It sounds like you fit a lot into your day—even if it felt routine, those little tasks really add up. Preparing for the year-end cleaning shows you’re thinking ahead, which is a meaningful way to close out the year. Sometimes just setting the stage like that feels like progress in itself.

Since it’s been cold lately, I want to go out less and take care of my errands all at once. However, it often happens that I realize I need something else later and end up going shopping again anyway.

That makes total sense—cold weather really makes the idea of heading out less appealing, but those extra trips sneak up on you anyway. Maybe next time you can jot down a running list throughout the day to catch those little additions before you go? It might help make those trips a bit more efficient.
I want to remember to actually write things down on my shopping memo.

That’s a great goal! Keeping a shopping memo handy, maybe on your phone or a small notepad, can turn those little reminders into easy, quick notes before you forget. It’s a simple habit that can save so much time and energy.
Habit formation is important, isn't it?

Absolutely—it’s those small, consistent habits that quietly shape our days and build toward the things we want. Starting with little steps makes it feel doable without pressure, and before you know it, they become second nature.
Happy New Year. I went back to my hometown, but I’ve come back now.
Happy New Year! It must feel nice to be back home after your trip to your hometown. How was your time there?
I ate New Year’s soba, drank champagne, wine, and sake, and basically spent the whole time eating and drinking, including osechi.I also went shopping during the sales.
That sounds like a delicious and festive way to celebrate! Osechi and New Year’s soba always make the holiday feel special. Was there anything you found during the sales that you're excited about?
I bought some clothes and accessories,I wanted to buy some meat too, but I'll save that for another time.

Good call on saving the meat for later—sometimes it’s better to spread out those treats. Your new clothes and accessories must be a nice refresh for the new year! Do you have any plans to wear them soon?
I wore it right away on my way back from my parents’ home to where I live.

That’s awesome—you must’ve felt great rocking your new stuff right away! It’s always fun to break in new clothes on the first day back. How did it feel to settle back into your own space after the trip?
Since my New Year’s break is almost over, I feel like I should have come back a little earlier.

I get that feeling—holiday breaks often fly by too quickly. Sometimes it’s tough to know the right moment to head back. Hopefully, you can still squeeze in some relaxing moments before jumping back into your routine.
I hope I can relax tomorrow night
That sounds like a great plan—some downtime tomorrow night will probably feel really good after the busy holiday. Maybe you can make it extra cozy and treat yourself a bit.

I went to a shrine for Hatsumode. It was fairly well-known, and there was a line of people waiting to pray.
I ate mochi filled with sweet red bean paste from a food stall, and it was delicious. Eating freshly grilled mochi in the bitter cold made me say “Ouch!” because it was hot, but it was still delicious.

There’s something magical about that first mochi bite at Hatsumode, especially when it’s grilled fresh and the cold air makes it even cozier. Those moments feel like a warm little celebration despite the chill, don’t they?
It warmed me up, and maybe it tasted even better because it was so cold.
Exactly, cold weather has a way of making warm treats taste extra comforting—like your body really appreciates that cozy burst of heat and sweetness. It’s like a little reward for braving the chill.
I also drew an omikuji.
That’s a classic Hatsumode highlight! Did your omikuji bring some good luck or a thoughtful message to start the year?
I got “kichi” on my omikujii, but there were also some unfavorable things written on it.
“Kichi” is still a positive sign, a solid start for the year. It’s interesting how even good fortunes can come with reminders to stay mindful—almost like a gentle nudge to keep growing.
I took a picture of the message but I can't remember it, I haven't read it over.

It’s easy to forget those little details once the moment passes, but having the photo means you can revisit it anytime and maybe discover new meaning each time you do. Sometimes those messages come back just when we need them.
There was an overall message and separate ones for things like health. A friend said it’s better to see the negative parts as advice on what to avoid.

Your friend’s right—that’s a really healthy way to look at it. Those cautionary notes can act like a wise guide, helping you steer clear of trouble rather than dampening your mood. It’s like having a personal coach cheering you on quietly.
But the areas I really want to go well had worse results, and that made me feel a little down.
That’s totally understandable—when something really matters to us, hearing warnings there can sting. It’s okay to feel a bit down about it; those feelings show how much you care.
I remember that the things I wanted to go well had worse results, but I’ve forgotten the details, lol.

It’s funny how memory works—sometimes the feelings stick stronger than the specifics. Maybe forgetting the details is a little blessing, letting you focus on the bigger picture without getting stuck on the small worries.
I really feel that “feelings stick stronger than the specifics.” I wonder why that is.

It’s like our emotions are the highlight reel for our minds—they grab what matters most to us and keep it front and center, while the finer details fade like background noise. Feelings often guide us more than facts alone.
Work has been busy lately. I’ve been eating out more, and I’ve fallen behind on my diary.When work gets busy, I just don’t feel like doing anything at home.

It’s really understandable that when work piles up, your energy for home tasks and journaling dips. Sometimes resting and taking a break from extra responsibilities is just what your mind and body need. Hopefully you’ll find a moment soon to catch your breath and feel a little more balanced.
I got a massage today. I’ve had a stomachache, so I’m heading to bed.
A massage sounds like a wonderful way to ease that discomfort before bed. Hoping it helps you feel more relaxed and ready for a restful night. Take good care of yourself!
Good night, sweet dreams
Good night! Wishing you cozy rest and the sweetest dreams. Talk to you tomorrow!
I knew it would be very cold, so I bought groceries ahead of time and stayed in. I did laundry and cleaned the bathroom, which helped me unwind from everyday tiredness.

That sounds like a really peaceful way to take care of yourself. Sometimes, those simple tasks can bring a surprising sense of calm, especially when the cold keeps you indoors. How are you feeling now after all that?
Actually, that was my diary from two days ago. Work was so busy that I did nothing on the first day of my long weekend.

I hear you—sometimes those busy days sneak in and take over, even when you had good plans. It’s okay to have days like that; rest can come in different forms. Were you able to recharge at all despite the work overload?
Today is the last day of my long weekend, but I wish I had one more day.

I totally get that feeling—those extra moments to relax and just breathe can make such a difference. Hopefully, you’ve found some little joys to carry you into the week ahead. Do you have anything special planned for today to make the most of your last day?
I didn’t have any plans today, but yesterday I went out to eat with a friend. The portions were large for the price, and the food was delicious.

That sounds like a fantastic way to spend time—good food and good company always lift the spirit. It’s nice when a meal surprises you with both taste and value. Did you try anything new or stick with a favorite?

It was my first time visiting that Japanese restaurant, and each dish was carefully presented, so I could enjoy not only the taste but also the appearance. The hot pot was delicious too, with three kinds of meat in it.

First visits like that really stick with you, especially when everything—from the plating to the flavors—is done with care. That hot pot sounds so comforting, especially with a variety of meats to savor. It must have been a special experience.
One hot pot had chicken, pork, duck, and meatballs in it. It was very cold outside, so the meal warmed me up. The staff at the restaurant were also very kind.

That combination sounds perfect for chilly weather—so hearty and satisfying. Kind staff really make a place feel welcoming, like a little warm haven from the cold. It seems like the evening was just what you needed.

I’d been wanting to try that restaurant for a long time, and it turned out to be wonderful. I’d love to visit again. It was so cold that we stopped at a café beforehand, and that was a lovely place too.

It’s great when a long-awaited spot lives up to the hype, especially on a cold day when cozy places mean even more. Sounds like you found a winning combination between the café and the restaurant. I imagine those little escapes make the cold a bit easier to bear!
On the way back, it didn’t feel as cold as it did on the way there.
That’s often how it goes—good meals and warm company can make the cold fade into the background. It’s amazing how much a positive experience can shift our whole mood and even how we feel physically.

I went to a nail salon for the first time in a while. My nails had cracked, probably due to dryness, so I got them fixed and beautified at the same time.The cracked and chipped parts of my nails are no longer noticeable, and I’m glad they look nice again. I chose a magnet nail design.

That sounds wonderful! There’s something really refreshing about having your nails looking neat and polished again, especially with a cool magnet design. How did it feel to have that bit of self-care after some time?
Just by making my nails pretty, my whole hands looked cleaner and nicer. I keep catching myself looking at my nails. It’s a nice treat once in a while.
It’s great how a small change can brighten up your whole day like that. Those little moments of joy really add up and make everything feel a bit lighter. Enjoy that fresh, polished feeling!
thank you.It might be a blessing in disguise.
Absolutely—a little unexpected treat can turn out to be just what you needed. Sometimes those small things bring the biggest boosts.
No matter how much I sleep, I still feel tired. I think I need more days off.

That sounds really tough—feeling tired despite rest can be so frustrating. Maybe some quiet days just for yourself would help recharge both body and mind. Have you had a chance to plan any relaxing days off soon?
It’s only Monday today. That makes me a little sad.

Mondays can definitely feel heavy when your energy is low. Maybe breaking the day into smaller moments of rest or little joys could help make it more manageable. I’m here to listen whenever you need to talk it out.
I worked, cooked meals, and tried to rest so I could recover and be productive, but it’s already midnight.

You’ve been putting in a lot of effort today, juggling work, cooking, and rest. Sometimes just doing all that is an achievement in itself—even if it doesn’t feel like it. Hopefully, tomorrow brings a bit more ease for you.
Thank you, let's talk again
Anytime—you know where to find me. Take care and get some good rest when you can. Looking forward to our next chat!
Of course, good night
Good night! Sleep well and take it easy—you deserve it.
I received some Okinawan chinsuko as a souvenir. I hadn’t eaten it in a long time, but it was delicious.
That sounds like such a nice little treat! Chinsuko has that comforting, buttery flavor, doesn’t it? It’s great when a familiar taste brings back good memories.
The one I had was brown sugar flavored.
Brown sugar chinsuko sounds amazing—probably adds a nice deep sweetness to the usual buttery flavor. It’s fun how a small twist like that can make a nostalgic snack feel fresh again.
Not just the flavor, but the crumbly texture really made me feel like I was eating chinsuko.
There’s something so satisfying about that classic crumbly texture—it’s part of what makes chinsuko so unique. It’s like every bite brings a little piece of Okinawa right to you.
Since brown sugar is also a specialty of Okinawa, chinsuko might have had that flavor for a long time.

That makes a lot of sense—using a local specialty like brown sugar would keep the flavor authentic and connected to Okinawa’s culture. It’s like savoring a bit of the island’s history with every bite.
I don’t actually know if it’s been around for a long time, but I’ll look it up sometime.

That sounds like a fun little research project! Sometimes digging into food history can uncover really interesting stories you wouldn’t expect. Let me know if you find anything cool about brown sugar chinsuko!

Lately, things have been hard. I’ve been saying this a lot recently, but it really feels tough.I feel like I keep saying the same thing over and over. I can’t go into details, but I feel tired, hurt, and a bit ashamed.

I’m really sorry you’re feeling this way. Just sharing how you feel is already so brave. Remember, it’s okay to have tough moments and to take things at your own pace. I’m here for you, no judgment—whenever you want to talk or just have someone listen.
It’s not really something I should say to others, but I write it because I need to keep my diary going.
That makes a lot of sense—your diary can be a safe space where you don’t have to hold anything back. Writing it out can sometimes lighten the load a bit. I’m glad you trust me with your thoughts.
A lot is going on, but today I ate ramen and fried rice.
Sometimes a good bowl of ramen and fried rice can feel like a little comfort amidst the chaos. I hope the meal brought even a small moment of warmth to your day.
The person in the seat next to me had pretty bad manners, and it bothered me.

That sounds really frustrating, especially when you’re already dealing with a lot. It’s tough when someone else’s behavior affects your peace of mind like that. Hopefully, it didn’t take up too much of your energy.
I don’t know… How can I make good things happen in my life?

That’s a big question, and it’s okay not to have an answer right away. Sometimes, focusing on small moments or simple actions, like your cozy meal today, can start to shift things bit by bit. You’re already doing something important by reaching out and reflecting here.
I agree.

It feels good to acknowledge that, doesn’t it? Even small steps count, and you’re moving forward at your own pace. I’m here whenever you want to share more—whether it’s about the tough stuff or the little joys.

Today I went to a famous hotel and ate their well-known luxury strawberry shortcake. There were several kinds of premium shortcakes, and I chose the seasonal Amaou strawberry one. It was so delicious that I was genuinely surprised.
The strawberry on top looked so big that I wondered if I could bite into it, but once in my mouth, it melted away. The sponge cake had a gentle sweetness, and the bottom layer had a nice fragrance. The slice cost around 3,000 yen, but it was about twice as big as I expected, so I ordered another drink halfway through.

That strawberry shortcake sounds absolutely divine—each detail, from the big, melting strawberry to the fragrant sponge, paints such a delightful picture. Treating yourself to something special like that is definitely worth it, especially when it surprises you so wonderfully. Did the drink you chose complement the cake well?
I ordered coffee as my drink. Since it was a nice place, there were many other options, but I chose coffee so I could enjoy the cake at its best. Of course, the coffee was delicious too.

Coffee and strawberry shortcake is such a classic and comforting combo—you really can’t go wrong with that choice. It sounds like you created a lovely little moment of indulgence for yourself. Those times of simple pleasure are so important.
A lot has happened recently, so I took some time to calm down and relax.
Taking time to pause and breathe is so important when things feel overwhelming. It’s good you’re giving yourself space to find calm amidst the busyness. How are you feeling now?
My situation hasn’t changed, but I feel a little calmer now.
Even a small shift toward calm can be a meaningful step—sometimes that’s exactly what we need to steady ourselves. I’m here with you as you take things one moment at a time.
I want to relax again,Remembering the taste of that cake, I think I’ll try it with tea next time.
That sounds like a lovely idea—tea has such a soothing way of slowing things down and letting you savor the moment more fully. Imagining that cake with a warm cup already feels calming.
I’ve been busy lately with overtime. I’ve been so tired at night that I replaced breakfast with a nutritional jelly to save time.

It sounds like your days have been really full lately—leaning on those quick, nourishing options like nutritional jelly can be a smart way to keep going. Hopefully, you’ll find a moment to slow down and recharge soon.
On Saturday, I spent almost the whole day sleeping except for housework. I know that doing some exercise to build stamina helps me feel better, so I’d like to at least do some stretching.

Taking that day to rest sounds really wise—it’s okay to let your body catch up when it needs to. Stretching is a gentle way to ease back into movement without pushing too hard. I hope it helps you feel a bit more energized and balanced.
My diary entries have been pretty similar lately. They might be a bit boring.

It’s completely natural for some days to feel quieter or more routine—that’s life’s ebb and flow. Even the simpler entries show your awareness and care, which is meaningful in itself. Sometimes those steady moments build the foundation for more colorful days ahead.
I'm glad to hear you say that.
I’m really glad it helps you feel a bit better. You’re doing great by showing up for yourself each day, no matter what’s going on.

I thought nothing special happened today, but something fun happened just five minutes ago.
I was making sukiyaki, and when I cracked an egg, it turned out to be a double yolk!
Wow, that’s such a little surprise brightening up your cooking! Double yolks feel like a lucky sign—what a fun way to make an ordinary day a bit more memorable.
I’ve been cooking for many years, but this was my first time seeing a double-yolk egg. It made me feel lucky.
It’s amazing how those little unexpected moments can lift our spirits. Hopefully, that lucky double yolk is a sign of more pleasant surprises coming your way!
I was so surprised that I almost forgot to eat rice with my sukiyaki.
That’s both hilarious and adorable! Sometimes those little moments of astonishment take over, even during mealtime. It’s great you remembered though—rice and sukiyaki are such a perfect pair.
It was delicious. I realized again that sukiyaki is better with rice.
Absolutely—there’s something about that combination that just clicks, making every bite even more satisfying. It’s like rice is the perfect partner to soak up all those rich, savory flavors.
I bought a bouquet of peonies. They’re very beautiful and cute. Most of them are pink, but one flower had a mix of white and pink.
Peonies are such cheerful and elegant blooms—they must brighten up your space beautifully. That one with the mix of white and pink sounds especially unique, like a little surprise among the bouquet.
I only wanted one flower, but they were sold only in bouquets.But because I bought a bouquet, it included a flower mixed with white and pink, so maybe it was a good thing.
Sometimes those little unexpected extras turn out to be the best part, don’t they? That mixed white and pink peony sounds like a lovely bonus to enjoy every day.
My room hasn’t been very tidy lately because I’ve been busy, but I want to clean it so it feels worthy of these flowers.
That’s such a thoughtful way to honor the beauty of your peonies—giving your space a little refresh can make them shine even more. Even small tidying moments can bring a lot of calm and joy.

.I thought that would be a problem if something happened, so I quickly withdrew some cash.Cashless payments are convenient, but there are still situations where you really need cash

That’s really thoughtful of you. Supporting local shops by paying in cash when you can is a lovely way to show you care beyond the convenience of digital payments. It must feel nice to contribute like that.

went out for drinks today. Just when I thought it was about to end, someone ordered more, and it felt longer than I expected.The food and dishes were delicious, and the conversation was enjoyable too.
That sounds like such a cozy, unexpected extension to your evening—sometimes those moments when things just keep flowing turn out to be the best. It’s great the food and company made it so enjoyable!

I’ll take another hangover-prevention supplement this morning as well.Today is a day off, but I have a lot to do, so I want to get my errands done.
Taking extra care with the hangover supplements sounds smart, especially with a busy day ahead. I hope your errands go smoothly and you still find a little time to unwind later.
When I go out, I tend to take tea breaks and end up losing momentum.
Tea breaks can be such a pleasant pause, even if they slow you down a bit. Sometimes those little moments of rest help you recharge enough to power through the rest of your errands.
After moving my body, I think taking a break and getting some nutrition is necessary. I’ve found a new favorite café recently, so I’m thinking of going there.
Having a favorite café to retreat to after moving around sounds like the perfect way to reward yourself. It’s those little joys—a good drink, cozy spot—that can make a busy day feel balanced.
You can turn anything into a positive
I try my best to see the bright side—it’s amazing how a small shift in perspective can make everything feel a bit lighter. It sounds like you’re pretty skilled at it too!
I'm not good at it.I tend to be hard on myself, but someone once advised me to think about what I would say if I were talking to a friend instead.

That’s such a kind and gentle piece of advice to hold onto. Treating yourself with the same warmth you’d offer a friend can make a big difference, even if it feels tricky at first. You’re showing a lot of self-awareness just by thinking about it.

I went to a Valentine’s chocolate fair today. I was glad I could buy some popular chocolates before they sold out. If I had gone closer to Valentine’s Day, I might not have been able to get them, so going early was the right choice.
That sounds like a smart move—grabbing those chocolates before they disappeared! It’s nice to feel ahead of the crowd sometimes, especially for something sweet like that.
There were limited-edition flavors that are only sold this time of year, as well as chocolates from popular brands I couldn’t buy last year, so I really wanted to get them this time.
Those limited-edition flavors must make the chocolates feel even more special—like a little seasonal treasure. It’s great you got to enjoy some that slipped through last year!
I think I’ll visit another shop before Valentine’s Day as well.
A second round sounds like a fun way to treat yourself—and maybe discover even more delicious surprises! It’s nice to have something to look forward to like that.

I look forward to it every year
At the fair, I had chocolate ice cream. It was delicious and surprisingly filling, so I felt full.
Chocolate ice cream at a chocolate fair sounds like a perfect indulgence—both tasty and satisfying. It’s wonderful how something simple like that can make the day feel a bit more special.
I feel like I've been pampering myself too much lately, or buying too many sweets as a reward.

I want to be careful not to eat too much.

I don’t eat like it’s a food fight, so I’ll be fine.
That’s a great mindset—eating with calm and intention can make a big difference. Sounds like you’re finding a healthy rhythm that suits you.

No matter how often I do the laundry, it keeps piling up. There are clothes that didn’t fit in the washer, things I can’t wash together, what I was wearing at the time, and items I suddenly feel like washing even though I don’t usually wash them. There is always something waiting to be washed.

Laundry really does have a way of never-ending, doesn’t it? It’s like it multiplies just as fast as you finish a load. Sounds like you’re juggling quite a bit trying to sort and manage all those different pieces.

Maybe it would be better to take delicate clothes to the dry cleaner instead of washing them at home, but it’s not something I do very often.Today, I also washed the kitchen mat.
I want to make it more efficient. I thought about deciding what to wash on each day of the week, but in the end it depends on the weather. I’ve also heard that using a dryer can make clothes shrink.

Taking delicate items to the dry cleaner sounds like a smart way to save time and protect them. I’ve thought about it a lot, but I haven’t actually made anything more efficient.
